items.n: 1/f noise (flicker noise)
items.x: Noise that grows larger at lower frequencies. In MOSFETs it comes from traps at the gate-oxide interface capturing and releasing carriers, and it matters in low-frequency analog circuits. 1/f雑音(フリッカ雑音)

items.n: 128b/130b encoding
items.x: Line coding that sends 128 data bits with a 2-bit header, about 98.5% efficient, relying on scrambling for transitions. Used from PCI Express 3.0 onward. 128b/130b符号化

items.n: 1T1C cell
items.x: The DRAM memory cell that stores one bit with one transistor and one capacitor. The presence or absence of charge on the capacitor represents 0 or 1. 1T1Cセル

items.n: 2.5D packaging
items.x: Placing several chips side by side on an intermediate substrate such as a silicon interposer and connecting them with dense, fine wiring. It is used, for example, to connect GPUs and HBM. 2.5D実装

items.n: 2D materials
items.x: Layered materials that remain stable at a thickness of one to a few atomic layers. Semiconductors such as MoS2 can form extremely thin channels that are difficult with silicon, so they are being researched for future ultra-scaled transistors. 2次元材料

items.n: 2DEG (two-dimensional electron gas)
items.x: A dense sheet of electrons confined at a heterojunction interface such as AlGaN/GaN. With little impurity scattering and high mobility, it serves as the channel of a HEMT. 2次元電子ガス(2DEG)

items.n: 3D DRAM
items.x: DRAM that stacks memory cells vertically in many layers to increase capacity without relying only on planar shrinking. Handling the capacitor is the biggest challenge, and as of the mid-2020s it is still in research and development. 3D DRAM

items.n: 3D NAND
items.x: NAND flash in which memory cells are stacked vertically in many layers to increase capacity. It was introduced to get past the limits of planar scaling, and layer counts now exceed 200. 3D NAND

items.n: 3D packaging
items.x: Stacking chips vertically and connecting them with TSVs or hybrid bonding. Shorter connections improve speed and power, but heat removal becomes a challenge. 3D実装

items.n: 3D XPoint
items.x: Cross-point non-volatile memory jointly developed by Intel and Micron. It stacked phase-change material with OTS selectors and was sold as Optane, but the business was wound down in 2022. 3D XPoint

items.n: 4H-SiC
items.x: The SiC polytype mainly used for power devices. It has a wide band gap of about 3.3 eV and relatively high electron mobility. 4H-SiC

items.n: 5 V tolerant
items.x: An input that can accept 5 V without damage and without current flowing into the supply, even when the IC runs from 3.3 V or similar. It only tolerates 5 V at the input; it does not mean the IC can output a 5 V signal. 5 Vトレラント

items.n: 6T SRAM cell
items.x: The SRAM memory cell made of two cross-coupled inverters (four transistors) and two access transistors. 6T SRAMセル

items.n: 8b/10b encoding
items.x: Line coding that sends 8 data bits as a 10-bit code with balanced 0s and 1s and short runs. It eases clock recovery but limits efficiency to 80%. 8b/10b符号化

items.n: ABA problem
items.x: The problem that when a value changes from A to B and back to A, a CAS comparing only values fails to notice and succeeds. Lock-free data structures must guard against it. ABA問題

items.n: Abatement system
items.x: Equipment that removes hazardous substances from tool exhaust gas by combustion, adsorption, water scrubbing and the like. 除害装置

items.n: ABC analysis
items.x: A method that sorts items in descending order of sales or usage value, divides them into groups A, B and C by cumulative share, and manages them differently according to their importance. It is done using a Pareto chart. ABC分析

items.n: Absolute maximum ratings
items.x: Limits on voltage, current, temperature and so on that may damage or degrade the device if exceeded even momentarily. Staying within them does not guarantee correct operation; normal use is within the recommended operating conditions. 絶対最大定格

items.n: Abstract syntax tree
items.x: A tree representing program structure with operations and statements as nodes. Meaningless details such as parentheses and separators are omitted, and operator precedence is expressed by the tree's shape. 抽象構文木(AST)

items.n: Accelerometer
items.x: A sensor that detects acceleration from the movement of a small spring-supported mass. It is used for detecting smartphone orientation, in airbags and elsewhere. 加速度センサー

items.n: Acceptor
items.x: An impurity that accepts electrons from a semiconductor and creates holes. For silicon, group III elements such as boron (B) act as acceptors and make p-type semiconductors. アクセプタ

items.n: ACID properties
items.x: The initials of four properties a transaction should satisfy: atomicity (everything is executed or nothing is), consistency (integrity constraints keep being satisfied), isolation (concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other) and durability (committed results are not lost even if a failure occurs). ACID特性

items.n: ACPI
items.x: Advanced Configuration and Power Interface: the standard mechanism by which an OS manages device power states, power saving and thermals. ACPI

items.n: Acquire-release semantics
items.x: An ordering guarantee: operations after an acquire cannot move before it, and operations before a release cannot move after it. Used for lock acquire and release, it is lighter than a full barrier. アクワイア・リリース

items.n: Activation function
items.x: The function applied in each neuron of a neural network to the weighted sum of its inputs (plus a bias). Using a nonlinear function lets a network with stacked layers represent complex relationships. ReLU is common in hidden layers, while output layers often use the sigmoid function for two-class classification, the softmax function for multi-class classification and the identity function (no change) for regression. 活性化関数

items.n: Activity factor
items.x: The fraction of a circuit's signals that switch per clock cycle, the α in the dynamic power formula αCV²f. It can be reduced by clock gating and similar. 活動率

items.n: Adaptive voltage scaling (AVS)
items.x: A technique that measures each chip's speed and temperature on chip and approaches the minimum voltage at which it works, trimming wasted margin. 適応電圧スケーリング

items.n: Address space layout randomization (ASLR)
items.x: A countermeasure that changes the addresses of the stack, heap, shared libraries and executable every run so attackers cannot easily predict them. ASLR

items.n: Addressing mode
items.x: The way an instruction specifies the address of data or a jump target. Examples include immediate, register, base register plus offset and PC-relative. アドレッシングモード

items.n: AEC-Q100
items.x: The qualification standard for reliability testing of automotive integrated circuits, defined by the Automotive Electronics Council (AEC). It has operating temperature grades: Grade 1 is −40 to 125 °C and Grade 0 is −40 to 150 °C. Discrete semiconductors are covered by AEC-Q101 and passive components by AEC-Q200. AEC-Q100

items.n: AFM (atomic force microscope)
items.x: A microscope that traces a sharp tip over a sample and measures fine surface topography from the forces between tip and surface. It is used, for example, to evaluate surface roughness. AFM(原子間力顕微鏡)

items.n: Agile development
items.x: A general term for ways of developing software that repeat short iterations of a few weeks, produce working software each time, incorporate user feedback and revise the plan to follow changing requirements. Representative methods include Scrum and Extreme Programming (XP). アジャイル開発

items.n: AI compiler
items.x: Software that analyzes a model's computational graph, optimizes fusion, data layout and tiling, and generates code for the target hardware, such as XLA and TVM. AIコンパイラ

items.n: AI inference
items.x: Running only the forward pass with weights fixed by training to produce answers from inputs. It needs less computation and memory than training. 推論

items.n: Air gap
items.x: Leaving part of the insulator between wires as empty space. Since air has a relative permittivity of about 1, it greatly reduces capacitance between wires. エアギャップ

items.n: Airborne molecular contamination (AMC)
items.x: Gaseous contaminants in the air such as acids, alkalis and organics. Particle filters cannot remove them, so chemical filters are used. 分子状汚染(AMC)

items.n: ALD
items.x: Atomic layer deposition. A deposition method that repeats self-limiting surface reactions of precursor gases to control film thickness one atomic layer at a time. ALD

items.n: ALE (atomic layer etching)
items.x: Etching by alternating surface modification and removal so that each cycle removes about one atomic layer. It gives extremely precise control of etch depth. ALE(原子層エッチング)

items.n: Aliasing
items.x: A phenomenon in which components above half the sampling frequency falsely appear as lower-frequency components. It is prevented with a low-pass filter before A/D conversion. エイリアシング

items.n: All-reduce
items.x: Communication that sums values held by all GPUs element by element and gives the result to every GPU, used to average gradients in data-parallel training. オールリデュース

items.n: Allowable power dissipation
items.x: The maximum power a package may dissipate, written Pd. It is set by the maximum junction temperature and the thermal resistance, and above a certain ambient temperature (often 25 °C) it must be reduced in proportion to temperature. 許容損失

items.n: Alloy semiconductor
items.x: A semiconductor crystal that mixes several elements, such as AlGaAs or InGaN. Changing the composition tunes the band gap and lattice constant continuously. 混晶半導体

items.n: Amdahl's law
items.x: The law that when only part of a program is parallelized, overall speedup is limited by the part that cannot be. For example, parallelizing 90% gives at most a 10x speedup. アムダールの法則

items.n: AMHS (automated material handling system)
items.x: The collective term for the equipment that automatically moves wafer carriers such as FOUPs between tools and storage in a semiconductor fab, and the control system that runs it. It consists of OHTs, stockers and related equipment. AMHS(自動搬送システム)

items.n: Anisotropic etching
items.x: Etching that proceeds only in a particular direction (mainly vertically). Needed to pattern fine features. 異方性エッチング

items.n: Annealing
items.x: Heat treatment. Used to repair crystal damage after ion implantation and to activate dopants, among other purposes. アニール

items.n: Anodic bonding
items.x: Joining silicon to sodium-containing glass by heating them together while applying a voltage. It is used, for example, to seal MEMS devices. 陽極接合

items.n: Antenna effect
items.x: Damage to a gate oxide when a connected conductor, such as a long wire, collects charge like an antenna during plasma processing. Design rules limit the area ratio of such wires to prevent it. アンテナ効果

items.n: Anti-rollback protection
items.x: A mechanism recording a minimum version number in unchangeable storage so software cannot be reverted to older vulnerable versions. ロールバック防止

items.n: APC (advanced process control)
items.x: Automatically adjusting the process settings for the next lot or wafer based on earlier measurements, as in run-to-run control. It reduces variation. APC(先進的プロセス制御)

items.n: Application binary interface (ABI)
items.x: The machine-level agreement that lets compiled programs and libraries work together, covering the calling convention, data type sizes and alignment, how system calls are made and more. ABI(アプリケーションバイナリインターフェース)

items.n: ARDE (aspect-ratio-dependent etching)
items.x: The slowdown of etch rate in narrower, deeper features because ions and radicals reach the bottom less easily. Also called the microloading effect. ARDE(アスペクト比依存エッチング)

items.n: Area-selective deposition
items.x: Growing a film only in certain places by exploiting differences in the underlying materials. Because it can save lithography and etch steps, it is being researched and introduced for advanced interconnects. 領域選択成膜

items.n: ArF excimer laser
items.x: A laser using argon and fluorine that emits 193 nm ultraviolet light. Combined with immersion, ArF immersion lithography is a leading-edge technique alongside EUV. The 248 nm version is the KrF excimer laser. ArFエキシマレーザー

items.n: Argument
items.x: A value passed when calling a function or procedure. The variable that receives the value in the declaration is called a formal parameter, and the value passed at the call is called an actual argument. Arguments can be passed by value, which copies the value, or by reference, which lets the callee refer to the variable or array itself. 引数

items.n: Arithmetic intensity
items.x: Operations performed divided by bytes moved to and from memory. High values tend toward compute-bound, low values toward memory-bound. 演算強度

items.n: Arithmetic shift
items.x: A right shift of a signed integer that copies the sign bit into the vacated high bits. Shifting a negative number right by one divides by 2, rounding toward negative infinity. Filling with zeros is a logical shift. 算術シフト

items.n: ARP
items.x: Address Resolution Protocol. A protocol that finds the MAC address of a device on the same network from its IP address. The request is broadcast, and the matching device replies. ARP

items.n: Array
items.x: A data structure that stores values of the same type in sequence and identifies each element by an index. Because the elements are stored contiguously in memory, the position of any element can be computed from its index, so any element can be read or written in constant time. Some languages start indices at 0, while some notations start them at 1. 配列

items.n: Arrhenius model
items.x: A model in which reaction or degradation rates vary with temperature as exp(−Ea/kT). It is used to estimate lifetime at operating temperature from accelerated tests at higher temperatures. アレニウスモデル

items.n: Arsine (AsH3)
items.x: A gas compound of arsenic and hydrogen used to introduce n-type dopant (arsenic) and to grow compound semiconductors such as GaAs. It is extremely toxic. アルシン(AsH3)

items.n: Ashing
items.x: Removing photoresist that is no longer needed after etching or implantation by oxidizing it to ash, typically with an oxygen plasma. アッシング

items.n: ASIC (application-specific integrated circuit)
items.x: An IC designed specifically for one application or customer. It beats general-purpose chips on performance and power, but high development costs suit it to high-volume uses. ASIC(特定用途向けIC)

items.n: ASID
items.x: A number tagged onto each TLB entry indicating which process's address space the translation belongs to. The TLB need not be flushed on a process switch, reducing TLB misses afterward. ASID(アドレス空間識別子)

items.n: ASIL (Automotive Safety Integrity Level)
items.x: In ISO 26262, the level of safety requirements assigned to each hazardous event from three factors: severity S, exposure E and controllability C. There are four levels, A to D, with D the most stringent; low-risk items that need no ASIL are classed as QM. ASIL(自動車安全度水準)

items.n: Aspect ratio
items.x: The ratio of a hole's or trench's depth to its width. Higher ratios make etching and deposition harder; memory holes in 3D NAND reach several tens or more. アスペクト比

items.n: Assembler
items.x: Software that converts a program written in assembly language into machine instruction bit patterns. It turns labels into addresses and expands pseudo-instructions into real instructions. アセンブラ

items.n: Asynchronous FIFO
items.x: A FIFO written and read on separate clocks, used to pass multi-bit data between clock domains. Its pointers are converted to Gray code before being synchronized into the other domain to decide full and empty. The pointers have one more bit than the address to distinguish wrap-around. 非同期FIFO

items.n: Asynchronous reset
items.x: A reset that initializes flip-flops as soon as the reset signal is asserted, regardless of the clock. Release should be synchronized to the clock. 非同期リセット

items.n: ATE (automatic test equipment)
items.x: Equipment that applies test patterns to chips, measures their outputs and automatically judges pass or fail. Also called a tester. ATE(自動試験装置)

items.n: Atomic instruction
items.x: An instruction that performs a memory read and write as one operation no other core can interrupt, such as CAS, fetch-and-add and LR/SC. アトミック命令

items.n: ATPG (automatic test pattern generation)
items.x: Automatically generating test patterns that detect faults from a circuit's netlist. It is used together with scan design. ATPG(自動テストパターン生成)

items.n: Attention mechanism
items.x: The Transformer mechanism in which each token gathers information by computing its relationship to every other token. Its cost grows with the square of sequence length. アテンション

items.n: Audit trail
items.x: Records that make it possible to trace and verify afterward the flow of a transaction or data from input through processing, output and storage, and who did what and when. Access and operation logs, processing records and approval records are examples. Auditors follow them to verify that processing was legitimate and accurate. Mechanisms that protect them from tampering or deletion and keep them for the required period are considered from the system design stage. 監査証跡

items.n: Auger recombination
items.x: Recombination in which the released energy is given to another carrier instead of being emitted as light. It becomes significant at high carrier densities and affects lifetime in heavily doped layers and efficiency loss in LEDs. オージェ再結合

items.n: Autodoping
items.x: Unintended incorporation into a growing epitaxial layer of dopant from the substrate or elsewhere via the gas phase. It is a problem when growing lightly doped layers on heavily doped substrates. オートドーピング

items.n: Avalanche breakdown
items.x: A phenomenon in which carriers accelerated by a strong reverse field strike atoms and create new carriers, which multiply in a chain reaction so that a large current flows. なだれ降伏

items.n: Average memory access time
items.x: The average time per memory access, computed as hit time + miss rate × miss penalty. A basic metric for comparing cache designs. 平均メモリアクセス時間(AMAT)

items.n: AXI
items.x: An on-chip bus from Arm's AMBA specifications that connects blocks in an SoC, with five independent channels and a VALID/READY handshake. Variants include AXI4-Lite and AXI4-Stream. AXI

items.n: Backgrinding
items.x: Grinding the back of a wafer before dicing to thin it for packaging. Chips for stacking are thinned to a few tens of micrometers. バックグラインド

items.n: Backpropagation
items.x: The training computation that propagates the error between output and target backward from output to input to obtain each weight's gradient. 逆伝播

items.n: Backside illumination (BSI)
items.x: An image sensor structure in which light enters from the back of the substrate, where there is no wiring. Light is not blocked by wiring, so sensitivity stays high even with small pixels. 裏面照射型(BSI)

items.n: Backside power delivery
items.x: Placing the power wiring on the back of the wafer so the front-side wiring can be used for signals. It reduces voltage drop and routing congestion. 裏面電源供給

items.n: Band gap
items.x: The energy difference between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band. About 1.12 eV for silicon at room temperature. A larger band gap means better tolerance to high temperatures and voltages. バンドギャップ

items.n: Bandgap voltage reference
items.x: A circuit that adds a diode voltage that falls with temperature to a voltage that rises with temperature, producing a reference of about 1.2 V that barely depends on temperature. It is widely used in ADCs and power ICs. バンドギャップ基準電圧回路

items.n: Bank
items.x: One of several independently operating sections inside a DRAM. Overlapping activation and access across different banks raises effective performance. バンク

items.n: Bank conflict
items.x: In GPU shared memory, multiple threads of a warp accessing different addresses in the same bank at once, which serializes the accesses. Padding can avoid it. バンク競合

items.n: Barrier metal
items.x: A thin metal film around copper wiring that prevents copper from diffusing into insulating films or silicon, such as Ta or TaN. バリアメタル

items.n: Barrier synchronization
items.x: Synchronization in which threads that arrive first wait until all threads reach the same point, keeping them in step phase by phase. Distinct from a memory barrier. バリア同期

items.n: Basic block
items.x: A sequence of instructions with no branch entering or leaving in the middle, always executed from start to end. Basic blocks are the nodes of a control-flow graph and units of local optimization. 基本ブロック

items.n: Batch size
items.x: The number of inputs processed together. Larger batches reuse weights for efficiency but increase latency and memory. バッチサイズ

items.n: Bathtub curve
items.x: A curve showing how the failure rate changes over time. It consists of the early-failure, random-failure and wear-out periods and is shaped like a bathtub. バスタブ曲線

items.n: Baud rate
items.x: The number of symbols sent per second in serial communication; for a UART it equals bits per second and must match on both sides. ボーレート

items.n: Bayer pattern
items.x: A color filter arrangement of red, green, green and blue over each 2×2 block of pixels, with two greens because the eye is most sensitive to green. Missing colors at each pixel are interpolated from neighbors (demosaicing). ベイヤー配列

items.n: Bayes' theorem
items.x: The relation that reverses the direction of a conditional probability: P(A | B) = P(B | A) × P(A) ÷ P(B). It is used to update the prior probability P(A) of a cause A into the posterior probability P(A | B) on the basis of an observed result B. It is used for calculating the positive predictive value of a test, for spam filtering (naive Bayes) and for estimating the causes of failures. It also shows the effect of the base rate: when the cause is rare, many positives are false even for an accurate test. ベイズの定理

items.n: BCP (business continuity plan)
items.x: A plan prepared in advance so that critical business activities are not interrupted, or are resumed within an acceptable time if they are, even when natural disasters, large-scale failures, epidemics and the like occur (Business Continuity Plan). A business impact analysis determines the critical activities and the acceptable downtime, and the plan sets out alternative sites and staff, procedures for recovering systems and so on. The whole ongoing effort of drawing up, exercising and reviewing the plan is called business continuity management (BCM). BCP(事業継続計画)

items.n: Beamforming
items.x: A technique that adjusts the phase (and amplitude) of each of several antenna elements so that radio waves reinforce one another in a particular direction for transmission or reception. Changing the phases electronically steers the beam without moving the antenna (a phased array). Besides making up for the large propagation loss of millimeter-wave bands, it is used in 5G base stations and wireless LANs to point a beam at each terminal, raising received power and reducing interference. ビームフォーミング

items.n: Benchmark
items.x: A representative program run under fixed conditions to compare computer or program performance. Choosing ones close to actual use is important. ベンチマーク

items.n: bfloat16
items.x: A 16-bit floating-point format with 1 sign, 8 exponent and 7 significand bits. Sharing FP32's exponent width gives it a wide range, so despite low precision it is used for AI training. FP16, with 5 exponent and 10 significand bits, is more precise but has a narrow range. bfloat16

items.n: BGA
items.x: Ball grid array. A high-pin-count package with solder balls arranged in a grid on its underside. BGA

items.n: Binary heap
items.x: A complete binary tree in which each parent's value is greater than or equal to (max-heap) or less than or equal to (min-heap) its children's values. It can be stored in an array: with the root at a[0], the children of a[i] are a[2i+1] and a[2i+2]. Reading the maximum (minimum) takes O(1), and insertion and removal take O(log n); it is used for priority queues and heapsort. 二分ヒープ

items.n: Binary search
items.x: A search method for sorted data that compares the target with the middle element and halves the search range each time. It finds a value among n items in at most ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 comparisons, so its complexity is O(log n). The data must be sorted. 二分探索

items.n: Binary search tree
items.x: A binary tree in which, for every node, all values in the left subtree are smaller and all values in the right subtree are larger than the node. Search, insertion and deletion take time proportional to the tree's height, and an in-order traversal visits the values in ascending order. 二分探索木

items.n: Binomial distribution
items.x: The probability distribution of the number of successes when a trial with success probability p is repeated n times independently. The probability of exactly k successes is nCk × pᵏ × (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ, the mean is np and the variance is np(1 − p). For example, when 10 parts are taken from a population with a 10% defect rate, the probability that none is defective is 0.9¹⁰ ≈ 0.349. It is used to calculate the acceptance probability of sampling inspection and the number of bit errors in communication, and when n is large and p is small it can be approximated by a Poisson distribution. 二項分布

items.n: Bird's beak
items.x: In LOCOS, the beak-shaped encroachment of oxide under the edge of the nitride mask. Because it wastes active area, it led to the switch to STI at finer geometries. バーズビーク

items.n: BIST (built-in self-test)
items.x: Test circuitry built into the chip so that it generates test patterns and checks results by itself. It is widely used, for example, to test memories. BIST(組み込み自己テスト)

items.n: Bit error rate (BER)
items.x: The fraction of transmitted bits received incorrectly. High-speed serial links typically require values such as 10^-12 or lower. ビット誤り率

items.n: Bit line
items.x: The wire used to read and write data in memory cells. In DRAM, the small change in bit-line potential caused by a cell's charge is amplified by a sense amplifier. ビット線

items.n: Bitwise operation
items.x: An operation that treats an integer as a sequence of binary bits and applies AND, OR, exclusive OR (XOR) or NOT to each bit, or shifts the bits left or right. It is used to extract or set particular bits, to count 1 bits, and to multiply or divide by powers of 2. ビット演算

items.n: Black-box testing
items.x: A testing approach that determines inputs and expected outputs from the specification alone, without looking at the internal structure of the program. Its techniques include equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis and decision tables. ブラックボックステスト

items.n: Black's equation
items.x: An empirical formula for interconnect lifetime under electromigration in terms of current density and temperature. Lifetime is inversely proportional to a power of current density and falls exponentially as temperature rises. ブラックの式

items.n: Blocking assignment
items.x: Verilog's "=" assignment, which updates the left side immediately so the next statement sees the new value. Used in combinational always blocks and testbenches. ブロッキング代入

items.n: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
items.x: The variant of the 2.4 GHz short-range wireless technology Bluetooth that emphasizes low power consumption. By keeping communication time very short and shutting down circuits the rest of the time, devices can run a long time even on coin cells. It is used in beacons that periodically send short signals called advertisements, in wearables, sensors and more. It cannot communicate directly with classic Bluetooth (BR/EDR). BLE(Bluetooth Low Energy)

items.n: Body diode
items.x: A parasitic diode formed between source and drain by the structure of a power MOSFET. It can serve as the freewheeling diode in an inverter, but its reverse recovery needs attention. ボディダイオード

items.n: Body effect
items.x: An increase in threshold voltage when reverse bias is applied between source and substrate (body), because the depletion charge grows. Also called the substrate bias effect; it is sometimes used to tune the threshold. 基板バイアス効果

items.n: Booth's algorithm
items.x: A multiplication method that recodes the multiplier's bits, for example in pairs, into signed digits to reduce the number of partial products. Radix-4 Booth encoding roughly halves them. ブースのアルゴリズム

items.n: Bootloader
items.x: A small program that runs first at power-on, verifying and starting the main firmware or updating it with new firmware. ブートローダ

items.n: Bosch process (deep RIE)
items.x: A dry-etching technique that alternates short etch and sidewall-passivation steps to cut deep, vertical holes and trenches in silicon. It is used for MEMS and TSVs. ボッシュプロセス(Deep RIE)

items.n: Bottom anti-reflective coating (BARC)
items.x: A layer coated under the resist that suppresses standing waves in the resist and dimension variation over topography caused by light reflected from the substrate. 反射防止膜(BARC)

items.n: Boundary value analysis
items.x: A black-box testing technique that, because defects tend to cluster at the boundaries between equivalence classes, tests the values immediately on both sides of each boundary (for example 0, 1, 100 and 101 when 1 to 100 is accepted). It is good at finding errors such as confused comparison operators. 境界値分析

items.n: Branch coverage
items.x: A white-box testing coverage criterion that requires both the true and false branches of every decision (such as an if statement) in a program to be executed at least once. It is also called decision coverage or C1, and it is stronger than statement coverage (C0), which requires every statement to be executed at least once. 分岐網羅

items.n: Branch delay slot
items.x: An ISA rule that the instruction right after a branch always executes, taken or not. Found in older ISAs such as MIPS, it exposed a pipeline detail in the ISA and later became a burden. 分岐遅延スロット

items.n: Branch prediction
items.x: A technique that predicts the outcome of conditional branches before they execute, so later instructions can proceed without stalling the pipeline. A misprediction forces the work to be redone. 分岐予測

items.n: Breadth-first search
items.x: A way of searching a graph or tree that visits vertices in order of distance from the start: first those one edge away, then those two edges away, and so on. It is implemented with a queue, and in a graph without edge weights it finds the smallest number of edges from the start to every vertex. It is abbreviated BFS. 幅優先探索

items.n: Break-even point
items.x: The sales or sales volume at which sales exactly equal costs (the sum of variable and fixed costs), so profit is zero. Break-even sales are found as fixed costs ÷ contribution margin ratio. 損益分岐点

items.n: Break-even time
items.x: The idle duration needed for the energy saved in a power-saving state to exceed the energy spent entering and leaving it. 損益分岐時間

items.n: Brown-out detection
items.x: A function that resets the microcontroller when the supply voltage drops below the operating minimum, preventing unreliable behavior and corrupt flash writes. ブラウンアウト検出

items.n: BSS section
items.x: The area for global and static variables with no initializer (or zero). Only its size is recorded in the file and it is zero-filled at load time, so it does not enlarge the executable. BSSセクション

items.n: Buffered hydrofluoric acid (BHF)
items.x: Hydrofluoric acid buffered with ammonium fluoride. It is used for wet etching of SiO2 with a stable etch rate and little damage to resist. バッファードフッ酸(BHF)

items.n: Built-in potential
items.x: The potential difference across the depletion layer of a PN junction even with no external voltage applied. About 0.6 to 0.9 V in silicon, it forms the barrier that stops further carrier diffusion. 内蔵電位

items.n: Burn-in
items.x: A test that operates products under stress such as high temperature and high voltage to remove units prone to early failure before shipment. バーンイン

items.n: Bus snooping
items.x: A coherence approach in which each cache watches other cores' reads and writes on a shared bus or similar and updates its own line states. It suits small core counts. スヌーピング

items.n: C-band
items.x: The optical fiber communication band around 1530 to 1565 nm. Silica fiber loss is lowest there (about 0.2 dB/km) and erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) can amplify it, so it is used for long-haul links and dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM). Cバンド

items.n: C-state
items.x: CPU idle states describing sleep depth. C0 is active; higher numbers use less power but take longer to wake. C-state

items.n: CAAT (computer-assisted audit techniques)
items.x: A collective term for techniques that use computers to perform audit procedures (Computer Assisted Audit Techniques). They include the test data method, in which a program processes data prepared by the auditor and the results are checked; the ITF method, which sets up fictitious audit accounts in the production system; the snapshot method, which writes out data midway through processing; parallel simulation, in which the auditor's own program processes production data and the results are compared; and extraction and analysis of data with generalized audit software. They allow large volumes of data to be examined in full. CAAT(コンピュータ支援監査技法)

items.n: Cache coherency
items.x: In a multicore CPU, the mechanism that keeps copies of the same address in different cores' caches consistent, for example by invalidating other copies when one core writes. キャッシュコヒーレンシ

items.n: Cache line
items.x: The unit in which data moves between a cache and the level below, also called a cache block. Many CPUs use 64 bytes, and the low address bits give the position (offset) within the line. キャッシュライン

items.n: Cache memory
items.x: Fast, small memory placed close to the CPU. It holds frequently used data to bridge the speed gap with main memory. Mostly built from SRAM. キャッシュメモリ

items.n: Callee-saved register
items.x: A register guaranteed to keep its value across a call; if the called function uses it, the function saves and restores it. In RISC-V these are s0-s11. 呼び出し先保存レジスタ

items.n: Caller-saved register
items.x: A register the called function may overwrite freely; if the caller needs its value after the call, the caller saves it. In RISC-V these include t0-t6 and a0-a7. 呼び出し元保存レジスタ

items.n: Calling convention
items.x: The agreement on how arguments and return values are passed in registers or on the stack, and who saves which registers, when calling a function. It is a key part of the ABI. 呼び出し規約

items.n: CAN bus
items.x: Short for Controller Area Network, an in-vehicle network that connects ECUs using differential signaling on two wires. Lower ID values have higher priority, and when nodes start transmitting at once, non-destructive arbitration leaves a single frame intact. Classical CAN runs at up to 1 Mbit/s, while CAN FD speeds up the data phase to several Mbit/s. CAN

items.n: Capacitive sensing
items.x: A method that detects displacement, pressure and the like from changes in capacitance between movable and fixed electrodes. It is widely used in MEMS sensors. 静電容量検出

items.n: Capacity miss
items.x: A cache miss caused by the working set being larger than the cache. It occurs even in a fully associative cache and is reduced by a larger cache or by improving data reuse. 容量ミス

items.n: Carry-lookahead adder
items.x: An adder that computes carries in parallel from each bit's generate signal g = a·b and propagate signal p = a ⊕ b, without waiting for carries to ripple. Delay stays small even for wide operands. 桁上げ先見加算器

items.n: Carry-save adder
items.x: An adder that reduces three numbers to two, a sum and a carry, without propagating carries. Made of independent full adders per bit, its delay is constant, so multipliers use it to add many partial products. 桁上げ保存加算器

items.n: CAS latency
items.x: The number of clock cycles in DRAM from a read command (specifying the column address) until data appears at the output, abbreviated CL. Smaller values mean a faster response. CASレイテンシ

items.n: Catastrophic cancellation
items.x: Loss of significant digits when subtracting two nearly equal numbers, as their leading digits cancel and the relative weight of existing rounding error grows. It is avoided by rearranging formulas. 桁落ち

items.n: Cause-and-effect diagram
items.x: A diagram that organizes the causes affecting a problem (the effect) in the shape of a fish skeleton. Also called a fishbone diagram. 特性要因図

items.n: CCD image sensor
items.x: An image sensor that shifts pixel charges along like a bucket brigade and converts them to voltage at an output stage. It offered low noise and high image quality but used more power, and CMOS sensors have replaced it in most uses. CCDイメージセンサ

items.n: CD-SEM
items.x: A scanning electron microscope for measuring pattern line widths (critical dimensions). Used for dimensional control after lithography and etching. CD-SEM

items.n: Ceria (cerium oxide)
items.x: An abrasive used in CMP slurries. It reacts chemically with oxide and gives high selectivity to nitride, so it is used for STI CMP. セリア(酸化セリウム)

items.n: CFET (complementary FET)
items.x: A structure that stacks nMOS and pMOS transistors vertically. It is under development because it could greatly shrink the area of CMOS circuits. CFET(相補型FET)

items.n: Chalcogenide
items.x: A compound containing group 16 elements such as sulfur, selenium or tellurium. It is used as the recording material of phase-change memory (such as GST) and in selectors (OTS) that switch on abruptly above a threshold voltage. カルコゲナイド

items.n: Change management
items.x: The process for preventing failures caused by changes, in which changes to IT services and their components are recorded, assessed for impact, risk and cost, and approved before being carried out. Change requests are received and recorded, and depending on their content they are reviewed at a meeting of the people concerned. An emergency change procedure, in which a small group approves quickly, is also defined for urgent changes. After implementation, the result is checked and the configuration management information is updated. 変更管理

items.n: Channel-length modulation
items.x: In a saturated MOSFET, raising the drain voltage moves the pinch-off point toward the source, shortening the effective channel and slightly increasing drain current. It makes the output resistance finite. チャネル長変調

items.n: Channeling
items.x: A phenomenon in which ions pass through gaps between rows of crystal atoms and penetrate deeper than expected. It is prevented by tilting the wafer during implantation and similar measures. チャネリング

items.n: Characteristic impedance
items.x: The ratio of voltage to current seen by a wave traveling along a transmission line, set by trace width and layer spacing. Changes along the path cause reflections. 特性インピーダンス

items.n: Charge-trap cell
items.x: A flash memory cell that stores electrons in traps within an insulating film such as silicon nitride instead of in a floating gate. It is mainly used in 3D NAND. 電荷トラップ型セル

items.n: Chemically amplified resist
items.x: A resist in which acid generated by exposure catalyzes a chain of reactions during the post-exposure bake (PEB). It needs little exposure dose and is widely used from KrF onward, but is sensitive to basic contamination. 化学増幅型レジスト

items.n: Chiplet
items.x: A small chip made for a specific function. Several chiplets are connected inside one package to build a larger system. チップレット

items.n: Chromatic dispersion
items.x: The broadening of light pulses in an optical fiber because light of different wavelengths travels at slightly different speeds. In standard single-mode fiber it is nearly zero near 1.31 µm and about 17 ps/(nm·km) at 1.55 µm. 波長分散

items.n: CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous delivery)
items.x: A combined name for continuous integration (CI), in which developers merge their changes into a shared branch frequently and each merge triggers a build and automated tests, and continuous delivery (CD), which keeps tested changes ready to be released to production at any time. When the release itself is also automated, it is called continuous deployment. CI/CD(継続的インテグレーション・継続的デリバリー)

items.n: CIDR
items.x: Classless Inter-Domain Routing. The scheme of freely setting the length of the network part of an IP address as a number of bits (the prefix length) after a slash, as in 192.168.1.0/24, and that notation. CIDR

items.n: Clock and data recovery (CDR)
items.x: A receiver circuit that extracts clock timing from transitions in the received data and decides each bit, removing the need for a dedicated clock wire. クロック・データ・リカバリ

items.n: Clock domain
items.x: A group of flip-flops driven by the same clock, or by clocks with a fixed frequency and phase relationship. Passing a signal between clock domains that are asynchronous to each other requires a synchronizer. クロックドメイン

items.n: Clock gating
items.x: A low-power design technique that stops the clock to idle circuit blocks, avoiding wasted switching power. クロックゲーティング

items.n: Clock skew
items.x: The difference in arrival time of the same clock signal at different flip-flops. Because it changes setup and hold margins, clock tree synthesis keeps it small. クロックスキュー

items.n: Clock uncertainty
items.x: A margin subtracted from the available time in timing analysis to account for jitter and for clock skew not yet known. It is set with set_clock_uncertainty in SDC, and before the clock tree is built it is set larger to cover skew as well. クロックの不確かさ

items.n: CMOS
items.x: A circuit style that combines nMOS and pMOS transistors in a complementary way. Almost no current flows through it in steady state, so power consumption is low. CMOS

items.n: CMOS image sensor
items.x: An image sensor made with a CMOS process that has an amplifier in each pixel. It is low-power, can integrate peripheral circuits, and dominates smartphone cameras and more. CMOSイメージセンサー

items.n: CMP
items.x: Chemical mechanical polishing. Planarizes the wafer surface by combining the chemical action of a slurry with mechanical polishing by a pad. CMP

items.n: CMRR (common-mode rejection ratio)
items.x: The ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain in a differential amplifier. The larger it is, the better the circuit rejects noise that appears equally on both inputs. CMRR(同相信号除去比)

items.n: Cold boot attack
items.x: An attack reading DRAM contents that persist briefly after power-off to extract keys and other secrets; cooling extends persistence. Prevented by memory encryption. コールドブート攻撃

items.n: Combinational circuit
items.x: A logic circuit whose output depends only on its current inputs. Examples include adders, multiplexers and decoders. 組み合わせ回路

items.n: Combinational loop
items.x: A structure in which combinational output feeds back to its own input without a flip-flop. It can oscillate or fail to settle and defeats timing analysis, so it is avoided. 組み合わせループ

items.n: Common subexpression elimination
items.x: An optimization that computes a repeatedly evaluated expression once and reuses the result, after confirming its operands do not change in between. 共通部分式の削除

items.n: Common-emitter circuit
items.x: An amplifier circuit in which the emitter is the common terminal for input and output. It provides both current gain and voltage gain and is the most widely used configuration. エミッタ接地回路

items.n: Comparator
items.x: A circuit that compares two input voltages and outputs the result as a binary high or low. It is also a basic building block of ADCs. コンパレータ

items.n: Compare-and-swap
items.x: An atomic instruction that writes a new value only if memory still holds an expected value. Wrapped in a retry loop, it enables lock-free updates. コンペア・アンド・スワップ

items.n: Compressed instruction
items.x: An instruction that encodes a common operation in fewer bits than usual. The RISC-V C extension adds 16-bit instructions and cuts code size by roughly 25-30%. 圧縮命令

items.n: Compulsory miss
items.x: A cache miss that inevitably occurs on the first access to data. A larger cache does not reduce it, but larger lines or prefetching can. 初期参照ミス

items.n: Computational graph
items.x: A representation of a model's computation with operations as nodes and tensor flows as edges, underpinning automatic differentiation and AI compiler optimization. 計算グラフ

items.n: Compute Express Link (CXL)
items.x: A standard on the PCI Express physical layer that enables coherent memory sharing between CPUs and accelerators or memory devices. CXL

items.n: Condition code
items.x: Flags such as zero, negative, carry and overflow that record the outcome of a compare or arithmetic operation. Conditional branches in x86 and Arm test them; RISC-V has none. 条件コード

items.n: Condition variable
items.x: A synchronization mechanism that puts a thread to sleep until a condition holds and wakes it on a signal from another thread. The condition must be rechecked after waking. 条件変数

items.n: Conditional probability
items.x: The probability that event A occurs given that event B has occurred. It is written P(A | B) and calculated as P(A | B) = P(A and B) ÷ P(B). It amounts to treating only the cases in which B occurred as the whole and considering the fraction of them in which A occurs. P(A | B) and P(B | A) are generally different values, and Bayes' theorem links the two. If A and B are independent, P(A | B) = P(A). 条件付き確率

items.n: Conductivity modulation
items.x: A large drop in the resistance of a lightly doped layer when many minority carriers are injected into it. PIN diodes and IGBTs use it to combine high breakdown voltage with low on-state voltage. 伝導度変調

items.n: Confidence interval
items.x: An interval that estimates an unknown value, such as the population mean, from a sample with a range. A 95% confidence interval is made by a method such that, if sampling were repeated, about 95% of the resulting intervals would contain the true value. When the population standard deviation σ is known, the 95% confidence interval for the population mean is the sample mean ± 1.96 × σ/√n, where σ/√n is called the standard error. Making the sample size n four times as large halves the width of the interval. 信頼区間

items.n: Configuration management
items.x: The process of identifying the components that make up an IT service (configuration items, CIs) and recording their attributes (version, location, owner and so on) and their relationships with other CIs accurately, keeping them up to date. The database that holds these records is called the CMDB (configuration management database). CIs include servers and network equipment, software, documents and the services themselves. Knowing the relationships between CIs makes it easier to determine the scope of a failure and the impact of a change. 構成管理

items.n: Conflict miss
items.x: A cache miss caused when several blocks compete for the same set and evict each other even though capacity remains. Higher associativity or shifting data placement reduces it. 競合ミス

items.n: Confusion matrix
items.x: A table that counts the data for each combination of a classification model's prediction and the actual correct answer. For two-class classification it has four cells: true positives (TP), positives correctly predicted as positive; false positives (FP), negatives wrongly predicted as positive; false negatives (FN), positives wrongly predicted as negative; and true negatives (TN), negatives correctly predicted as negative. Accuracy, precision, recall, the F1 score and other metrics can be calculated from it, and it also shows which classes are easily mistaken for which. 混同行列

items.n: Constant folding
items.x: An optimization that evaluates expressions whose values are known at compile time and replaces them with the resulting constant, such as turning 3 * 4 into 12. It removes run-time computation. 定数畳み込み

items.n: Constant memory
items.x: A small GPU region for values that do not change during a kernel. When every thread in a warp reads the same address, one read is broadcast to all, which is fast. 定数メモリ

items.n: Constant-time implementation
items.x: A way of writing cryptographic code so that branch directions, loop counts and memory addresses accessed do not depend on secret values. 定数時間実装

items.n: Constrained random verification
items.x: Verification that generates random input values within constraints allowed by the specification, broadly exercising cases people might not think of. 制約付きランダム検証

items.n: Contact bounce
items.x: The rapid on-off flickering of a mechanical switch's contacts when pressed or released, removed by debouncing. チャタリング

items.n: Context switch
items.x: Switching the process or thread running on a CPU. Registers, the program counter and other state are saved and restored, and switching processes also switches address spaces. コンテキストスイッチ

items.n: Contribution margin
items.x: Sales minus variable costs: the amount that covers fixed costs and produces profit. Its ratio to sales is the contribution margin ratio, equal to 1 − variable cost ratio. 限界利益

items.n: Control chart
items.x: A chart that plots process measurements over time against a center line and control limits (usually ±3σ) to judge whether the process is stable. Points outside the limits or runs on one side signal problems. 管理図

items.n: Control structure
items.x: A basic structure that determines the flow of a program. There are three: sequence, which runs statements in order from the top; selection (conditional branching), which chooses statements according to a condition; and iteration, which repeats statements, for example while a condition holds. Any procedure is known to be expressible as a combination of these three (the structured program theorem). 制御構造

items.n: Control-flow graph
items.x: A graph representing a program's execution flow, with basic blocks as nodes and branches between them as edges. It is used to detect loops and analyze data flow. 制御フローグラフ

items.n: Convolutional neural network (CNN)
items.x: A neural network built mainly from convolutional layers, which slide small filters (kernels) over the input and compute sums of products, stacked with pooling layers and others. Because the same filter is reused over the whole input, it has far fewer parameters than fully connected layers and extracts local features such as edges and textures in an image regardless of their position. It is used for image recognition, object detection, audio processing and more. 畳み込みニューラルネットワーク(CNN)

items.n: Copy-on-write
items.x: Sharing duplicated memory with the original at first and copying a page only when either side tries to write it. It speeds process creation and saves memory. コピーオンライト

items.n: Coriolis force
items.x: An apparent force acting perpendicular to the motion of an object moving in a rotating frame. Vibratory MEMS gyroscopes detect angular rate from the displacement it causes. コリオリ力

items.n: Correlated double sampling (CDS)
items.x: Taking the difference between a pixel's voltage just after reset and its voltage when the signal is read. It removes reset noise and per-pixel offsets. 相関二重サンプリング(CDS)

items.n: Correlation coefficient
items.x: A measure expressing the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two quantities as a value from −1 to 1. It is calculated by dividing the covariance of x and y by the product of the standard deviation of x and the standard deviation of y. The closer it is to 1, the stronger the positive correlation; the closer to −1, the stronger the negative correlation; close to 0, the linear relationship is weak. Curved relationships hardly show up in the correlation coefficient, and correlation does not mean that one quantity causes the other. The slope of the regression line is the correlation coefficient multiplied by the ratio of the standard deviations of the two quantities. 相関係数

items.n: Counterfeit chip
items.x: A used, defective or lower-grade chip relabeled and sold as genuine, leading to failures and safety problems. 偽造チップ

items.n: CoWoS
items.x: TSMC's 2.5D packaging technology, which places logic chips and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer. It is widely used for AI GPUs and similar products. CoWoS

items.n: CPO (co-packaged optics)
items.x: Technology that mounts the optical transceiver parts (optical engines) in the same package as a switch IC or similar. Shorter electrical connections lower the energy per bit, but the optics cannot be swapped out by unplugging, so testing before assembly and the use of external laser sources become important. CPO(コパッケージドオプティクス)

items.n: CPU time
items.x: The total time the CPU spent executing a program's instructions, excluding waits; with parallel execution it can exceed wall-clock time. CPU時間

items.n: CRC (cyclic redundancy check)
items.x: An error-detection method that treats the data bits as a polynomial, appends the remainder of dividing it by a generator polynomial, and lets the receiver repeat the calculation to detect errors. It is widely used in Ethernet, PCI Express, USB and file formats. CRC(巡回冗長検査)

items.n: Credit-based flow control
items.x: A scheme in which the receiver advertises free buffer space as credits and the sender transmits only within them, so buffers never overflow. クレジット方式のフロー制御

items.n: Critical path
items.x: The path with the largest delay in a circuit, which sets the maximum clock frequency. In STA it is the path with the smallest slack, and speeding up a design starts by reducing its delay. クリティカルパス

items.n: Critical path method (CPM)
items.x: A scheduling technique that uses the durations of a project's activities and the order relations between them to find each activity's earliest and latest start and its float, and then finds the longest path connecting activities with zero float (the critical path) and the total project duration. A delay in any activity on the critical path delays the whole project. クリティカルパス法(CPM)

items.n: Critical section
items.x: A part of a program that operates on shared data and must be run by only one thread at a time. It is protected by a lock and kept as short as possible. クリティカルセクション

items.n: Critical thickness
items.x: The maximum thickness to which a lattice-mismatched layer can be grown while staying strained without forming dislocations. Beyond it, misfit dislocations appear. 臨界膜厚

items.n: Cross-point memory
items.x: Memory with a storage element at each intersection of row and column lines. It is very dense, but a selector is placed in series with each element to stop current sneaking through unselected cells. クロスポイント型メモリ

items.n: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
items.x: A vulnerability in which a web application outputs user input into HTML as is, so that a script contained in the input runs in visitors' browsers as a page of that site. Escaping characters with special meaning on output is the fundamental countermeasure. クロスサイトスクリプティング(XSS)

items.n: Cross-validation
items.x: A method that splits the data into k groups, trains on all but one group and evaluates on the remaining one, repeats this k times while rotating the evaluation group, and estimates the model's performance as the average of the k evaluations (k-fold cross-validation). Every data point is used for evaluation exactly once, so limited data is used efficiently and the variation of the estimate caused by how the data happens to be split is reduced. It is used for tuning hyperparameters and selecting models, at roughly k times the computation. 交差検証

items.n: Crossover distortion
items.x: Distortion in a class-B push-pull amplifier near 0 V, where neither transistor conducts during the handover between positive and negative half-cycles. Class-AB biasing with a small idle current reduces it. クロスオーバーひずみ

items.n: Crosstalk
items.x: Noise that appears on one wire when the signal on a neighboring wire changes, mainly through capacitive coupling. Wider spacing and shield wires reduce it. クロストーク

items.n: CRPR (clock reconvergence pessimism removal)
items.x: A correction in OCV-based STA that adds back to the slack the difference caused by applying both slow and fast factors to the shared portion of the launch and capture clock paths. The shared portion is physically the same, so it cannot be both slow and fast within one clock edge. CRPR(共通パスの悲観性の除去)

items.n: Crystal orientation
items.x: The direction of crystal planes and axes, expressed with Miller indices such as (100). The (100) surface is standard for silicon wafers used for MOSFETs. 結晶方位

items.n: CSMA/CA
items.x: The access control method used in wireless LAN. A station checks that the channel is idle, waits an additional random time before sending, and confirms delivery with an ACK from the receiver, so as to avoid collisions as far as possible. CSMA/CA

items.n: CSP (chip-scale package)
items.x: A general term for packages shrunk to nearly the size of the chip. They are widely used in compact devices such as smartphones. CSP(チップサイズパッケージ)

items.n: CUDA
items.x: NVIDIA's platform for general-purpose computing on its GPUs. Kernels are written in an extended C++, with parallelism expressed as a grid, blocks and threads. CUDA

items.n: Current gain (hFE)
items.x: The ratio of collector current to base current (IC/IB) in a bipolar transistor. 電流増幅率(hFE)

items.n: Current mirror
items.x: A circuit that uses two matched transistors to copy the current flowing in one into the other (or at a fixed ratio). It is widely used for bias current sources and active loads in analog ICs. カレントミラー回路

items.n: Cutoff frequency
items.x: The frequency at which the output of a filter or amplifier falls 3 dB (to about 0.707 times) below the passband. For an RC circuit it is 1/(2πRC). カットオフ周波数

items.n: Cutoff region
items.x: The state of a bipolar transistor in which both junctions are reverse-biased and almost no collector current flows. It corresponds to a switch in the off state. 遮断領域

items.n: CVD
items.x: Chemical vapor deposition. A method of depositing thin films on a wafer through chemical reactions of source gases. CVD

items.n: Cycles per instruction (CPI)
items.x: The average number of clock cycles per instruction, one factor in execution time = instruction count × CPI × cycle time, and the reciprocal of IPC. CPI

items.n: Czochralski (CZ) method
items.x: A method of making single-crystal silicon by dipping a seed crystal into molten silicon in a crucible and slowly pulling it up while rotating. CZ法(チョクラルスキー法)

items.n: Damascene process
items.x: A method of forming interconnects by etching trenches in an insulating film, filling them with metal, and removing the excess metal by CMP. Used for copper wiring. ダマシン法

items.n: Dark current
items.x: Current that flows in a photodiode even without light, caused for example by thermal generation of carriers. It rises with temperature and appears as noise in dark images. 暗電流

items.n: Darlington connection
items.x: A connection that feeds the emitter current of one transistor into the base of a second. The overall current gain is roughly the product of the two, so a small base current can control a large current. ダーリントン接続

items.n: Data parallelism
items.x: Distributed training in which each GPU holds a full model replica, processes its share of the data, and gradients are averaged across GPUs before updating. データ並列

items.n: Data race
items.x: A situation in which threads access the same variable concurrently without synchronization and at least one access is a write. Results vary between runs; in C and C++ it is undefined behavior. データ競合

items.n: Database index
items.x: A data structure in a database for quickly finding, from a value in a particular column of a table, the location of the rows holding that value. B+ trees are commonly used. It makes searches faster but must be maintained every time a row is inserted, updated or deleted, and it uses storage. インデックス

items.n: Database view
items.x: In a relational database, a virtual table defined by giving a name to a SELECT statement. It normally holds no data of its own and builds its result from the underlying tables each time it is referenced. It is used to simplify complex queries and to restrict access by limiting the columns and rows shown. ビュー

items.n: DC-DC converter
items.x: A circuit that converts one DC voltage into another. Using switches, inductors and capacitors, buck types lower the voltage and boost types raise it. DC-DCコンバータ

items.n: DDR SDRAM
items.x: Synchronous DRAM that transfers data on both the rising and falling clock edges. Successive generations such as DDR4 and DDR5 have raised the data rate. It is the standard main memory of PCs and servers. DDR SDRAM

items.n: De Morgan's theorem
items.x: The rules for transforming logic expressions: NOT (A AND B) equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B), and NOT (A OR B) equals (NOT A) AND (NOT B). ド・モルガンの定理

items.n: Dead time
items.x: A short interval during which both the upper and lower switches of an inverter are off while switching between them. It prevents both from being on at once and shorting the supply. デッドタイム

items.n: Deadlock
items.x: A state in which threads each hold a resource while waiting for one held by another, so none can proceed. Fixing a global lock order prevents it. デッドロック

items.n: Deal-Grove model
items.x: A model of thermal oxidation in which the oxidant diffuses through the oxide and reacts with silicon at the Si/SiO2 interface. Thickness grows linearly with time for thin oxides and with the square root of time for thick ones. Deal-Groveモデル

items.n: Debouncing
items.x: Processing that removes switch bounce, by software that accepts a change only after repeated identical readings or by hardware filtering. デバウンス

items.n: Decoder
items.x: A circuit that activates exactly one of 2ⁿ outputs according to an n-bit input. It is used to select the row addressed in a memory. The reverse function is an encoder. デコーダ

items.n: Decoherence
items.x: The process by which a qubit, through interactions with its environment, loses the phase and energy information of its superposition and its quantum properties break down. Its speed is described by the energy relaxation time T1 and the dephasing time T2. デコヒーレンス

items.n: Default gateway
items.x: The router to which a host hands packets for destinations on other networks. The host uses its subnet mask to decide whether a destination is on the same network, and sends to this router if not. デフォルトゲートウェイ

items.n: Defect inspection system
items.x: Equipment that finds particles and pattern defects on wafers, for example by detecting scattered light or by comparing images of neighboring dies. 欠陥検査装置

items.n: Degenerate semiconductor
items.x: A semiconductor doped so heavily that the Fermi level lies inside the conduction or valence band. It behaves almost like a metal and is used in tunnel diodes and low-resistance contacts. 縮退半導体

items.n: Delta-sigma ADC
items.x: An ADC that oversamples at a high rate, pushes quantization noise to high frequencies and then filters it out. Used in high-resolution applications such as audio and measurement. ΔΣ型ADC

items.n: Demand paging
items.x: Loading a program's pages into physical memory only when first accessed and a page fault occurs, rather than all at once. It speeds startup and saves memory for unused parts. デマンドページング

items.n: Dennard scaling
items.x: The rule that shrinking transistor dimensions and supply voltage by the same factor gives faster, denser circuits at constant power density. It broke down in the mid-2000s when voltages could no longer be lowered easily. デナードスケーリング

items.n: Depletion layer
items.x: A region near a PN junction boundary that contains almost no carriers. It widens under reverse bias. 空乏層

items.n: Depreciation
items.x: The accounting procedure of allocating the acquisition cost of long-lived assets such as equipment and buildings as an expense over the period of use (the useful life). Typical methods are the straight-line and declining-balance methods. 減価償却

items.n: Depth of focus (DOF)
items.x: The range of focus over which a pattern prints with acceptable quality. Raising the numerical aperture improves resolution but reduces DOF, which makes wafer planarity important. 焦点深度(DOF)

items.n: Depth-first search
items.x: A way of searching a graph or tree that goes as far as possible along one path and backtracks to try another path when it reaches a dead end. It is implemented with recursion or a stack and is used for maze solving, finding connected components and cycles, and topological sorting. It is abbreviated DFS. 深さ優先探索

items.n: Derating
items.x: Using parts with margin below their ratings for voltage, current, temperature and so on, rather than at the full rating, to improve reliability. Typical guidelines are voltage at no more than 70 to 80% of rating, or junction temperature at no more than 125 °C against a 150 °C maximum. ディレーティング

items.n: Device driver
items.x: An OS component that operates a specific peripheral. It handles the device's registers and interrupts and lets applications use the device through a common interface. デバイスドライバ

items.n: DFT (design for testability)
items.x: A design approach that builds test features such as scan chains and BIST into the circuit in advance. DFT(テスト容易化設計)

items.n: DHCP
items.x: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol. A protocol that automatically assigns devices joining a network an IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS servers and other settings for a limited time. DHCP

items.n: Diagnostic coverage
items.x: The fraction of faults that a safety mechanism can detect or control, abbreviated DC. Adding a safety mechanism with 99% diagnostic coverage to a 200 FIT circuit leaves 2 FIT of undetected faults. 診断カバレッジ

items.n: Diamond semiconductor
items.x: A semiconductor made from diamond, a crystal of carbon. With a bandgap of about 5.5 eV, one of the highest thermal conductivities of any material and a high breakdown field, it is promising for high-voltage, high-frequency and high-temperature devices, but n-type doping and large substrates are difficult. ダイヤモンド半導体

items.n: DIBL
items.x: Short for drain-induced barrier lowering. In short-channel MOSFETs, a higher drain voltage lowers the potential barrier at the source, reducing the threshold voltage and increasing off-state leakage. DIBL

items.n: Dicing
items.x: Cutting a wafer into individual chips (dies). Besides sawing with a rotating blade, there are methods such as stealth dicing, which forms a modified layer inside the wafer with a laser. ダイシング

items.n: Die bonding
items.x: Attaching and fixing a diced chip at its position on a lead frame or package substrate, using adhesive, solder or sintered material. ダイボンディング

items.n: Differential amplifier
items.x: A circuit that amplifies the difference between two inputs while rejecting components common to both, such as noise. It is used as the input stage of op-amps. 差動増幅回路

items.n: Differential backup
items.x: A backup method that backs up all data changed since the previous full backup. Each backup grows as the days since the full backup increase, but a restore needs only two: the full backup and the latest differential backup. 差分バックアップ

items.n: Differential signaling
items.x: Signaling that sends opposite signals on two wires and represents 0 and 1 by their voltage difference. Noise picked up equally on both cancels, allowing fast transmission with small swings. 差動信号

items.n: Diffusion capacitance
items.x: Capacitance in a forward-biased PN junction caused by injected minority carriers stored in the neutral regions. It grows in proportion to forward current and limits high-speed operation. 拡散容量

items.n: Diffusion length
items.x: The average distance minority carriers diffuse before recombining, given by L = √(Dτ) from the diffusion coefficient D and lifetime τ. It strongly affects the efficiency of solar cells and photodetectors. 拡散長

items.n: Digital signature
items.x: A technique for confirming who created an electronic document and that it has not been altered since. The signer processes the document's hash value with their own private key to create the signature, and the recipient verifies it with the signer's public key. It is also used for non-repudiation. デジタル署名

items.n: Dijkstra's algorithm
items.x: An algorithm that finds the shortest paths from one starting vertex to every vertex in a graph whose edge weights are 0 or greater. It repeatedly finalizes the nearest vertex whose distance is not yet final and updates the distances of its neighbors. It does not work correctly with negative edge weights. ダイクストラ法

items.n: Dilute hydrofluoric acid (DHF)
items.x: Hydrofluoric acid diluted with water. It removes native oxide from silicon and leaves a hydrophobic, hydrogen-terminated surface. 希フッ酸(DHF)

items.n: Dilution refrigerator
items.x: A refrigerator that uses a mixture of helium-3 and helium-4 to produce cryogenic temperatures of about 10 mK continuously. It is used to operate superconducting qubits and silicon spin qubits. The cooling power of its coldest stage is small, roughly ten to several tens of µW, so heat flowing in through the wiring is a challenge for scaling up. 希釈冷凍機

items.n: DIMM
items.x: A memory module that mounts several DRAM chips on a small board so it can be plugged into a slot in a PC or server. DIMM

items.n: Direct band gap
items.x: A band structure in which the bottom of the conduction band and the top of the valence band are at the same wave number. Electron-hole recombination emits light efficiently. Example: GaAs. 直接遷移型

items.n: Direct-conversion receiver
items.x: A receiver architecture (zero-IF) that sets the local oscillator (LO) to the received frequency and converts directly to baseband without an intermediate frequency, using two mixers for the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) components. It needs no image-reject or IF filters and is easy to integrate on one CMOS chip. On the other hand, it needs countermeasures against the DC shift (DC offset) caused by LO leakage, 1/f noise and I/Q imbalance. ダイレクトコンバージョン方式

items.n: Direct-mapped cache
items.x: A cache organization in which each address can be placed in exactly one location. It is simple with short hit time, but prone to conflict misses when addresses compete for the same slot. ダイレクトマップ方式

items.n: Directed self-assembly (DSA)
items.x: A technique that uses the tendency of block copolymers to form regular fine patterns on their own, aligning their position and orientation with guides made by lithography to create patterns finer than the resolution limit. Reducing defects to extremely low levels is the challenge for volume production. 誘導自己組織化(DSA)

items.n: Directory-based coherence
items.x: A coherence approach that records in a table which cores hold each line and notifies only those cores. Used in systems with many cores. ディレクトリ方式

items.n: Discrete semiconductor
items.x: The category of semiconductor products that perform one function as a single device, such as diodes, individual transistors and power MOSFETs, as opposed to integrated circuits. ディスクリート半導体

items.n: Dishing
items.x: A CMP phenomenon in which the center of a wide metal line is over-polished into a dish-like depression. ディッシング

items.n: DMA (direct memory access)
items.x: A mechanism that transfers data directly between peripherals and memory without going through the CPU, so the CPU can do other work during large transfers. DMA(ダイレクトメモリアクセス)

items.n: DNL (differential nonlinearity)
items.x: The error in each code step width of an ADC relative to the ideal 1 LSB. When it reaches −1 LSB, a missing code occurs. DNL(微分非直線性)

items.n: DNS (Domain Name System)
items.x: A system, managed in a distributed way by servers around the world, that maps domain names such as www.example.com to the IP addresses used for communication. DNS

items.n: Donor
items.x: An impurity that supplies electrons to a semiconductor. For silicon, group V elements such as phosphorus (P) and arsenic (As) act as donors and make n-type semiconductors. ドナー

items.n: Downflow
items.x: A cleanroom airflow method that sends clean air in one direction from the entire ceiling to the floor, quickly carrying generated particles away under the floor. ダウンフロー

items.n: DRAM (dynamic random-access memory)
items.x: Volatile memory that stores each bit in a cell of one transistor and one capacitor and needs periodic refresh before the charge leaks away. It is used as main memory in PCs and servers. DRAM(ダイナミックRAM)

items.n: DRC (design rule check)
items.x: Verification that checks whether a layout follows the geometric rules required for manufacturing, such as line widths and spacings. DRC(デザインルールチェック)

items.n: Drive-in
items.x: In thermal diffusion, the high-temperature step after a fixed amount of dopant has been introduced at the surface (predeposition), which pushes the dopant deeper. ドライブイン

items.n: Dropout voltage
items.x: The minimum input-to-output voltage difference a linear regulator needs to hold its output voltage. It increases with output current and, usually, with temperature; for LDOs it is typically tens to hundreds of mV. ドロップアウト電圧

items.n: Dry etching
items.x: Removing material with plasma or gas instead of liquid chemicals. Combining ion bombardment allows anisotropic etching, which is essential for fine patterns. ドライエッチング

items.n: Dry oxidation
items.x: Thermal oxidation with dry oxygen. Growth is slow, but it produces dense, high-quality oxide, used for gate oxides and the like. ドライ酸化

items.n: DTCO (design-technology co-optimization)
items.x: Optimizing cell area and performance by considering circuit design and process technology together, as scaling becomes harder. DTCO(設計・技術協調最適化)

items.n: Dual damascene
items.x: Forming both the trench for a wire and the hole for a via in the insulator, filling them with copper together and finishing with a single CMP step. It reduces process steps. デュアルダマシン法

items.n: Dual system
items.x: A redundancy scheme in which two systems perform the same processing at the same time and operate while comparing the results. Errors can be noticed from disagreements in the results, and if one system fails the other continues processing as is. Reliability is high, but the cost is large because two sets of equipment do the same work. デュアルシステム

items.n: Duplex system
items.x: A redundancy scheme that builds a system from a primary (active) system that does the processing and a standby system kept ready for failures, and switches to the standby to continue processing when the primary fails. Depending on how ready the standby is, it is classified as hot standby, warm standby or cold standby. デュプレックスシステム

items.n: Duty cycle
items.x: The fraction of each period during which a periodic pulse signal is high. In PWM it sets the average power. デューティ比

items.n: DUV (deep ultraviolet)
items.x: Light in the deep-ultraviolet range used in semiconductor lithography. DUV lithography generally refers to exposure using KrF excimer lasers (248 nm) and ArF excimer lasers (193 nm) as light sources. DUV(深紫外線)

items.n: DVFS (dynamic voltage and frequency scaling)
items.x: Changing operating frequency and supply voltage dynamically according to load. Since dynamic power scales with the square of voltage, lowering voltage during light loads saves a lot of power. DVFS(動的電圧・周波数制御)

items.n: Dynamic linker
items.x: Software that, when a dynamically linked program starts, finds and loads shared libraries, applies relocations and binds symbols before starting the program, such as ld.so on Linux. 動的リンカ

items.n: Dynamic linking
items.x: Linking that loads and binds shared libraries at run time. Libraries can be shared between processes and fixed by replacement, but a compatible library must be present on the system. 動的リンク

items.n: Dynamic power
items.x: Power consumed in CMOS circuits charging and discharging capacitance when signals switch, expressed as αCV²f with activity factor α, capacitance C, voltage V and frequency f. 動的消費電力

items.n: Dynamic programming
items.x: An algorithm design method that splits a problem into smaller subproblems and records their answers in a table for reuse, avoiding repeated computation of the same thing. It is used for the knapsack problem, minimum-coin change, the longest common subsequence, shortest paths and more. 動的計画法

items.n: DZ (denuded zone)
items.x: A layer near the wafer surface with few defects such as oxygen precipitates, made by out-diffusing oxygen during heat treatment. Devices are built in this layer while precipitates deeper inside provide gettering. DZ(無欠陥層)

items.n: E-R diagram
items.x: A diagram depicting the things managed in a database (entities) and the relationships between them. Relationships have multiplicities such as one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many. A many-to-many relationship is implemented in tables by adding an associative entity that holds both primary keys as foreign keys, breaking it into two one-to-many relationships. E-R図

items.n: Early effect
items.x: A phenomenon in which raising the collector voltage widens the base-collector depletion layer, narrowing the effective base width and slightly increasing collector current. アーリー効果

items.n: Earned value management (EVM)
items.x: A technique for managing a project's progress and cost by comparing them on a monetary scale using the planned value (PV), earned value (EV) and actual cost (AC). The schedule performance index SPI = EV ÷ PV and the cost performance index CPI = EV ÷ AC are used to judge delays and budget overruns and to estimate the total cost at completion. アーンドバリューマネジメント(EVM)

items.n: ECC (error-correcting code)
items.x: A scheme that adds redundant bits to data so that bit errors can be detected and corrected on readout. It is used in server memory, flash memory and inside DDR5 chips, among others. ECC(誤り訂正符号)

items.n: ECU (electronic control unit)
items.x: An in-vehicle controller built around a microcontroller that controls the engine, brakes, doors and so on. ECUs multiplied with each new function, sometimes exceeding 100 per car, and are now being consolidated through zonal architectures and similar approaches. ECU(電子制御ユニット)

items.n: Edge coupler
items.x: A device that couples light by butting an optical fiber against the edge facet of the chip. An inverse taper that narrows the waveguide tip expands the optical mode to match the fiber. It offers low loss over a wide wavelength range but needs facet preparation and is hard to test at wafer level. エッジカプラ

items.n: EDX (energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy)
items.x: An analysis method that measures the energies of characteristic X-rays emitted under an electron beam to identify which elements are present and how much. It is used with SEM or TEM. EDX(エネルギー分散型X線分光)

items.n: EFEM
items.x: Short for equipment front end module: the unit at the front of a tool that opens FOUPs and transfers wafers into the tool in a clean environment. It includes load ports and a transfer robot. EFEM

items.n: Effective mass
items.x: An apparent mass used to treat electrons and holes in a crystal as if they were free particles responding to external forces. It is set by the curvature of the band; a smaller effective mass tends to give higher mobility. 有効質量

items.n: Efficiency droop
items.x: The drop in luminous efficiency of InGaN LEDs as current increases. Auger recombination is thought to be one cause. 効率ドループ

items.n: eFuse
items.x: One-time-programmable storage written bit by bit by blowing thin wires with current, used for per-device keys, settings and anti-rollback counters. eFuse
