items.n: Einstein relation
items.x: The relation D = μkT/q that links the diffusion coefficient D and mobility μ of carriers. It shows that materials with higher mobility also allow faster diffusion. アインシュタインの関係式

items.n: Electroforming
items.x: An initialization step for ReRAM in which a relatively high voltage is first applied after fabrication to create the conductive filament that later switches resistance. フォーミング

items.n: Electromigration
items.x: The movement of metal atoms in interconnects caused by electric current. It creates voids and hillocks that lead to open or short circuits. エレクトロマイグレーション

items.n: Electron affinity
items.x: The energy difference between the vacuum level and the bottom of the conduction band of a semiconductor. It is used to estimate band offsets at heterojunctions and barrier heights at metal contacts. 電子親和力

items.n: Electroplating
items.x: Depositing metal by passing current through a plating bath with the wafer as the cathode. It fills copper interconnect trenches, with additives making the fill proceed from the bottom up. 電解めっき

items.n: Electrostatic chuck
items.x: A mechanism that holds the wafer to its stage by electrostatic force. It works in vacuum and allows backside gas for temperature control; it is widely used in deposition and etch tools. 静電チャック

items.n: Ellipsometry
items.x: A measurement method that shines polarized light on a sample and determines thin-film thickness and refractive index from the change in polarization on reflection. It is nondestructive. エリプソメトリ

items.n: Emitter follower
items.x: A common-collector amplifier. Its voltage gain is about 1, but its high input impedance and low output impedance make it a buffer that drives the next stage without loading the signal. エミッタフォロワ

items.n: Endpoint detection
items.x: Detecting the moment when the target film has been fully etched, commonly by monitoring changes in the plasma's emission spectrum. 終点検出

items.n: Energy-delay product (EDP)
items.x: A metric multiplying energy per operation by its duration, used to evaluate the balance between energy efficiency and speed. エネルギー遅延積

items.n: ENOB (effective number of bits)
items.x: The real performance of an ADC, including noise and distortion (SINAD), expressed as the bit count of an ideal ADC. A 12-bit ADC with an ENOB of around 10 bits is not unusual. ENOB(有効ビット数)

items.n: Entry point
items.x: The address where a program begins execution, recorded in the ELF header. In C it is usually start-up code such as _start, which initializes and then calls main. エントリポイント

items.n: EOT (equivalent oxide thickness)
items.x: The thickness of SiO2 that would give the same gate capacitance as a gate insulator such as a high-k film. A physically thick film can have a small EOT, giving high capacitance while limiting tunneling current. EOT(等価酸化膜厚)

items.n: Epitaxial growth
items.x: A technique for growing a single-crystal thin film on a single-crystal substrate with the same crystal orientation as the substrate. エピタキシャル成長

items.n: Epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELO)
items.x: Growing crystal from mask openings and letting it spread sideways over the mask. Dislocations from below do not propagate into the overgrown regions, reducing dislocations in materials such as GaN. 横方向エピタキシャル成長(ELO)

items.n: Equivalence partitioning
items.x: A black-box testing technique that divides the inputs into groups that the program should handle in the same way (equivalence classes) and tests one representative value from each class. Both valid classes of accepted inputs and invalid classes of inputs that should cause an error are chosen. 同値分割

items.n: Erosion
items.x: In CMP, excessive polishing of an entire region of dense lines, insulator included, so it ends up lower than its surroundings. Along with dishing of wide lines, it is a typical CMP defect. エロージョン

items.n: Errata
items.x: A document listing known defects found after shipment, such as behavior that differs from the specification, together with the affected chip revisions, the conditions under which they occur, and workarounds. It is provided for complex ICs such as microcontrollers and should be checked early in design. エラッタ

items.n: Escalation
items.x: In IT service management, handing an incident or similar matter that the person in charge cannot resolve alone over to another person or team, or asking someone higher up for a decision. Functional escalation passes it to a technical team with the specialist knowledge or authority needed to resolve it, while hierarchical escalation reports to higher management to obtain decisions or resources when the target time is about to be exceeded or the impact is large. The conditions for escalation and the contacts are decided in advance. エスカレーション

items.n: ESD (electrostatic discharge)
items.x: A sudden discharge of static electricity from a charged person or object. Applied to an IC pin it can destroy gate oxides and other structures, so I/O pins have protection circuits. ESD(静電気放電)

items.n: EUV lithography
items.x: Lithography using extreme ultraviolet light with a wavelength of 13.5 nm. It uses reflective optics and a vacuum environment. EUV露光

items.n: Executable and Linkable Format (ELF)
items.x: The file format used for object files, executables and shared libraries on Linux and other UNIX-like systems and in embedded devices. ELF

items.n: Expected value
items.x: The average value taken by a quantity determined by chance. It is found by multiplying each possible value by the probability of that value and adding the results. For example, the expected value of a die roll is (1 + 2 + … + 6) ÷ 6 = 3.5. The expected value of a sum is the sum of the expected values (linearity of expectation), and this holds even for quantities that are not independent. It is used for comparing countermeasures by expected loss, for decision making and for calculating averages in queueing. 期待値

items.n: Exponent field
items.x: The bits of a floating-point number giving the power of two. To represent negative exponents, the true exponent plus a bias (127 for single precision) is stored. 指数部

items.n: Exponential distribution
items.x: A continuous probability distribution followed by the intervals between randomly occurring events and by the time to failure of a part with a constant failure rate. With rate λ, the probability that the event does not occur by time t is e^(−λt), and the mean is 1/λ. It is memoryless: the distribution of the remaining time does not depend on how much time has already passed. It is used as the model of the intervals between arrivals when the number of arrivals follows a Poisson distribution and of the time to failure in the random-failure period, and it is an assumption of the M/M/1 queueing model. 指数分布

items.n: Exposed pad
items.x: A large metal area on the underside of packages such as QFN, connected to the die pad. Soldered to the board, it is the main path for removing heat and is usually tied to inner-layer planes with thermal vias. 露出パッド(エクスポーズドパッド)

items.n: Extinction ratio
items.x: In intensity modulation, the ratio of the optical power P1 for a "1" to the power P0 for a "0", expressed in dB as 10 log(P1/P0). The larger it is, the greater the difference between 1 and 0 and the fewer decision errors at the receiver. 消光比

items.n: Eye diagram
items.x: A plot overlaying many bit periods of a waveform. The height of the central eye shows noise margin and its width shows timing margin. アイパターン

items.n: Fabless
items.x: A company model that owns no fabrication plant and focuses on designing and selling semiconductors. ファブレス

items.n: Fading
items.x: In radio communication, large variation of received power with location, time and frequency. In multipath fading, waves reflected by buildings and other objects arrive over paths of different lengths and interfere, and received power can drop by several tens of dB. The variation becomes faster when the terminal moves. Countermeasures include diversity, OFDM and error-correcting codes. フェージング

items.n: Fail-safe
items.x: The design concept of making a system go into a safe state when a failure or abnormality occurs. Examples include railway signals that fall to red or stop when they fail, and normally closed valves that close when power or air pressure is lost. フェールセーフ

items.n: Fail-soft
items.x: The design concept of isolating the failed part when part of a system fails and keeping the system as a whole operating, even with reduced function or performance. An example is a system in which several servers share the processing and the rest continue processing when one fails. フェールソフト

items.n: False path
items.x: A path that exists structurally but along which no signal actually propagates in operation. It is excluded from STA as a timing exception, specified with set_false_path in SDC. フォールスパス

items.n: False sharing
items.x: A slowdown in which threads update different variables that happen to share a cache line, so the line bounces between cores. 偽共有

items.n: Faraday cup
items.x: A device that collects an ion beam and measures the resulting current. In ion implanters it is used to determine the implanted dose. ファラデーカップ

items.n: Fault coverage
items.x: The fraction of modeled faults that a set of test patterns can detect. The higher it is, the less likely defective chips are to escape. 故障検出率(フォールトカバレッジ)

items.n: Fault injection attack
items.x: An attack that deliberately makes a chip malfunction with voltage or clock glitches, lasers and the like to bypass authentication or infer keys. 故障注入攻撃

items.n: Fault tolerance
items.x: The concept of accepting that parts and equipment will fail and, through means such as redundancy, ensuring that the system as a whole keeps operating correctly even if part of it fails. It is contrasted with fault avoidance, which makes failures themselves less likely. フォールトトレランス

items.n: FD-SOI (fully depleted SOI)
items.x: Building transistors in a very thin silicon layer on buried oxide so the channel is fully depleted. The channel can be lightly doped, and body bias can tune the threshold voltage easily. FD-SOI(完全空乏型SOI)

items.n: FeFET (ferroelectric FET)
items.x: A transistor with a ferroelectric gate insulator. Its threshold voltage depends on the polarization direction, so a single transistor can store data non-volatilely and be read non-destructively. FeFET(強誘電体トランジスタ)

items.n: FeRAM (ferroelectric RAM)
items.x: Nonvolatile memory that stores information in the polarization direction of a ferroelectric. Writes are fast and low-power, and it is used in IC cards and the like. FeRAM(強誘電体メモリ)

items.n: Fermi level
items.x: The energy at which the probability of an electron occupying a state is exactly one half. It lies closer to the conduction band in n-type material and closer to the valence band in p-type. フェルミ準位

items.n: FFU (fan filter unit)
items.x: A unit combining a fan with a high-efficiency filter. Arrays of them in the cleanroom ceiling blow clean air downward. FFU(ファンフィルタユニット)

items.n: FIB (focused ion beam)
items.x: An instrument that mills or deposits material with a finely focused ion beam. It is used for cross-sectioning tiny areas, preparing thin TEM samples and editing circuits. FIB(集束イオンビーム)

items.n: FinFET
items.x: A 3D transistor whose channel stands up like a fin and is surrounded by the gate on three sides. It suppresses short-channel effects well. FinFET

items.n: FIT rate
items.x: A unit of failure rate: 1 FIT is one failure per billion (10⁹) device-hours. It is used for parts with very low failure rates, such as semiconductors. FIT

items.n: Five forces analysis
items.x: A method, proposed by Michael Porter, of analyzing an industry's profitability through five competitive forces: rivalry among existing competitors, the threat of new entrants, the threat of substitutes, the bargaining power of suppliers and the bargaining power of buyers. ファイブフォース分析

items.n: Fixed cost
items.x: A cost incurred in a constant amount each period regardless of production volume or sales, such as depreciation of equipment and buildings, rent and the salaries of permanent employees. 固定費

items.n: Fixed point
items.x: Representing fractions with ordinary integer bit patterns and an agreed binary-point position. Integer arithmetic circuits suffice, giving small, low-power hardware, but the range is narrow. Formats are often named by fraction bits, as in Q15. 固定小数点

items.n: Fixed-pattern noise
items.x: Noise that appears in the same place every time, caused by variations between pixels or readout circuits. It is removed by correlated double sampling or calibration. 固定パターンノイズ

items.n: Flame graph
items.x: A profiling visualization stacking call chains vertically, with each function's width showing its share of time. フレームグラフ

items.n: Flash ADC
items.x: The fastest type of ADC, which compares the input against many comparators at once. N bits need 2ᴺ − 1 comparators, so the circuit grows rapidly with resolution. フラッシュ型ADC

items.n: FlashAttention
items.x: A fast attention implementation that tiles the computation in on-chip memory and never writes the large intermediate table to HBM. Its results match standard attention. FlashAttention

items.n: Flat-band voltage
items.x: The gate voltage at which the bands at the semiconductor surface of a MOS structure are flat. It is set by the work-function difference between gate and substrate and by charges in the oxide, and is one component of the threshold voltage. フラットバンド電圧

items.n: Flip chip
items.x: A mounting method in which the chip is placed face down and connected directly to the substrate with bumps. Short connections make it suitable for high pin counts. フリップチップ

items.n: Flip-flop
items.x: The basic element of sequential circuits that stores one bit. A D flip-flop captures its input at a clock edge. フリップフロップ

items.n: Floating gate
items.x: An electrode in a flash memory cell that is completely surrounded by insulator. Storing electrons on it shifts the transistor's threshold voltage, so data is kept even without power. フローティングゲート

items.n: Floating-point absorption
items.x: Loss of the smaller operand's low-order digits when adding numbers of very different magnitude, because they do not fit in the significand. It matters when summing many small values. 情報落ち

items.n: FMEA (failure mode and effects analysis)
items.x: A method that lists the possible failure modes of a product or process, evaluates their effects and severity, and plans countermeasures in advance. FMEA(故障モード影響解析)

items.n: Fool-proof
items.x: The design concept of ensuring that incorrect human operation does not lead to a hazardous state or malfunction, or that incorrect operation is not possible in the first place. Examples include connectors shaped so that they cannot be inserted the wrong way round and equipment that does not start unless its door is closed. フールプルーフ

items.n: Foreign key
items.x: A column that refers to the primary key (or a unique column) of another table. Through the referential integrity constraint, which allows only values that exist in the referenced table or NULL, it prevents data that points to nonexistent rows. The behavior when a referenced row is deleted or updated (rejection, cascading deletion and so on) can also be specified. 外部キー

items.n: Forming gas anneal
items.x: Heat treatment in a mixture of hydrogen and nitrogen (forming gas). Hydrogen terminates dangling bonds at the Si/SiO2 interface, reducing interface states. フォーミングガスアニール

items.n: Forward bias
items.x: Applying a positive voltage to the p side and a negative voltage to the n side. The barrier drops and current flows readily. The opposite is reverse bias, under which almost no current flows. 順方向バイアス

items.n: Forward-active region
items.x: The state with the base-emitter junction forward-biased and the base-collector junction reverse-biased. A collector current proportional to the base current flows, and it is used for amplification. 能動領域

items.n: Foundry
items.x: A company or business model that specializes in manufacturing semiconductors designed by other companies. ファウンドリ

items.n: FOUP
items.x: A sealed container for transporting and storing 300 mm wafers. FOUP

items.n: Four-point probe method
items.x: A method that passes current through the outer two of four collinear needles and measures voltage across the inner two to find the sheet resistance of wafers and thin films. 四探針法

items.n: Four-state logic
items.x: The four values used in HDL simulation: 0, 1, X (unknown) and Z (high impedance). Uninitialized or conflicting signals become X. 4値論理

items.n: Fowler-Nordheim tunneling
items.x: Current that flows when a strong electric field lets electrons tunnel through the triangular barrier of a thin insulator. It is used to program and erase NAND flash. FNトンネル電流(ファウラー・ノルドハイム)

items.n: FP8
items.x: 8-bit floating-point formats: E4M3 (4 exponent, 3 significand bits) and E5M2 (5 exponent, 2 significand bits), chosen to trade precision against range. Used to make AI training and inference faster and more power-efficient. FP8

items.n: FPGA
items.x: A chip whose logic configuration the user can rewrite after manufacture. It is used for prototypes, low-volume products and ASIC verification. FPGA

items.n: Frame pointer
items.x: A register that keeps pointing at the stack position on function entry; s0 (fp) in RISC-V. Locals can be addressed at fixed offsets, and the call chain is easy to walk. フレームポインタ

items.n: Free-space path loss (FSPL)
items.x: The rate at which radio power weakens as it spreads out spherically with distance between isotropic antennas in free space with no obstacles or reflections. It is given by L = (4πd/λ)², and in dB it grows by about 6 dB each time the distance doubles and by 20 dB each time it increases tenfold. It is used as the reference propagation loss in link budget calculations. 自由空間伝搬損失

items.n: FTTI (fault tolerant time interval)
items.x: The shortest time from the occurrence of a fault to a hazardous event if no safety mechanism acts. A safety mechanism must complete detection of the fault and transition to a safe state within the FTTI. FTTI(フォールトトレラント時間間隔)

items.n: Full adder
items.x: A circuit that adds two bits plus a carry-in from the lower digit and outputs a sum and a carry-out. A version without carry-in is a half adder. Chaining full adders makes a multi-bit adder. 全加算器

items.n: Full-well capacity
items.x: The maximum number of electrons one image-sensor pixel can hold. The larger it is, the brighter the scene can be before highlights clip, widening dynamic range. 飽和電子数(フルウェル容量)

items.n: Fully associative cache
items.x: A cache organization in which any data can be placed in any location. It has no conflict misses but must compare against every tag, so it suits small structures such as TLBs rather than large caches. フルアソシアティブ方式

items.n: Function inlining
items.x: Replacing a function call with the body of the called function. It removes call overhead and enables further optimizations but enlarges the code. インライン展開

items.n: Fused multiply-add
items.x: An operation computing a × b + c in one instruction, rounding only once at the end without rounding the intermediate product. It is faster and more accurate than separate multiply and add and is heavily used in matrix computation. FMA(融合積和演算)

items.n: FZ method (float zone)
items.x: A method that melts a zone of a polysilicon rod and moves that molten zone along to form a single crystal. With no crucible, oxygen content is low, suiting high-resistivity wafers. FZ法(フローティングゾーン法)

items.n: Ga2O3 (gallium oxide)
items.x: An oxide semiconductor with a band gap of about 4.5-4.9 eV, even wider than SiC or GaN. Its crystals can be grown from the melt, and it is being researched as a next-generation power semiconductor material. Ga2O3(酸化ガリウム)

items.n: GAA (gate-all-around)
items.x: A transistor structure in which the gate surrounds the channel on all sides. It controls current better than FinFET and is used in the generations after FinFET. GAA(ゲートオールアラウンド)

items.n: GaAs (gallium arsenide)
items.x: A III-V compound semiconductor of gallium and arsenic with a direct band gap of about 1.42 eV. Its high electron mobility makes it useful for high-frequency transistors and infrared LEDs and lasers. GaAs(ガリウムヒ素)

items.n: Gain-bandwidth product (GBW)
items.x: The product of an op-amp's gain and bandwidth, which stays roughly constant. With a GBW of 1 MHz, for example, a gain-of-10 circuit has a bandwidth of about 100 kHz. 利得帯域幅積(GBW)

items.n: GaN (gallium nitride)
items.x: A III-V compound semiconductor with a band gap of about 3.4 eV. Used in blue LEDs and in high-frequency and power devices. GaN(窒化ガリウム)

items.n: Garbage collection
items.x: In an SSD, moving the still-valid data out of blocks that contain invalid data and then erasing those blocks to create free space. ガベージコレクション

items.n: Gate driver
items.x: A circuit that receives control signals and drives a power device's gate with the right voltage and enough current. Many include isolation or level shifting to drive high-side switches. ゲートドライバ

items.n: Gate-last (replacement metal gate)
items.x: Building the transistor first with a dummy gate, then removing it after high-temperature steps such as source/drain activation and replacing it with a high-k dielectric and metal gate. ゲートラスト(リプレースメントメタルゲート)

items.n: Gate-level simulation
items.x: Simulation of the post-synthesis or post-layout netlist, optionally with delay information, to catch problems invisible at RTL. ゲートレベルシミュレーション

items.n: Generate statement
items.x: A Verilog construct that expands hardware descriptions by loops or conditions, used for example to instantiate a module repeatedly in a regular pattern. generate文

items.n: Geometric mean
items.x: The nth root of the product of n values, used to average performance ratios because the comparison does not depend on the reference chosen. 幾何平均

items.n: Gettering
items.x: A technique that collects and traps metal impurities in a wafer at locations away from the surface where devices are built, using oxygen precipitates and the like. ゲッタリング

items.n: GHS
items.x: The internationally harmonized system that communicates chemical hazards with pictograms and precautionary statements. GHS

items.n: GIDL (gate-induced drain leakage)
items.x: Off-state leakage caused by band-to-band tunneling in the strong field where the gate overlaps the drain. It is a concern for data retention in DRAM, among others. GIDL(ゲート誘起ドレインリーク)

items.n: Glass core substrate
items.x: A package substrate whose core is a sheet of glass instead of glass-fiber-reinforced resin. Because glass is flat and dimensionally stable, it is being developed to form fine wiring and dense through-vias even in large packages. ガラスコア基板

items.n: Glitch
items.x: An unwanted momentary pulse on an output, caused for example by differing delays along signal paths. In combinational logic it is also called a hazard; in DACs it appears when the code changes. グリッチ

items.n: Global offset table
items.x: A table of the actual addresses of external variables and functions, filled in by the dynamic linker at run time. Position-independent code refers to them through it, so code pages need no patching. GOT(グローバルオフセットテーブル)

items.n: Global shutter
items.x: An electronic shutter method that exposes all pixels at the same time. Unlike a rolling shutter, which reads row by row, it does not distort images of moving objects. グローバルシャッター

items.n: GPIO
items.x: General-purpose input/output: microcontroller pins that software can configure as inputs or outputs, used for reading switches, lighting LEDs and so on. GPIO

items.n: GPU
items.x: Short for graphics processing unit: a processor with many simple execution units that processes large amounts of data in parallel. Besides graphics, it is widely used for AI training and inference. GPU

items.n: GPU kernel
items.x: A function that many threads execute simultaneously on a GPU. It is launched from the CPU-side program, and each thread uses its index to choose its data. Distinct from an OS kernel. GPUカーネル

items.n: GPU occupancy
items.x: The ratio of warps actually resident on a GPU SM to the maximum it can hold, determined by register and shared-memory use. 占有率

items.n: GPU shared memory
items.x: Small, fast memory inside each GPU SM that threads of the same block can share. The program decides what is stored there. シェアードメモリ

items.n: Gradient checkpointing
items.x: Storing only some intermediate forward results and recomputing the rest during backpropagation, trading extra computation for less memory. 勾配チェックポイント

items.n: Gradient descent
items.x: An optimization method that computes the gradient of the loss function (the partial derivative with respect to each parameter) and repeatedly moves the parameters a little in the direction opposite to the gradient, searching for parameters that make the loss small. The update is written w ← w − η∇L, where η is called the learning rate. Stochastic gradient descent (SGD), which uses gradients computed on part of the data (a mini-batch), and its refinements such as momentum and Adam are widely used to train neural networks. 勾配降下法

items.n: Grating coupler
items.x: A device that etches a periodic grating into a waveguide so that diffraction redirects light to couple with an optical fiber positioned above the chip. Its advantage is that optical testing is possible on the wafer before dicing, but its coupling bandwidth is narrow and it is polarization dependent. グレーティングカプラ

items.n: Gray code
items.x: A code in which successive values differ in only one bit. It prevents read errors in rotary encoders and when passing counter values between different clock domains. グレイコード

items.n: Greedy algorithm
items.x: An algorithm design method that builds a solution by repeatedly picking the choice that looks best at that moment, without revisiting earlier choices. It is fast and simple, but it gives an optimal solution only when the problem has special properties, as with coin systems like Japan's or Kruskal's algorithm for minimum spanning trees. 貪欲法

items.n: Grid-stride loop
items.x: Writing a kernel as a loop in which each thread processes elements spaced by the total thread count, decoupling launch size from element count. グリッドストライドループ

items.n: Gustafson's law
items.x: The observation that when processors are added and the problem is enlarged, the parallel fraction grows, giving gains nearly proportional to processor count. グスタフソンの法則

items.n: Gyroscope
items.x: A sensor that detects rotation rate (angular velocity). MEMS versions use the Coriolis force acting on a vibrating structure. ジャイロスコープ

items.n: Hall-effect sensor
items.x: A sensor that detects magnetic fields using the Hall effect: a magnetic field applied to a current-carrying semiconductor produces a voltage perpendicular to both. It is used, for example, to sense motor rotation. ホール素子

items.n: Halo implant (pocket implant)
items.x: Angled implantation of dopant of the same type as the channel near the source and drain edges. It limits the spread of the drain depletion region and suppresses short-channel effects. ハロー注入(ポケット注入)

items.n: Handshake
items.x: A scheme that transfers data reliably by exchanging a request (req) from the sender and an acknowledgment (ack) from the receiver. Across clock domains only req and ack are synchronized while the data is held stable, which is safe but takes several cycles or more per transfer. ハンドシェイク

items.n: HARA (hazard analysis and risk assessment)
items.x: The ISO 26262 analysis that identifies hazardous events at the vehicle level and rates severity, exposure and controllability to determine ASILs and safety goals. It is done at the very start of development. HARA(ハザード分析とリスクアセスメント)

items.n: Hard mask
items.x: A durable mask of nitride, carbon, metal or similar used when photoresist alone cannot survive the etch, for example in deep-hole etching. ハードマスク

items.n: Hard real-time
items.x: A strict timing requirement in which missing a deadline even once is a system failure, as in automotive brake or airbag control. Where occasional lateness is acceptable, it is soft real-time. ハードリアルタイム

items.n: Hardware description language (HDL)
items.x: A language for describing the structure and behavior of digital circuits, such as Verilog, SystemVerilog and VHDL, converted into circuits by logic synthesis. ハードウェア記述言語

items.n: Hardware Trojan
items.x: Malicious circuitry inserted during design or manufacturing to leak information or disable operation. It activates only under rare conditions, making it hard to detect. ハードウェアトロイ

items.n: Harmonic mean
items.x: The reciprocal of the mean of reciprocals, used to average rates over equal amounts of work. 調和平均

items.n: Hash function
items.x: A function that computes a value of fixed length (a hash value) from data of any length. Those used in cryptography, such as SHA-256, are built so that it is practically impossible either to find the original data from a hash value or to find two pieces of data with the same hash value, and they are used for detecting tampering, digital signatures and password storage. ハッシュ関数

items.n: Hash table
items.x: A data structure that computes a storage position from a key with a hash function, allowing search, insertion and deletion in O(1) on average. Collisions, where different keys map to the same position, are handled by chaining or open addressing. ハッシュテーブル

items.n: HAST (highly accelerated stress test)
items.x: A test that applies bias in pressurized steam at high humidity and temperatures above 100 °C to evaluate moisture resistance quickly. For example, 96 hours at 130 °C/85% RH is treated as equivalent to 1000 hours of temperature-humidity-bias testing (THB) at 85 °C/85% RH. HAST(高度加速ストレス試験)

items.n: HBM
items.x: High Bandwidth Memory. Multiple DRAM dies stacked with TSVs, achieving very high bandwidth through an extremely wide bus. HBM

items.n: HBT (heterojunction bipolar transistor)
items.x: A bipolar transistor using materials with different band gaps for the emitter and base. Types include SiGe and GaAs-based devices, used in high-frequency amplifiers. HBT(ヘテロ接合バイポーラトランジスタ)

items.n: HDP-CVD (high-density plasma CVD)
items.x: CVD using a high-density plasma that deposits while ion sputtering trims film at the trench openings. It has been used to fill narrow trenches with insulator without voids. HDP-CVD(高密度プラズマCVD)

items.n: Heap memory
items.x: The area from which a running program obtains memory of any size with malloc and the like and returns it with free. Repeated allocation and release can cause fragmentation. ヒープ

items.n: HEMT (high-electron-mobility transistor)
items.x: A transistor that uses the high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas formed at a heterojunction interface as its channel. It is used in high-frequency and high-power applications. HEMT(高電子移動度トランジスタ)

items.n: HEPA filter
items.x: A high-efficiency air filter that captures at least 99.97% of 0.3 µm particles. Filters that capture even finer particles are ULPA filters. HEPAフィルタ

items.n: Heteroepitaxy
items.x: Growing a single-crystal film of a material different from the substrate, such as SiGe on silicon or GaN on sapphire. Growth of the same material is homoepitaxy. ヘテロエピタキシー

items.n: Hidden node problem
items.x: A problem in wireless LANs that occurs when signals from two terminals both reach the access point but the terminals cannot hear each other because of distance or obstacles. Unaware of each other's transmissions, they transmit at the same time and collide at the access point. It is mitigated by RTS/CTS, in which the CTS returned by the access point makes nearby terminals hold off transmitting. 隠れ端末問題

items.n: High-k / metal gate
items.x: The combination of a high-dielectric-constant gate insulator and a metal gate electrode. It keeps gate capacitance high while suppressing gate leakage. High-k/メタルゲート

items.n: High-level synthesis (HLS)
items.x: Automatically generating RTL from an algorithm written in C, C++ or similar. It is used in developing FPGAs and accelerators. 高位合成(HLS)

items.n: High-NA EUV
items.x: Next-generation EUV lithography that raises the projection optics' numerical aperture from 0.33 to 0.55 to improve resolution. High-NA EUV

items.n: High-temperature storage test (HTS)
items.x: A reliability test that keeps products at high temperature without applying voltage to evaluate degradation of wire-bond joints, data retention in nonvolatile memory and similar effects. It is also called HTS or HTSL. 高温放置試験(高温保存試験)

items.n: Hold time
items.x: The minimum time after the active clock edge during which a flip-flop's data input must stay unchanged. Violations are not fixed by lowering the clock frequency, so delay is added to the path. ホールド時間

items.n: Hot carrier injection (HCI)
items.x: Degradation in which carriers accelerated by the strong field near the drain are injected into the gate insulator, shifting the threshold voltage and reducing drive current. ホットキャリア注入(HCI)

items.n: Hot plugging
items.x: Connecting and disconnecting devices with power on while the OS automatically recognizes or detaches them. Used with USB, server SSDs and more. ホットプラグ

items.n: Hot standby
items.x: A scheme in a duplex system in which the standby system is kept running and the primary's data is always reflected to it. When the primary fails, processing can switch to the standby and continue in a short time. A scheme that keeps the standby stopped and starts it after a failure is called a cold standby. ホットスタンバイ

items.n: HTOL (high-temperature operating life test)
items.x: A reliability test that operates products at high temperature under voltage for a long time to accelerate and evaluate chip lifetime and failure rate. A typical condition is 1000 hours at around 125 °C. HTOL(高温動作寿命試験)

items.n: HVPE (hydride vapor phase epitaxy)
items.x: Vapor-phase growth using gallium chloride, formed by reacting HCl with gallium, together with ammonia. Its very high growth rate is used to grow thick GaN crystals for free-standing substrates. HVPE(ハイドライド気相成長)

items.n: Hybrid bonding
items.x: A technique that directly bonds copper electrodes and dielectric surfaces without bumps, providing huge numbers of connections at extremely fine pitch. ハイブリッドボンディング

items.n: Hypervisor
items.x: Software that runs multiple virtual machines on one computer, allocating CPU, memory and devices to each guest OS and isolating them from one another. Also called a virtual machine monitor. ハイパーバイザ

items.n: Hypothesis testing
items.x: A statistical method for judging, on the basis of data, whether to reject a hypothesis such as "there is no difference". The hypothesis to be refuted is set up as the null hypothesis, and the probability of obtaining a result equal to or more extreme than the one observed, assuming it is true (the p-value), is calculated. If the p-value is smaller than a significance level decided in advance (such as 5%), the null hypothesis is rejected. There are type I errors, rejecting a true null hypothesis, and type II errors, failing to reject a false one. 仮説検定

items.n: I2C
items.x: A synchronous serial bus connecting several devices on two wires, clock (SCL) and data (SDA), selecting the partner by address. The lines are open-drain with pull-ups. I2C

items.n: ICP (inductively coupled plasma)
items.x: A method that generates a high-density plasma with RF current in a coil. It makes it easy to control plasma density and the energy of ions reaching the wafer independently. ICP(誘導結合プラズマ)

items.n: IDDQ test
items.x: A test that measures the supply current of a CMOS circuit at rest and flags defects such as bridging faults when it is abnormally high. IDDQテスト

items.n: Ideality factor
items.x: The factor n in the diode equation I ∝ exp(qV/nkT). It is close to 1 when diffusion current dominates and close to 2 when recombination in the depletion layer dominates, so it indicates junction quality. 理想係数

items.n: IDM (integrated device manufacturer)
items.x: A semiconductor company that does everything in-house, from design through front-end and back-end manufacturing to sales. IDM(垂直統合型デバイスメーカー)

items.n: IEEE 754
items.x: The international standard defining floating-point formats and arithmetic, including single (32-bit) and double (64-bit) precision, rounding, and special values such as infinity and NaN, so results agree across computers. IEEE 754

items.n: IGBT
items.x: Insulated-gate bipolar transistor. Driven by a MOS gate, it achieves a low on-state voltage even at high voltage ratings through conductivity modulation. IGBT

items.n: III-V compound semiconductor
items.x: Semiconductors made of group III elements (Ga, In, Al, etc.) and group V elements (As, P, N, etc.), such as GaAs, InP and GaN. III-V族化合物半導体

items.n: Immediate operand
items.x: A constant embedded directly in an instruction. In RISC-V addi it is a 12-bit signed integer that is sign-extended before use. 即値

items.n: Immersion lithography
items.x: Exposure with the space between the lens and the wafer filled with water. It allows a numerical aperture above 1, so ArF excimer lasers can form finer patterns. 液浸露光

items.n: Implant dose
items.x: The number of ions implanted per unit area in ion implantation, expressed in cm⁻². It is set by beam current and implant time. ドーズ量

items.n: In-memory computing
items.x: Performing computations such as multiply-accumulate inside the memory array to cut data movement between memory and processor. Research is under way on using resistive elements and the like for AI inference. インメモリコンピューティング

items.n: Incident management
items.x: The process whose goal is to restore an IT service to normal operation as quickly as possible, using workarounds where needed, when the service stops or degrades because of a failure or similar event (an incident), so that the impact on the business is kept small. It proceeds through logging, categorization and prioritization, investigation and resolution, escalation where needed, and confirmation with the user and closure. Identifying the root cause and preventing recurrence is the role of problem management. インシデント管理

items.n: Income statement (P/L)
items.x: A financial statement that compares revenues and expenses over a period (the accounting period) to show a company's operating results. Subtracting expenses from sales step by step, it shows gross profit, operating profit, ordinary profit (in Japanese statements), profit before income taxes and net income. 損益計算書(P/L)

items.n: Incremental backup
items.x: A backup method that backs up only the data changed since the previous backup, whether full or incremental. Each backup is small and quick, but a restore requires restoring the full backup and then applying every incremental backup after it in order. 増分バックアップ

items.n: Indirect band gap
items.x: A band structure in which the bottom of the conduction band and the top of the valence band occur at different momenta. Transitions need a phonon, so light emission is inefficient. Silicon and germanium are typical examples. 間接遷移型

items.n: Inference runtime
items.x: Software that loads a trained model and runs inference quickly through graph optimization, quantization and hardware-specific kernel selection. 推論ランタイム

items.n: Ingot
items.x: A cylindrical single-crystal block grown by the CZ method or similar, before it is cut into wafers. The ends are removed and the outside is ground to a uniform diameter before slicing. インゴット

items.n: INL (integral nonlinearity)
items.x: The maximum deviation of an ADC's or DAC's actual transfer characteristic from the ideal straight line. It corresponds to the accumulated DNL. INL(積分非直線性)

items.n: InP (indium phosphide)
items.x: A compound semiconductor of indium and phosphorus. As a substrate for lattice-matched layers such as InGaAs, it is used for fiber-optic lasers and photodetectors and for high-speed transistors. InP(リン化インジウム)

items.n: Input capture
items.x: A timer function in which hardware records the counter value at the instant an input signal changes, allowing precise measurement of pulse width or frequency. インプットキャプチャ

items.n: Input offset voltage
items.x: The small voltage that must be applied between an op amp's inputs to bring its output to zero, caused by mismatch among internal devices. It is multiplied by the circuit's gain into an output error: 2 mV at a gain of 100 shifts the output by up to 200 mV. 入力オフセット電圧

items.n: Inrush current
items.x: The large transient current that flows to charge capacitance the instant power is connected to an unpowered circuit, which can sag the supply voltage. 突入電流

items.n: Instruction scheduling
items.x: Reordering instructions without changing results so that latencies of operations and memory accesses are filled with independent instructions. 命令スケジューリング

items.n: Instruction set architecture (ISA)
items.x: The processor specification as seen by software, including the instructions and registers it supports. Examples include x86, Arm and RISC-V. 命令セットアーキテクチャ(ISA)

items.n: Instrumentation amplifier
items.x: A differential amplifier, typically built from three op-amps, with high input impedance and high CMRR. It amplifies small differential signals from sensors with high accuracy. 計装アンプ(インスツルメンテーションアンプ)

items.n: INT8
items.x: An 8-bit signed integer (−128 to 127). In AI inference, quantizing weights and activations to INT8 with a scale factor greatly cuts computation and memory and allows fast processing on small integer circuits. INT8

items.n: Integer division
items.x: Division of integers that produces an integer quotient. How the fractional part is handled differs between languages: some truncate toward zero (C, Java), and others round down toward negative infinity (Python's //). The results are the same for positive numbers but differ for negative ones. 整数除算

items.n: Interconnect via
items.x: A conductor that electrically connects the wiring layers above and below it in a multilevel interconnect. It is made by filling a hole in the insulator with metal. ビア

items.n: Interface states
items.x: Energy levels within the band gap at a semiconductor-insulator interface, created by broken bonds and similar defects. They trap and release carriers, causing threshold shifts, lower mobility and noise. 界面準位

items.n: Intermediate representation
items.x: A form of the program inside a compiler that depends on neither the source language nor the target CPU. Most optimizations operate on it, separating language-specific front ends from CPU-specific back ends. 中間表現

items.n: Internal control
items.x: The mechanisms and procedures built into an organization's operations and carried out by everyone in it in order to achieve the organization's objectives. In the framework of Japan's internal control reporting system (J-SOX), the objectives are effectiveness and efficiency of operations, reliability of reporting, compliance with laws and regulations related to business activities, and safeguarding of assets, and the basic components are the control environment, risk evaluation and response, control activities, information and communication, monitoring, and response to IT. It is based on the U.S. COSO framework. 内部統制

items.n: Interrupt
items.x: A CPU mechanism that temporarily suspends the current task to handle a request, for example from an external device, and then returns to the original task. 割り込み

items.n: Interrupt handler
items.x: The routine a CPU runs when an interrupt or exception occurs. It saves the interrupted state, handles the cause and returns. Handlers should be kept as short as possible. 割り込みハンドラ

items.n: Interrupt vector table
items.x: A table listing, for each type of interrupt or exception, the start address of its handler. The CPU indexes it by the cause number to find where to begin handling. 割り込みベクタテーブル

items.n: Intrinsic carrier density
items.x: The density of thermally generated electrons and holes in an undoped semiconductor, written ni. For silicon it is about 1×10¹⁰ cm⁻³ at room temperature and rises steeply with temperature. In equilibrium, n × p = ni². 真性キャリア密度

items.n: Inversion layer
items.x: A layer formed at the semiconductor surface by the gate voltage, where carriers of the type opposite to the substrate gather. It becomes the MOSFET's channel. 反転層

items.n: IOMMU
items.x: A unit that translates and protects the addresses peripherals use for DMA. It keeps devices from writing to unauthorized memory and is also used when assigning devices to virtual machines. IOMMU

items.n: Ion implantation
items.x: A technique that ionizes impurities, accelerates them and implants them into the wafer. The dose and depth can be controlled precisely. イオン注入

items.n: Ion trap
items.x: A device that holds ions in a vacuum with electric fields or similar means, or the quantum computing approach that uses one. Electronic energy levels of the ions serve as qubits and are controlled with lasers or microwaves. All the qubits are identical, with long coherence times and high fidelities, but gates are slower than in superconducting platforms. イオントラップ

items.n: IPC
items.x: Short for instructions per cycle: the number of instructions executed per clock. It expresses design efficiency; performance is roughly IPC times clock frequency. Its reciprocal is CPI. IPC

items.n: IR drop
items.x: The drop in supply voltage reaching a circuit because current (I) flows through the resistance (R) of the power wiring. It increases delay and can cause malfunctions. IRドロップ
The international standard that defines cleanroom cleanliness classes by the number of airborne particles. The smaller the number, the cleaner. ISO 14644-1

The international standard for automotive functional safety, aimed at reducing risks from failures of electrical and electronic systems to an acceptable level. It adapts IEC 61508 to road vehicles and covers the whole lifecycle from concept through development and production to decommissioning. ISO 26262

items.n: Isochronous transfer
items.x: A USB transfer type that reserves bandwidth and sends at fixed intervals without retrying on error. Used for audio and video. アイソクロナス転送

items.n: Isolation cell
items.x: A cell placed at a boundary that passes a fixed value to running logic even when the outputs of a powered-off block are undefined. アイソレーションセル

items.n: Isolation level
items.x: A setting that determines how far interference between concurrently running transactions is prevented. The SQL standard defines four levels: READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE. Higher levels prevent more of dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantom reads, but reduce the amount of work that can be processed concurrently. 分離レベル

items.n: Isotropic etching
items.x: Etching that proceeds at the same rate vertically and laterally. It cuts in under the mask (undercut). 等方性エッチング

items.n: IT governance
items.x: The system by which management (the board and senior executives) takes responsibility for directing IT investment and use, evaluating its execution and results and monitoring it, so that the use of IT supports the organization's goals and strategy. The international standard ISO/IEC 38500 describes the role of the governing body as Evaluate, Direct and Monitor. Day-to-day operations management and the management of individual projects are management activities carried out under that direction. ITガバナンス

items.n: ITIL
items.x: A set of books that systematically collects good practice (best practice) for IT service management. Work on it began in a UK government agency, and it has been revised many times and is widely referenced around the world. It describes ideas such as service level management, incident management, problem management, change management, configuration management and the service desk, which organizations adapt to their own needs. It is not a standard; for certification, the international standard for IT service management, ISO/IEC 20000, is used. ITIL

items.n: JFET (junction field-effect transistor)
items.x: A field-effect transistor whose gate is a pn junction, controlling channel current through the width of the depletion layer that grows under reverse bias. Most are depletion-mode devices that conduct at a gate voltage of 0 V. JFET(接合型FET)

items.n: JIT compilation
items.x: Compiling frequently executed parts of a program to machine code while it runs, enabling optimizations based on run-time information. Used in runtimes for Java, JavaScript and others. JITコンパイル

items.n: Jitter
items.x: Small fluctuations in the timing of clock or signal edges from their ideal positions. When sampling high-frequency signals, even slight jitter causes large voltage errors. ジッタ

items.n: Josephson junction
items.x: A structure in which two superconductors are separated by a thin insulating film or similar layer about 1–2 nm thick. A superconducting current flows through it without producing a voltage, and it acts as a lossless nonlinear inductor. It is used in superconducting qubits, ultra-sensitive magnetic sensors (SQUIDs), voltage standards and more. For qubits it is usually made of aluminum and its oxide. ジョセフソン接合

items.n: JTAG
items.x: A standard interface for chip testing and debugging that lets developers halt programs, inspect internal values and program flash. Arm also uses SWD, which needs fewer wires. JTAG

items.n: Junction capacitance (depletion capacitance)
items.x: Capacitance arising because the depletion layer of a PN junction acts like a parallel-plate capacitor. It decreases as reverse bias widens the depletion layer; varactor diodes use this property. 接合容量(空乏層容量)

items.n: k-means clustering
items.x: A representative clustering method that divides data into a predetermined number k of clusters. It places k tentative centers, then repeats assigning each data point to the cluster of the nearest center and moving each center to the mean of its cluster's data until the assignments stop changing. It is simple to compute and works on large data, but the result depends on the initial centers, k must be chosen by the user, and clusters that are not roughly spherical are hard to separate. k平均法

items.n: Karnaugh map
items.x: A diagram that arranges a truth table so that adjacent cells differ in one bit. Grouping neighboring 1s lets you simplify a logic expression visually. カルノー図

items.n: Kernel page-table isolation (KPTI)
items.x: An OS countermeasure to Meltdown that removes most kernel memory from the page tables while user programs run. KPTI

items.n: KGD (known good die)
items.x: A chip confirmed to be good before packaging. It matters when several chips go into one package, because a single bad chip ruins the whole module. KGD(ノウングッドダイ)

items.n: Killer defect
items.x: A defect that makes a chip fail, such as particles or pattern anomalies of a size and location that cause shorts or opens in wiring. キラー欠陥

items.n: Knowledge distillation
items.x: Training a small student model to mimic a large teacher model's outputs so the small model achieves similar performance. 知識蒸留

items.n: KV cache
items.x: Memory in LLM inference holding the attention keys and values of already processed tokens. It avoids recomputation but grows with context length and batch size. KVキャッシュ

items.n: Laser anneal
items.x: Heating only the near-surface region of a wafer for an extremely short time with laser light. It achieves high activation with almost no diffusion. レーザーアニール

items.n: Latch-up
items.x: A condition in which a parasitic thyristor structure in a CMOS circuit turns on and a large current keeps flowing between supply and ground. It is prevented by well-contact placement, guard rings and similar measures. ラッチアップ

items.n: Latency hiding
items.x: Keeping waits, such as for memory, from showing up in performance by doing other work in the meantime. GPUs do it by switching among many warps. レイテンシ隠蔽

items.n: Lattice mismatch
items.x: A difference in the atomic spacing (lattice constant) between a grown film and its substrate. A large mismatch causes strain and defects such as dislocations. 格子不整合

items.n: LDD structure
items.x: Short for lightly doped drain. The drain is made lightly doped only at its edge next to the gate, relaxing the electric field and suppressing hot-carrier degradation. LDD構造

items.n: LDO
items.x: Short for low-dropout regulator: a linear regulator that works with only a small difference between input and output voltage. It is low-noise, but the voltage difference times the current is lost as heat. LDO

items.n: Lead frame
items.x: A thin metal sheet combining the pad that holds the chip with the external terminals (leads). It is used in packages such as QFP. リードフレーム

items.n: Leaf function
items.x: A function that calls no other functions. Its return address is never overwritten, so it need not be saved, and it often needs no stack frame at all. 葉関数

items.n: Level shifter
items.x: A circuit that converts signal voltages between blocks running at different supply voltages to suit the receiving side. レベルシフタ

items.n: Lexical analysis
items.x: The first compiler phase, which splits the characters of source code into tokens such as identifiers, numbers, operators and keywords. Whitespace and comments are removed here. 字句解析

items.n: Line edge roughness (LER)
items.x: Nanometer-scale roughness along the edges of fine resist lines. It causes line-width variation (LWR) and leads to variation in transistor characteristics. ラインエッジラフネス(LER)

items.n: Link budget
items.x: A calculation that adds up the gains and losses from transmit power to received power to estimate the power reaching the receiver and the margin over the power needed for reception (the sensitivity). It is done in dB and dBm by adding and subtracting terms such as transmit power + antenna gains − propagation loss − cable loss. The same approach is used for power budgets in optical communication as well as radio. リンクバジェット

items.n: Linked list
items.x: A data structure in which each element holds a value and a pointer to the next element, and the elements are linked by following the pointers. Once the position is known, insertion and deletion are O(1) pointer changes, but reading the i-th element requires walking from the front, O(n). The elements tend to be scattered in memory, so caches work less well than with arrays. 連結リスト

items.n: Linker
items.x: Software that combines object files and libraries, performs symbol resolution and relocation, and produces an executable or shared library. リンカ

items.n: Linker script
items.x: A file telling the linker at which memory addresses to place each section. Embedded development uses it to lay out flash and RAM and to fix the interrupt vector address. リンカスクリプト

items.n: Lint tool
items.x: A tool that checks HDL or other code against rules without simulation, flagging problem-prone constructs such as width mismatches and unintended latches. Lint

items.n: Little's law
items.x: The relationship that the average number in a system equals the arrival rate times the average time each spends there: L = λW. リトルの法則

items.n: LLVM
items.x: A compiler infrastructure built around a common intermediate representation (LLVM IR), combining language front ends, optimization passes and CPU back ends. It is used for many languages and CPUs. LLVM

items.n: Load balancer
items.x: A device or software that distributes users' requests among several servers to spread the load. It checks the state of each server regularly (health checks) and removes failed servers from distribution, so it also serves a redundancy role. Unless it is itself made redundant, the load balancer becomes a single point of failure. ロードバランサ

items.n: Load-reserved/store-conditional (LR/SC)
items.x: A pair of instructions, also called LL/SC: if another core writes the address after the load-reserved, the store-conditional fails, enabling atomic updates. LR/SC

items.n: Load-store architecture
items.x: An ISA style in which only load and store instructions access memory and arithmetic works only on registers. Used by RISC-V and Arm, it gives instructions a uniform shape that is easy to pipeline. ロード・ストア・アーキテクチャ

items.n: Local exhaust ventilation
items.x: Equipment that draws in gases and mists at their source, such as tools handling chemicals, and exhausts them. It keeps workers from inhaling hazardous substances. 局所排気装置

items.n: Lock-free algorithm
items.x: A property of an algorithm that some thread can always make progress even if others stall partway. Built with atomic instructions such as CAS. ロックフリー

items.n: Lockout/tagout (LOTO)
items.x: A procedure that isolates energy sources such as power and gas before maintenance and fits locks and tags so no one can accidentally restore them during the work. ロックアウト・タグアウト(LOTO)

items.n: Lockstep CPU
items.x: A scheme in which two identical CPU cores run the same program and a comparator checks their outputs to detect faults. To keep common-cause faults from corrupting both cores the same way, execution is offset by a few clocks or the cores are placed apart. Performance is that of one core. ロックステップ

items.n: LOCOS
items.x: A method that isolates devices by thickly oxidizing only areas not covered by nitride. It forms a beak-like encroachment at the edges (the bird's beak) and has been replaced by STI. LOCOS

items.n: Logic synthesis
items.x: The design step that converts a circuit described in RTL into a netlist made of gates from a cell library. 論理合成

items.n: Loop blocking
items.x: An optimization that processes large arrays in small blocks that fit in the cache so loaded data is reused many times before eviction. Very effective for matrix multiplication. ループブロッキング

items.n: Loop unrolling
items.x: Replicating a loop body several times to reduce the number of iterations. It cuts branch and counter overhead and gives more freedom to reorder instructions, at the cost of larger code. ループ展開

items.n: Low-k material
items.x: An interlayer dielectric with a low dielectric constant. It lowers the capacitance between wires, reducing signal delay and power consumption. Low-k材料

items.n: Lower explosive limit (LEL)
items.x: The lowest concentration in air at which a flammable gas can burn or explode. Gas detectors are often set to alarm at a percentage of this level. 爆発下限界(LEL)

items.n: LPCVD (low-pressure CVD)
items.x: Thermal CVD performed under reduced pressure. Faster gas diffusion gives good thickness uniformity and step coverage, and many wafers can be processed at once in a vertical furnace. It is used for polysilicon and nitride films. LPCVD(減圧CVD)

items.n: LPDDR
items.x: Short for low-power DDR: a DRAM standard for smartphones and laptops with lower supply voltages and enhanced power-saving features. LPDDR

items.n: LPWA (low-power wide-area)
items.x: A general term for wireless communication intended to send small amounts of data, such as sensor readings, from devices that run on batteries for years to places several kilometers or more away. Keeping the transmission rate low allows even weak signals to be received, extending the range. Some, such as LoRaWAN, use license-exempt bands (such as the 920 MHz band in Japan), while others, such as LTE-M and NB-IoT, use mobile phone bands. LPWA(Low Power Wide Area)

items.n: LRU replacement
items.x: A cache replacement policy that evicts the least recently used data. It exploits temporal locality well, but exact tracking is costly with many ways, so approximations are used. LRU(Least Recently Used)

items.n: LVS
items.x: Short for layout versus schematic: checking that the connectivity extracted from the layout matches the schematic or netlist. It is always run before tape-out, along with DRC. LVS

items.n: MAC address
items.x: The 48-bit address used in Ethernet and wireless LAN to identify devices within the same network. The upper 24 bits identify the manufacturer, and it is assigned to each interface at manufacture. MACアドレス

items.n: Mach-Zehnder modulator
items.x: A modulator that splits incoming light into two arms, shifts the phase between them by changing the arms' refractive index with an electrical signal, and recombines them to turn the phase change into an intensity change. A phase difference of 0 gives maximum brightness and π gives minimum. Silicon versions use the plasma dispersion effect and are a few mm long. マッハツェンダー変調器

items.n: Machine epsilon
items.x: The difference between 1 and the next larger representable floating-point number, a measure of relative precision: 2⁻²³ (about 1.19 × 10⁻⁷) in single precision and 2⁻⁵² (about 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶) in double. マシンイプシロン

items.n: Magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ)
items.x: A structure with a thin insulating film between two magnetic layers. Resistance is low when the layers' magnetizations are parallel and high when antiparallel. It is the storage element of MRAM. 磁気トンネル接合(MTJ)

items.n: Magnetron sputtering
items.x: Sputtering with magnets behind the target that trap electrons near it and raise plasma density. It increases deposition rate and is the mainstream sputtering method today. マグネトロンスパッタリング

items.n: Mass flow controller (MFC)
items.x: A device in deposition and etch tools that precisely measures the mass flow of a gas and holds it at a set value. マスフローコントローラ(MFC)

items.n: MBE (molecular beam epitaxy)
items.x: Epitaxial growth in ultra-high vacuum by supplying source materials to the substrate as molecular beams. It controls thickness and composition at the atomic-layer level and is used in compound-semiconductor research and quantum structures. MBE(分子線エピタキシー)

items.n: MCZ method (magnetic-field-applied CZ)
items.x: A CZ variant that applies a magnetic field to the crucible to suppress melt convection. It makes the oxygen concentration in the crystal easier to control and is used for large-diameter crystals. MCZ法(磁場印加CZ法)

items.n: Mealy machine
items.x: A state machine whose outputs depend on both the current state and the inputs. Input changes reach outputs within the same cycle, but so can input glitches. A Moore machine's outputs depend only on state. ミーリ型

items.n: Measured boot
items.x: A mechanism that cumulatively records hashes of each boot stage's software in a TPM or similar so the boot state can be verified later. 測定ブート

items.n: Median
items.x: The value in the middle when data are sorted by size. When there is an even number of values, it is the average of the two middle values. Unlike the mean, it is little affected by values far from the rest (outliers), so it suits as the representative value of data that include some extreme values, such as response times or incomes. Half of the data are at or below it and half at or above it, and it corresponds to the second quartile. The most frequent value is called the mode. 中央値

items.n: Megasonic cleaning
items.x: A cleaning method that applies ultrasound of about 1 MHz to the cleaning solution to remove fine particles from wafer surfaces. メガソニック洗浄

items.n: Meltdown
items.x: A vulnerability in some CPUs where kernel memory could be read speculatively before the permission exception took effect, with values inferred from cache traces. Mitigated by KPTI and other measures. Meltdown

items.n: Memory barrier
items.x: An instruction guaranteeing that memory operations before it become visible to other cores before those after it, also called a fence, such as RISC-V fence. メモリバリア

items.n: Memory coalescing
items.x: Combining accesses into a few memory transactions when adjacent threads in a warp access adjacent addresses. メモリコアレッシング

items.n: Memory consistency model
items.x: The contract specifying in what order a core's reads and writes to multiple addresses may be observed by other cores. Examples include sequential consistency, x86 TSO and the weak models of Arm and RISC-V. メモリ一貫性モデル

items.n: Memory fragmentation
items.x: The condition in which repeated allocation and release split free memory into small pieces, so a large contiguous block cannot be allocated even though the total is sufficient. 断片化

items.n: Memory wall
items.x: The problem that memory bandwidth and latency improve more slowly than processor performance, limiting overall performance. HBM, larger caches and advanced packaging are used to address it. メモリウォール

items.n: Memory-mapped I/O
items.x: Assigning peripheral registers to specific addresses in the same address space as memory and accessing them with ordinary load and store instructions. That region is configured as uncached. メモリマップドI/O

items.n: MEMS
items.x: Micro-electro-mechanical systems. Devices that integrate tiny mechanical structures and electronic circuits using semiconductor microfabrication. MEMS

items.n: MESI protocol
items.x: A coherence protocol that tracks each cache line in one of four states: Modified, Exclusive, Shared or Invalid. On a write it invalidates other cores' copies. MESIプロトコル

items.n: Message authentication code
items.x: A short value (MAC) computed from a message and a symmetric key shared by the sender and receiver. By recomputing it with the same key and comparing, the receiver can confirm that the message came from someone who knows the key and was not altered. Because the receiver can also create the same value, it cannot provide non-repudiation. HMAC is a typical example. メッセージ認証コード

items.n: Message-signaled interrupts (MSI)
items.x: A scheme in which a device signals an interrupt by writing to a designated address. It needs no dedicated interrupt wire and lets one device have many interrupts. MSI(メッセージシグナル割り込み)

items.n: Metastability
items.x: A state in which a flip-flop's output stays between 0 and 1 for a while when setup or hold time is violated. Asynchronous signals are passed through two flip-flops (a synchronizer) to guard against it. メタステーブル

items.n: Micro-operation
items.x: A simple internal operation into which a CPU decodes an instruction, also written μop. x86 CPUs split complex instructions into μops and execute them with RISC-like fast techniques. マイクロオペレーション

items.n: Microbenchmark
items.x: A benchmark timing a tiny isolated operation; beware pitfalls such as the compiler optimizing the computation away. マイクロベンチマーク

items.n: Microbump
items.x: A bump far smaller than an ordinary solder ball, used to connect TSV-stacked chips or chips to an interposer. The pitch is a few tens of micrometers. マイクロバンプ

items.n: Microcontroller (MCU)
items.x: A small computer that integrates a CPU, memory and peripherals such as timers and ADCs on one chip. It is embedded in appliances, cars and other equipment to control them. Also called an MCU. マイコン(マイクロコントローラ)

items.n: Microlens
items.x: A tiny lens placed over each pixel of an image sensor. It gathers light and directs it efficiently onto the photodiode, raising sensitivity. マイクロレンズ

items.n: Miller effect
items.x: The effect by which a capacitance between the input and output of an inverting amplifier appears (1 + gain) times larger from the input. It degrades the high-frequency response of common-emitter and common-source stages. ミラー効果

items.n: MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output)
items.x: A wireless technique that uses multiple antennas at both the transmitter and the receiver. It raises the transmission rate through spatial multiplexing, sending different data on the same frequency at the same time, or raises reliability through diversity, sending the same data over several paths. The number of streams that spatial multiplexing can send is limited by the smaller of the numbers of transmit and receive antennas. MIMO(多入力多出力)

items.n: Mini-environment
items.x: Keeping only the small space around the wafers highly clean. Sealed carriers such as FOUPs combined with EFEMs on the tools lower the cleanliness required of the room as a whole, reducing cost. ミニエンバイロメント

items.n: Misfit dislocation
items.x: A dislocation at the interface between crystals with different lattice constants that relieves strain. It forms when the grown layer exceeds the critical thickness. ミスフィット転位

items.n: Miss penalty
items.x: The extra time needed to fetch data from the next level when a cache miss occurs, determined by the lower level's access time and the line transfer time. ミスペナルティ

items.n: Missing code
items.x: A defect in which an ADC never outputs a particular code no matter how the input varies. It occurs when DNL reaches −1 LSB. ミッシングコード

items.n: Mixed precision
items.x: Using different numeric precisions for different parts of a computation, such as multiplying in FP16 and accumulating in FP32, to balance speed and accuracy. 混合精度

items.n: MMIC
items.x: Short for monolithic microwave integrated circuit: a high-frequency IC that integrates transistors together with passive components such as inductors and capacitors on a substrate such as GaAs. MMIC

items.n: Mobile ions
items.x: Ions such as sodium and potassium that can move within the gate oxide. They drift with field and temperature and shift the threshold voltage. Because they can come from sources such as human sweat, they are tightly controlled. 可動イオン

items.n: Mobility
items.x: How easily carriers move when an electric field is applied. In silicon, electron mobility is higher than hole mobility. 移動度

items.n: MOCVD (metal-organic chemical vapor deposition)
items.x: A method that grows crystals using metal-organic compounds and source gases such as ammonia. It is widely used to grow compound semiconductors such as GaN and GaAs. MOCVD(有機金属気相成長)

items.n: Model FLOPs utilization (MFU)
items.x: The percentage of hardware peak performance achieved, computed from the operations a model actually requires. MFU

items.n: Modulo operation
items.x: An operation that gives the remainder of a division, written mod in the pseudo-language and % in many languages. x mod 10 gives the ones digit, x mod 2 tells whether x is even or odd, and i mod n + 1 gives an index that cycles through 1 to n. The sign of the remainder for negative numbers differs between languages. 剰余演算

items.n: MOL (middle of line)
items.x: The contacts and local interconnects that link transistors (FEOL) to the multilevel wiring (BEOL). With scaling, their resistance has grown and now limits performance. MOL(ミドル・オブ・ライン)

items.n: Monitor wafer
items.x: A wafer run through a process separately from products to check equipment or measure film thickness and particles. Also called a test wafer, it is often stripped, repolished and reused as a reclaimed wafer. モニターウエハ

items.n: Monolithic 3D integration
items.x: Three-dimensional integration in which transistor layers are built one after another on a single wafer. Layers can be connected far more finely than by bonding finished chips, but the upper layers must be made at low temperature. Also called sequential 3D integration. モノリシック3D集積

items.n: Moore's law
items.x: The empirical rule that the number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles about every two years. It has served as a target for semiconductor scaling. ムーアの法則

items.n: MPW (multi-project wafer)
items.x: Prototyping several customers' designs together on one wafer (one mask set). Sharing the expensive mask cost makes it popular with universities and startups. MPW(マルチプロジェクトウエハ)

items.n: MRAM
items.x: Non-volatile memory that stores data as the difference in resistance caused by the magnetization direction of a magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ). MRAM

items.n: MSL (moisture sensitivity level)
items.x: A rating of how readily a surface-mount part absorbs moisture, defined by JEDEC's J-STD-020. It sets the floor life allowed between opening the moisture barrier bag and reflow: 168 hours at or below 30 °C/60% RH for MSL 3. Parts past their floor life are baked dry before mounting. MSL(吸湿感度レベル)

items.n: MTBF (mean time between failures)
items.x: The average interval between failures. For a synchronizer it is the average time between metastable events that fail to resolve and propagate onward, given by MTBF = e^(t_r/τ) ÷ (T_0 × f_clk × f_data). Adding stages lengthens the resolution time t_r and increases it exponentially. MTBF(平均故障間隔)

items.n: MTTF (mean time to failure)
items.x: The average time until a non-repairable product fails. It is used as an indicator of product lifetime. MTTF(平均故障時間)

items.n: MTTR (mean time to repair)
items.x: The average time it takes to repair a failed system or device and return it to a usable state (Mean Time To Repair). It includes the time to detect the failure, isolate the cause, replace parts or fix the settings, and verify the result. Availability is expressed as MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR), so the shorter the MTTR, the higher the availability. It is shortened by monitoring that detects failures quickly, spare parts on hand, well-prepared procedures and automatic failover. MTTR(平均修復時間)

items.n: Multi-factor authentication
items.x: Authentication that verifies a person by combining two or more different factors among knowledge (such as a password), possession (such as a smartphone or smart card) and inherence (such as a fingerprint or face). Even if the password leaks, logging in is impossible without the other factors. Also called MFA. 多要素認証

items.n: Multicycle path
items.x: A timing exception telling STA that a path may take several clock cycles to transfer data. When setup is set to N cycles, hold is usually set to N − 1 to move the hold check edge back to its original position. マルチサイクルパス

items.n: Multilevel interconnect
items.x: A structure that stacks many wiring layers separated by insulating films and connects them vertically with vias. Leading-edge ICs have more than ten layers. 多層配線

items.n: Multiple patterning
items.x: Forming patterns with a pitch too fine for a single exposure by splitting them across several exposures or process steps. Splitting into two is double patterning. マルチパターニング

items.n: Multiplexer
items.x: A circuit that selects one of several inputs according to select signals and passes it to the output. The reverse, routing one input to one of several outputs, is a demultiplexer. マルチプレクサ

items.n: Mutex
items.x: A lock that only one thread can hold at a time. Typically a thread that cannot get it sleeps and yields the CPU, and the OS wakes it when the lock is released. ミューテックス

items.n: Name mangling
items.x: A C++ compiler's encoding of argument types and namespaces into a function's symbol name, so the linker can tell overloaded functions apart. 名前修飾

items.n: NaN
items.x: Short for Not a Number, a floating-point special value produced by operations with no numeric result, such as 0 ÷ 0 or the square root of a negative number. It has an all-ones exponent and a nonzero significand, and compares unequal even to itself. NaN

items.n: NAND flash memory
items.x: Non-volatile memory in which memory cells are connected in series. It is dense and easy to scale to large capacities, and is used in SSDs and memory cards. NAND型フラッシュメモリ

items.n: Nanoimprint lithography
items.x: Transferring patterns by pressing a mold with fine features into resist on the wafer. It can make fine patterns without expensive optics. ナノインプリントリソグラフィ

items.n: Nanosheet
items.x: A GAA transistor structure that stacks several thin, plate-like silicon channels vertically, each surrounded by the gate. Current can be tuned by the sheet width. ナノシート

items.n: NAT (Network Address Translation)
items.x: A technique that rewrites the IP addresses of packets passing through a router. The variant that also rewrites port numbers so many devices can share one global address is called NAPT (IP masquerading). NAT

items.n: Native oxide
items.x: A thin oxide about 1 nm thick that forms naturally when silicon is exposed to air or water. Because it raises contact resistance and disturbs epitaxial growth, it is removed right before such steps. 自然酸化膜

items.n: NBTI (negative bias temperature instability)
items.x: A degradation phenomenon in which the magnitude of a pMOS threshold voltage gradually increases under negative gate voltage at high temperature. NBTI

items.n: Near-threshold computing
items.x: Operating with supply voltage near the transistor threshold, greatly cutting energy per operation at the cost of speed and greater sensitivity to variation. ニアスレッショルド動作

items.n: Necking
items.x: Growing a thin neck just after the seed at the start of CZ pulling. It lets dislocations created by thermal shock when the seed touches the melt escape, giving a dislocation-free crystal. ネッキング

items.n: Negative feedback
items.x: Returning part of the output to the input with opposite polarity. Gain drops, but it becomes stable, and distortion and bandwidth improve. 負帰還

items.n: Nested paging
items.x: Hardware that walks two levels of page tables in succession, one managed by the guest OS and one by the hypervisor. It reduces hypervisor intervention and speeds up virtualization. 入れ子ページング

items.n: Net present value (NPV)
items.x: The sum of the future cash flows from an investment converted to present value using a discount rate, minus the amount invested. If it is greater than zero, the investment is judged worthwhile at that discount rate. 正味現在価値(NPV)

items.n: Netlist
items.x: Data describing the elements (cells) of a circuit and how they are connected. It is the output of logic synthesis and the input to place-and-route and timing analysis. ネットリスト

items.n: Network-on-chip (NoC)
items.x: An on-chip interconnect of routers and links arranged as a network that carries data as packets, moving many transfers between blocks simultaneously. ネットワークオンチップ

items.n: Neuromorphic computing
items.x: Computing that imitates neurons and synapses in the brain, exchanging information as pulses called spikes and computing only when something changes. It places memory close to computation and aims for low power. ニューロモーフィックコンピューティング

items.n: NF3 (nitrogen trifluoride)
items.x: A gas used for cleaning CVD chambers and the like. Its global warming potential is high, so emission reduction is required. NF3(三フッ化窒素)

items.n: NFC (near-field communication)
items.x: Wireless communication over distances of a few centimeters to about 10 cm using electromagnetic induction by a 13.56 MHz magnetic field. The card receives power from the reader's magnetic field, so it needs no battery. It is used in transit IC cards, contactless payments, data exchange between smartphones and more, and FeliCa, widespread in Japan, also uses the same 13.56 MHz. NFC(Near Field Communication)

items.n: NISQ
items.x: Short for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum: intermediate-scale quantum computers with noise (errors) that do not perform full-scale error correction. The term was proposed by John Preskill in 2018. Because the depth of circuit they can run is limited by gate error rates, error mitigation and methods that combine quantum and classical computation are being studied. NISQ

items.n: Noise figure (NF)
items.x: A measure of how much a circuit such as an amplifier or receiver degrades the signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) through its own noise. The input S/N divided by the output S/N (the noise factor), expressed in dB, is called the noise figure (NF). It is defined with thermal noise at 290 K as the reference. The value for cascaded circuits is found with Friis's formula and is set mainly by the first stage's noise figure and gain. 雑音指数(NF)

items.n: Noise margin
items.x: The difference between the voltage level an output guarantees and the level an input is guaranteed to interpret correctly. The low-level margin is VIL(max) − VOL(max) and the high-level margin is VOH(min) − VIH(min); noise smaller than this causes no misreading. ノイズマージン

items.n: Noise shaping
items.x: A technique that uses a feedback loop to push quantization noise toward high frequencies, lowering noise in the signal band. Delta-sigma ADCs combine it with oversampling to achieve high resolution. ノイズシェーピング

items.n: Non-blocking cache
