items.x: A cache that keeps servicing other accesses while a miss is outstanding. It can handle multiple misses at once, overlapping and hiding memory latency. ノンブロッキングキャッシュ

items.n: Non-maskable interrupt
items.x: An interrupt that is always accepted regardless of interrupt masking. It is used to report uncorrectable memory errors, serious hardware faults and watchdog events. NMI(マスク不可能割り込み)

items.n: Non-uniform memory access (NUMA)
items.x: An organization in which each core has near and far memory, and far accesses take longer. Placing data and threads on the same side is faster. NUMA

items.n: Nonblocking assignment
items.x: Verilog's "<=" assignment, which evaluates every right-hand side at a time step before updating all left-hand sides together. It matches flip-flop behavior and is used for sequential logic. ノンブロッキング代入

items.n: Nonvolatile memory
items.x: Memory that retains stored data when power is removed, such as flash memory and MRAM. DRAM and SRAM are volatile. 不揮発性メモリ

items.n: NOR flash memory
items.x: Flash memory with cells connected in parallel. Random reads are fast, and it is used to store programs for microcontrollers and the like. NOR型フラッシュメモリ

items.n: Normal distribution
items.x: A continuous probability distribution with a symmetric bell shape centered on the mean μ, whose shape is determined by the mean μ and the standard deviation σ. It is also called the Gaussian distribution. About 68% lies within the mean ±1σ, about 95% within ±2σ and about 99.7% within ±3σ. A quantity formed by adding many small independent factors approaches a normal distribution (the central limit theorem), so it is widely used as a model of measurement errors and manufacturing variation. Standardizing with z = (x − μ) ÷ σ gives the standard normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. 正規分布

items.n: Normalization
items.x: A design procedure that splits relational database tables based on functional dependencies between columns so that the same fact is not recorded in several places. It removes duplicated data and prevents update, insertion and deletion anomalies. Its stages include first to third normal form and Boyce-Codd normal form. 正規化

items.n: Normally-off
items.x: The property of passing no current when the gate voltage is 0 V. It is required of power devices for safety, since current stops even if the drive circuit fails. ノーマリーオフ

items.n: NoSQL
items.x: A collective term for databases other than relational databases, including key-value, document, column-oriented and graph types. Many products are easy to scale out across multiple servers and allow flexible data formats, but they are often poor at complex queries such as table joins and at strict consistency. NoSQL

items.n: Notch
items.x: A small cut in a wafer's edge that indicates its crystal orientation. Used on 200 mm and larger wafers; smaller wafers used an orientation flat (a straight edge) instead. ウエハのノッチ

items.n: NPU (neural processing unit)
items.x: A dedicated circuit for running neural-network inference quickly and at low power. It is built into the SoCs of smartphones and PCs. NPU(ニューラルプロセッシングユニット)

items.n: NRZ
items.x: Non-return-to-zero: the most basic signaling scheme, sending 1 bit per symbol with two voltage levels. NRZ

items.n: Numerical aperture (NA)
items.x: A value that expresses the range of angles of light a lens can collect. A larger NA gives higher resolution. 開口数(NA)

items.n: NVMe
items.x: An interface standard for fast access to SSDs connected over PCI Express. It processes many commands in parallel and has lower latency than SATA, which was designed for HDDs. NVMe

items.n: Nyquist frequency
items.x: Half the sampling frequency. Components above it are folded back to lower frequencies when sampled (aliasing). ナイキスト周波数

items.n: O-band
items.x: The optical fiber communication band around 1260 to 1360 nm. It includes the region near 1.31 µm where chromatic dispersion in standard single-mode fiber is nearly zero, and is widely used for short links such as those inside data centers. Oバンド

items.n: Object file
items.x: The file a compiler produces from one source file. It contains machine code, initial data, a symbol table and relocation entries, but addresses in other files are unresolved, so it cannot run until linked. オブジェクトファイル

items.n: Object-oriented programming
items.x: An approach that builds programs from objects, each bundling data with the procedures (methods) that operate on it. The blueprint for objects is called a class, each object created from a class is called an instance, and each instance has its own values of the member variables. オブジェクト指向

items.n: OCV (on-chip variation)
items.x: Variation in transistor and wire delay from place to place within a single chip. STA applies separate factors to launch and capture paths (for example 1.1× and 0.9×) to analyze the most pessimistic combination. OCV(オンチップばらつき)

items.n: OFDM (orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing)
items.x: A scheme that splits data across many mutually orthogonal subcarriers, modulates each at a low symbol rate and sends them in parallel. Setting the subcarrier spacing to the reciprocal of the symbol length lets the subcarriers be separated without interfering even though their spectra overlap. It is robust against multipath and is used in wireless LANs, 4G LTE, 5G NR, digital terrestrial broadcasting and more. OFDM(直交周波数分割多重)

items.n: Off-by-one error
items.x: A mistake in which a loop count or an array range is off by exactly one. It arises from whether the final value is included, whether indices start at 0 or 1, and confusing the number of intervals with the number of points (the fence-post problem). Tracing with the boundary values makes it easier to find. オフバイワンエラー

items.n: Ohmic contact
items.x: A metal-semiconductor contact with low resistance in both directions and a linear current-voltage relation. It is made by heavily doping the semiconductor surface so carriers can tunnel through the barrier. オーミック接触

items.n: OHT (overhead hoist transport)
items.x: Vehicles that run along ceiling rails and automatically carry FOUPs between tools. They are the backbone of automated transport in 300 mm fabs. OHT(天井走行式無人搬送車)

items.n: On-resistance
items.x: The resistance of the current path when a power device is on. The smaller it is, the lower the conduction loss. オン抵抗

items.n: One-hot encoding
items.x: State encoding that assigns one flip-flop per state with exactly one set at a time. Logic tends to be simple and fast, and it is common on FPGAs. ワンホット符号化

items.n: ONNX
items.x: Open Neural Network Exchange: a common model format for exchanging models between frameworks and inference runtimes. ONNX

items.n: OPC (optical proximity correction)
items.x: A technique that corrects mask patterns in advance, anticipating distortion of the printed pattern caused by diffraction of light and similar effects. OPC(光学近接効果補正)

items.n: Open-drain output
items.x: An output that brings out only the drain of the output transistor, actively driving only the low level. The high level comes from an external pull-up resistor, so several outputs can share one line or connect to circuits on a different supply voltage. It is used on I2C buses, for example. オープンドレイン

items.n: OpenCL
items.x: A standard parallel-programming framework for GPUs, CPUs, FPGAs and more from multiple vendors, defined by the Khronos Group industry consortium. OpenCL

items.n: Operational amplifier (op-amp)
items.x: An amplifier with differential inputs and very high gain. Used with negative feedback in amplifiers, filters and more. オペアンプ

items.n: Operator fusion
items.x: An optimization that combines several operations into one kernel, avoiding writing intermediate results to memory and reading them back. 演算の融合

items.n: OSAT
items.x: A company that provides back-end services such as semiconductor assembly and testing under contract. OSAT

items.n: OSI reference model
items.x: A model that organizes communication functions into seven layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation and application. It serves as a common vocabulary for thinking about each layer's role separately. OSI参照モデル

items.n: Out-of-order execution
items.x: Executing instructions as soon as their dependencies allow, in a different order from the program, to improve performance. Results are committed in program order through a reorder buffer. アウトオブオーダー実行

items.n: Over-the-air update
items.x: Updating a device's firmware via wireless communication, often using two flash slots so the device can still boot if an update fails. OTA更新

items.n: Overetch
items.x: Continuing to etch for a set time after endpoint so the film is removed everywhere on the wafer. It is done under conditions with high selectivity to the underlying layer. オーバーエッチング

items.n: Overfitting
items.x: A state in which a model memorizes fine details and chance noise in the training data, so that its error on the training data is small but its error on new data (generalization error) is large. It tends to occur when a complex model with many parameters is trained on little data. It is reduced by adding data, simplifying the model, regularization, dropout, early stopping and similar methods. 過学習

items.n: Overlay
items.x: How accurately a new pattern is placed relative to the patterns made in earlier steps. Misalignment causes defects such as missed contacts, so it is controlled at the nanometer level. オーバーレイ(重ね合わせ精度)

items.n: Oversampling
items.x: Sampling at a rate well above what the signal requires (twice its bandwidth). It spreads quantization noise over a wider band and reduces noise in the signal band; it is the basis of delta-sigma ADCs. オーバーサンプリング

items.n: Oxidation-enhanced diffusion (OED)
items.x: Faster diffusion of boron and phosphorus during oxidation than without it, caused by silicon interstitials injected into the silicon by the oxidation. 酸化増速拡散(OED)

items.n: Oxygen deficiency
items.x: A condition in which the oxygen concentration in air falls below 18%. It tends to occur where large amounts of nitrogen are used or in confined spaces, and can cause unconsciousness within a few breaths. 酸素欠乏(酸欠)

items.n: Oxygen precipitates (BMD)
items.x: Tiny defects formed inside a CZ silicon wafer when its oxygen precipitates during heat treatment. Also called BMDs (bulk micro defects), they serve as gettering sites that capture metal impurities. 酸素析出物(BMD)

items.n: Oxynitride (SiON)
items.x: Gate oxide with nitrogen incorporated. It blocks boron penetration from the gate electrode and has a slightly higher permittivity, so it was used as the gate insulator before high-k films. 酸窒化膜(SiON)

items.n: P-state
items.x: Performance levels of a running CPU defined by frequency and voltage combinations, switched by DVFS to match load. P-state

items.n: Pad conditioning
items.x: Abrading the surface of a CMP polishing pad with a diamond tool to restore its texture and slurry-holding ability, stabilizing the removal rate. Also called dressing. パッドコンディショニング

items.n: Page fault
items.x: An exception raised when an accessed page is not mapped to physical memory or the access type is not permitted. The OS either supplies the page and retries the instruction or treats it as an illegal access. ページフォルト

items.n: Page table
items.x: A table recording the mapping from virtual page numbers to physical page numbers. The OS builds one per process, and the CPU's MMU walks it to translate addresses. Each entry also holds protection bits. ページテーブル

items.n: PAM4
items.x: Four-level pulse amplitude modulation, sending 2 bits per symbol. It doubles the bit rate at the same symbol rate but reduces noise margin. PAM4

items.n: Panel-level packaging (PLP)
items.x: A method that manufactures many packages at once on a large rectangular panel instead of a round wafer. It uses area efficiently and can lower cost, but warpage, die shift over large areas and equipment standardization are challenges. パネルレベルパッケージ(PLP)

items.n: Parallel efficiency
items.x: Parallel speedup divided by the number of processors, indicating how effectively the cores are used. 並列効率

items.n: Parallel reduction
items.x: Computing a sum or similar over many values in parallel with a tree that repeatedly combines neighbors, finishing n values in log2 n stages. 並列リダクション

items.n: Pareto chart
items.x: A chart that lists items such as defect types as bars in descending order of count, with a line for the cumulative share. It shows which items to tackle first. パレート図

items.n: Passivation layer
items.x: A film formed as the topmost layer of a chip to protect the circuitry from moisture, contamination and mechanical damage. Silicon nitride and polyimide are typical materials. パッシベーション膜

items.n: Patent
items.x: A right that protects a technical idea (an invention). It arises when an application is filed with the patent office, examined and registered, and in principle gives the exclusive right to work the invention for 20 years from filing. In exchange, the content of the invention is published. 特許

items.n: Pattern collapse
items.x: A defect in which tall, fine patterns topple or stick together during cleaning and drying because of the surface tension of liquid left between them. パターン倒壊

items.n: PC-relative addressing
items.x: Specifying a branch target or data address as a distance from the current instruction's address (PC). The distance is unchanged wherever the program is loaded, so it underpins position-independent code. PC相対アドレッシング

items.n: PCI Express
items.x: A high-speed serial expansion interface connecting the CPU with GPUs, SSDs, network cards and more, also written PCIe. Lanes are bundled for bandwidth, and speed roughly doubles each generation. PCI Express

items.n: PCM (phase-change memory)
items.x: Nonvolatile memory that stores information by the difference between the crystalline (low-resistance) and amorphous (high-resistance) states of a chalcogenide material. PCM(相変化メモリ)

items.n: PDK (process design kit)
items.x: The set of design data a foundry gives to designers, including design rules, device models, cell libraries and verification rule decks. PDK(プロセスデザインキット)

items.n: PECVD (plasma-enhanced CVD)
items.x: CVD that decomposes source gases with plasma to deposit films. It can deposit at lower temperatures than thermal CVD and is used for insulating films in interconnect steps and the like. PECVD(プラズマCVD)

items.n: Pellicle
items.x: A thin membrane stretched a short distance above a photomask. It keeps particles off the mask surface, and particles landing on the pellicle are out of focus and do not print. ペリクル

items.n: Perfluorocarbons
items.x: Also called PFCs. Fluorinated gases such as CF4 and C2F6 used in etching and chamber cleaning. Their greenhouse effect is very large. パーフルオロカーボン

items.n: Performance counter
items.x: A hardware counter in the CPU that tallies events such as instructions executed, cache misses and branch mispredictions. 性能カウンタ

items.n: Permutations and combinations
items.x: Ways of counting the number of cases when some items are chosen from a set. A permutation distinguishes the order of the chosen items: the number of ways to choose and arrange r of n items is nPr = n!/(n − r)!. A combination ignores the order: nCr = n!/(r!(n − r)!) = nPr/r!. With repetition allowed, there are nʳ arrangements. They are the basis of probability calculations and are also used to estimate the total number of PINs or the number of test combinations. 順列と組合せ

items.n: Phase margin
items.x: How far the phase lag is from 180° at the frequency where the feedback loop gain is 1 (0 dB). A small margin causes ringing, and zero or negative margin causes oscillation; 45-60° or more is a common target. 位相余裕(フェーズマージン)

items.n: Phase-shift mask
items.x: A photomask that shifts the phase of light passing through neighboring openings, using interference to improve image contrast and resolution. 位相シフトマスク

items.n: Phishing
items.x: A fraud technique that lures people to fake websites through emails, text messages and the like posing as real companies or organizations, and gets them to enter IDs, passwords, credit card numbers and so on, which are then stolen. フィッシング

items.n: Phosphine (PH3)
items.x: A gas compound of phosphorus and hydrogen used to introduce n-type dopant (phosphorus) into silicon. It is extremely toxic. ホスフィン(PH3)

items.n: Photodiode
items.x: A diode that generates charge (current) when it receives light. Used as the light-receiving element in image sensor pixels. フォトダイオード

items.n: Photomask (reticle)
items.x: The master pattern used for exposure, typically a light-blocking pattern on a quartz substrate (reflective for EUV). For reduction scanners it is made four times larger than the pattern on the wafer. フォトマスク(レチクル)

items.n: Photonics-electronics convergence
items.x: Technologies and the approach of integrating optical and electronic circuits very close together or as one unit, replacing electrical wiring with light. The aim is to cut power by extending optical links from between equipment to between boards and between chips. The Japanese term (kōden yūgō) is widely used in Japan. 光電融合

items.n: Photoresist
items.x: A light-sensitive material whose solubility in developer changes when exposed. In positive resist the exposed areas dissolve; in negative resist they remain. フォトレジスト

items.n: Physically unclonable function (PUF)
items.x: A mechanism using per-chip manufacturing variation to produce values unique to each chip and hard to clone, allowing keys to be regenerated without storing them. PUF(物理的複製困難関数)

items.n: Piezoresistive effect
items.x: The change in a material's electrical resistivity under mechanical stress. It is especially large in silicon and is used in semiconductor pressure sensors and similar devices. ピエゾ抵抗効果

items.n: Pinned memory
items.x: Memory locked so the OS will not move or evict its physical pages. The GPU can access it directly by DMA, speeding transfers and enabling asynchronous copies. ピン留めメモリ

items.n: Pinned photodiode
items.x: A photodiode with a heavily doped p+ layer at the surface that keeps the collection region away from the interface. It suppresses dark current from interface states and allows complete charge transfer; it is standard in CMOS image sensors. 埋め込みフォトダイオード(ピンドフォトダイオード)

items.n: Pipeline parallelism
items.x: Splitting a model's layers across GPUs in sequence, streaming micro-batches to reduce the time GPUs sit idle (the bubble). パイプライン並列

items.n: Pipelined ADC
items.x: An ADC that splits conversion into stages, each resolving a few bits and passing the residue to the next, like an assembly line. It combines high speed with medium to high resolution. パイプライン型ADC

items.n: Pipelining
items.x: A method that splits instruction processing into stages such as fetch, decode and execute, and processes several instructions at once, each offset by a stage. パイプライン処理

items.n: Place and route
items.x: The design step that arranges cells on the chip (placement) from the netlist produced by logic synthesis and determines the wiring between them (routing). 配置配線

items.n: Plasma
items.x: A state in which a gas is ionized into a mixture of electrons, ions and radicals (reactive neutrals). It is used in many processes, including dry etching, plasma CVD and ashing. プラズマ

items.n: Plasma dispersion effect
items.x: The change in refractive index and optical absorption of a semiconductor when its free electron or hole concentration changes. Because silicon has almost no Pockels effect, this effect is used to shift phase in silicon modulators. Increasing the carrier concentration lowers the refractive index. キャリア分散効果(プラズマ分散効果)

items.n: Plasma doping
items.x: Implanting low-energy ions by exposing the wafer directly to a plasma containing the dopant. It delivers high doses quickly and dopes 3D structures such as fins fairly uniformly. プラズマドーピング

items.n: PLL (phase-locked loop)
items.x: A circuit that detects the phase difference from a reference clock and controls an oscillator to produce a clock locked to the reference, for example at an integer multiple of its frequency. It is used to generate CPU clocks and synthesize radio frequencies. PLL(位相同期回路)

items.n: Poisson distribution
items.x: The probability distribution of the number of times a rare event that occurs independently happens within a fixed time or area. With mean λ, the probability of k occurrences is λᵏ × e^(−λ) ÷ k!, and both the mean and the variance are λ. It is used to model the number of requests arriving at a server, the number of inquiries to a service desk, the number of defects on a wafer and the number of photons. The probability of zero defects, e^(−λ), corresponds to the Poisson yield model. When the number of arrivals follows a Poisson distribution, the intervals between arrivals follow an exponential distribution. ポアソン分布

items.n: Poisson yield model
items.x: A model that assumes defects are randomly distributed and expresses yield as Y = exp(−D×A), where D is defect density and A is chip area. ポアソン歩留まりモデル

items.n: Polling
items.x: A method in which the CPU repeatedly checks a peripheral's status to detect changes. Simple, but it consumes time and power even when nothing happens. ポーリング

items.n: Port number
items.x: A number from 0 to 65535 used by TCP and UDP to identify which application on a host the traffic is for. Ports 0–1023, such as 80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS and 53 for DNS, are called well-known ports. ポート番号

items.n: Position-independent code
items.x: Machine code that runs without modification at any load address, also called PIC. It uses PC-relative references and the GOT and is used for shared libraries and PIEs. 位置独立コード

items.n: Position-independent executable
items.x: An executable whose main program is also built as position-independent code. It runs at any address, so ASLR can randomize the main program's code too. PIE(位置独立実行ファイル)

items.n: Positive photoresist
items.x: A photoresist whose exposed areas dissolve and are removed during development. One whose exposed areas remain is a negative resist. ポジ型フォトレジスト

items.n: Post-quantum cryptography
items.x: Cryptography that bases its security on mathematical problems believed to be hard to solve efficiently even for quantum computers, such as lattice problems and hash functions. It runs on conventional computers and is used to replace RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, which Shor's algorithm can break. 耐量子計算機暗号

items.n: Post-training quantization
items.x: Converting a trained model's weights and activations to lower precision after examining value ranges with representative data. 学習後量子化

items.n: Power analysis attack
items.x: A side-channel attack inferring secrets from a chip's power consumption traces. Differential power analysis (DPA), which processes many traces statistically, is especially powerful. 電力解析攻撃

items.n: Power capping
items.x: Setting and enforcing an upper limit on server or CPU power, used in data centers to stay within power and cooling limits. パワーキャップ

items.n: Power domain
items.x: A region of a chip sharing the same supply voltage and power on/off control, allowing voltage and power to be managed per block. 電源ドメイン

items.n: Power gating
items.x: A low-power technique that switches off the supply to unused blocks, eliminating nearly all their leakage. State saving and wake-up time must be considered. パワーゲーティング

items.n: Power management IC (PMIC)
items.x: An IC that generates multiple voltages from a battery or similar and manages power-up sequencing and voltage changes. PMIC

items.n: Power MOSFET
items.x: A MOSFET built to handle large currents and voltages. It switches quickly and is widely used in power supply circuits and the like. パワーMOSFET

items.n: Power sequencing
items.x: The specified order for applying and removing multiple supply voltages to a chip; violating it can cause malfunction or latch-up. パワーシーケンス

items.n: Power usage effectiveness (PUE)
items.x: Total data center power divided by IT equipment power; values closer to 1 indicate higher efficiency. PUE

items.n: Pre-amorphization implant (PAI)
items.x: Implanting germanium or similar first to make the surface amorphous, so that the following implant does not channel and a shallow junction results. プリアモルファス化注入(PAI)

items.n: Precharge
items.x: Charging the bit lines to a set potential (half the supply voltage in DRAM, for example) before a read. In DRAM it also means closing the open row to prepare for activating the next one. プリチャージ

items.n: Precision and recall
items.x: Evaluation metrics for two-class classification models. Precision is the fraction of items predicted positive that are actually positive, TP ÷ (TP + FP), and recall is the fraction of actually positive items that were predicted positive, TP ÷ (TP + FN). In general, changing the decision threshold raises one and lowers the other. Their harmonic mean, 2PR ÷ (P + R), is called the F1 score. 適合率と再現率

items.n: Precursor
items.x: A source compound that reacts to form the desired film in CVD or ALD, such as TEOS or metal-organic compounds. プリカーサ(前駆体)

items.n: Prefetching
items.x: Loading data into the cache before it is requested because it is likely to be needed soon. Hardware prefetchers detect access patterns, and software prefetching uses explicit instructions. プリフェッチ

items.n: Prefill
items.x: The first stage of LLM inference, processing all input prompt tokens together; it tends to be compute-bound. The following token-by-token generation is called decode. プリフィル

items.n: Prefix sum
items.x: Computing the running totals of an array from the start, also called a scan. It can be computed in parallel and is used to find write positions when compacting output. プレフィックスサム

items.n: Prescaler
items.x: A circuit that divides the clock fed to a timer or similar by a fixed ratio, bringing a fast clock into a range the timer can count. プリスケーラ

items.n: Preston's equation
items.x: The empirical rule that the CMP removal rate is proportional to the product of polishing pressure and the relative speed between pad and wafer. プレストンの式

items.n: Primary key
items.x: A column, or set of columns, used to uniquely identify one row in a table. It carries the constraints that its values must not be duplicated and must not include NULL. The primary key is chosen from among the minimal sets of columns that can identify a row uniquely (candidate keys). 主キー

items.n: Principal component analysis (PCA)
items.x: A dimensionality-reduction method that represents data with many variables using fewer variables while losing as little information as possible. It takes the direction of greatest variance in the data as the first principal component, the direction of greatest variance orthogonal to it as the second, and so on, and represents the data with only the leading components. Mathematically this amounts to finding the eigenvectors of the data's covariance matrix. It is used for visualizing data, removing noise and preprocessing before training. 主成分分析(PCA)

items.n: Principle of least privilege
items.x: The idea of giving users, programs and services only the minimum privileges needed to do their job. It keeps the scope of damage small even if an account is taken over, malware runs or someone makes a mistake. 最小権限の原則

items.n: Priority inheritance
items.x: Temporarily raising a low-priority task holding a resource to the priority of the high-priority task waiting for it, preventing priority inversion. 優先度継承

items.n: Priority inversion
items.x: A situation in which a high-priority task waiting for a resource held by a low-priority task is held up because a medium-priority task preempts the low one. 優先度逆転

items.n: Privileged mode
items.x: A CPU operating mode reserved for the OS kernel, in which dangerous operations such as setting page tables and controlling I/O are allowed. It is distinguished from user mode, where applications run. 特権モード

items.n: Probe card
items.x: A fixture that presses many needles (probes) onto chip electrodes on the wafer to connect them electrically to a tester. プローブカード

items.n: Probe effect
items.x: The phenomenon in which adding a measurement mechanism changes the behavior of the program being measured. プローブ効果

items.n: Problem management
items.x: The process whose goal is to identify the root cause (the problem) behind one or more incidents and prevent recurrence with a permanent fix. It includes reactive work, investigating causes from incidents that have occurred, and proactive work, analyzing incident trends to prevent failures that have not happened yet. A problem whose root cause or workaround is known but whose fix is not yet complete is recorded as a known error and shared with the service desk and others. When a fix changes a system, it goes through change management. 問題管理

items.n: Procedure linkage table (PLT)
items.x: A table of small stubs used to call shared-library functions. With lazy binding, the dynamic linker resolves the address on the first call and writes it into the GOT. PLT(プロシージャリンケージテーブル)

items.n: Process capability index (Cpk)
items.x: An index of how much margin a process's variation and mean offset leave relative to the specification limits. A common benchmark is 1.33 or higher. 工程能力指数(Cpk)

items.n: Process window
items.x: The range of exposure dose and focus over which pattern dimensions stay within tolerance. The wider it is, the more robust manufacturing is to variation. プロセスウィンドウ

items.n: Product life cycle
items.x: A model that divides the period from a product's launch to its disappearance from the market into four stages (introduction, growth, maturity and decline) to consider how sales and profit change and which strategies suit each stage. プロダクトライフサイクル

items.n: Product portfolio management (PPM)
items.x: A method of classifying businesses or products into four groups (stars, cash cows, question marks and dogs) along two axes, market growth rate and relative market share, to decide how to allocate management resources. It was proposed by Boston Consulting Group. プロダクトポートフォリオマネジメント(PPM)

items.n: Profiler
items.x: A tool that measures which functions or parts of a program consume execution time, using sampling or instrumentation. プロファイラ

items.n: Program loader
items.x: The OS function that reads an executable into memory, maps its parts with the right permissions, sets up arguments on the stack and starts the program. ローダ

items.n: Projected range
items.x: The average depth at which implanted ions come to rest. It is deeper with higher acceleration energy and with lighter ions. 投影飛程

items.n: Propagation delay
items.x: The time from an input change to the resulting output change. For logic ICs it is measured between the points where input and output cross 50% of their swing, and is specified separately as tPLH (output low to high) and tPHL (output high to low). It grows with load capacitance. 伝搬遅延

items.n: Propagation loss
items.x: The fraction of optical power lost to scattering and absorption as light travels through a waveguide or fiber, expressed in dB/cm or dB/km. In silicon waveguides the main cause is scattering from sidewall roughness, with typical values around 1 to 3 dB/cm, far higher than fiber's roughly 0.2 dB/km. 伝搬損失

items.n: Pruning
items.x: Zeroing out low-impact weights in a neural network to reduce computation and memory. Structured pruning, which follows fixed patterns, is easier to accelerate in hardware. プルーニング

items.n: Pseudo-instruction
items.x: Something written like an instruction in assembly that the assembler replaces with one or more real instructions, such as RISC-V nop, mv, li, j and ret. 疑似命令

items.n: Pseudocode
items.x: A way of writing an algorithm's steps that does not depend on any particular programming language. Part B of Japan's Fundamental Information Technology Engineer Examination presents programs in a pseudo-language that defines type declarations, assignment with ←, control structures such as if, while and for, and array indices that start at 1. 擬似言語

items.n: PSRR (power supply rejection ratio)
items.x: A measure of how little supply-voltage variation reaches a circuit's output. The larger it is, the more immune the circuit is to supply noise. PSRR(電源電圧変動除去比)

items.n: Public-key cryptography
items.x: A cryptographic method that uses a matched pair of different keys for encryption and decryption: a public key and a private key. The public key may be known to anyone, while only its owner holds the private key. It makes key distribution easy but is computationally heavy, so it is combined with symmetric-key cryptography for encrypting the data itself. RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography are typical examples. 公開鍵暗号

items.n: Pull-up resistor
items.x: A resistor connecting a signal line to the supply so it rests at logic 1 when nothing drives it. It keeps input pins from floating and is used on I2C lines and elsewhere. プルアップ抵抗

items.n: Pulse-width modulation (PWM)
items.x: A method that adjusts average voltage or power by varying the high time of an output while keeping the period constant. Used to dim LEDs and control motor speed. PWM(パルス幅変調)

items.n: Punch-through
items.x: A condition in which the source and drain depletion regions merge and current flows that the gate cannot control. It occurs when the channel is too short or the substrate doping is too low. パンチスルー

items.n: QAM (quadrature amplitude modulation)
items.x: A digital modulation scheme that represents data by changing both the amplitude and the phase of the carrier. Each symbol sends one of a grid of signal points formed by combinations of in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) components, and M-QAM with M points sends log₂ M bits per symbol: 4 bits for 16QAM, 6 for 64QAM and 8 for 256QAM. More levels mean higher speed, but the points are closer together, so a higher S/N is needed. QAM(直交振幅変調)

items.n: QFN (quad flat no-lead package)
items.x: A surface-mount package with terminals exposed around the perimeter of its underside and no leads projecting from the sides. The central thermal pad on the bottom can be soldered to the board, making it small with good heat dissipation. QFN

items.n: QFP (quad flat package)
items.x: A surface-mount package with gull-wing leads extending from all four sides. Its joints are easy to inspect visually, and it is widely used for microcontrollers and similar ICs. QFP

items.n: Quantization error
items.x: The error that arises when rounding a continuous analog value to a digital value with a finite number of bits. At most half of one LSB. 量子化誤差

items.n: Quantization-aware training
items.x: Training that simulates quantization rounding so weights adapt to its error, preserving accuracy even at low bit widths. 量子化を考慮した学習

items.n: Quantum efficiency
items.x: The fraction of incident photons converted into signal electrons. The higher it is, the better the sensitivity. 量子効率

items.n: Quantum entanglement
items.x: A link between the states of several qubits that cannot be written as a combination of the states of the individual qubits. In (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2, the two measurement results always agree. It is one of the sources of the computing power of quantum computers, but it cannot be used to send information faster than light. 量子もつれ

items.n: Quantum error correction
items.x: A technology that spreads the information of one logical qubit over many physical qubits and measures only clues to the errors (the syndrome), so that errors can be found and corrected during a computation. It must handle both bit-flip and phase-flip errors and requires the physical error rate to be well below a threshold. 量子誤り訂正

items.n: Quantum gate
items.x: A basic operation that changes the state of qubits. There are single-qubit gates such as X (bit flip), Z (phase flip) and H (Hadamard) and two-qubit gates such as CNOT, and they can be represented as rotations on the Bloch sphere. They are implemented with microwave pulses for superconducting qubits and with lasers and similar means for ions and neutral atoms. 量子ゲート

items.n: Quantum superposition
items.x: The ability of a quantum system such as a qubit to be in a state formed by adding several states, such as |0⟩ and |1⟩, with complex amplitudes. A measurement gives one of the outcomes at random, and differences in the phases of the amplitudes affect the results through interference. 量子重ね合わせ

items.n: Quantum well
items.x: A structure in which a thin layer, a few nanometers thick, with a small band gap is sandwiched between layers with a larger band gap. It confines carriers to promote recombination and is used as the active layer of LEDs and lasers. 量子井戸

items.n: Quartile
items.x: The values at the positions that divide data sorted by size into four equal parts, called from the smallest the first quartile, the second quartile (the median) and the third quartile. The interquartile range, the third quartile minus the first, is the width containing the middle half of the data and is a measure of spread little affected by outliers. A box plot shows the quartiles as a box and the minimum, maximum and so on as whiskers, making the shapes of distributions easy to compare. There are several conventions for computing quartiles, and the values differ slightly between methods. 四分位数

items.n: Quasi-Fermi level
items.x: Separate Fermi levels for electrons and holes, used to describe a semiconductor driven out of equilibrium by light or current injection. The larger the split between them, the more excess carriers there are. 擬フェルミ準位

items.n: Qubit
items.x: The unit that represents information in a quantum computer. It can be in a superposition α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ of |0⟩ and |1⟩, and a measurement gives 0 with probability |α|² and 1 with probability |β|². Qubits are realized with superconducting circuits, ions, neutral atoms, electron spins in silicon, photons and more. 量子ビット

items.n: Queue
items.x: A first-in, first-out (FIFO) data structure in which the element added first is removed first. Adding to the back is called enqueue and removing from the front is called dequeue. Queues are used for waiting lines of work, passing data between tasks and breadth-first search. キュー

items.n: Queueing theory
items.x: The theory that models with probability how processing requests arrive at a window or server and wait until it is free to be served, and that derives waiting times and queue lengths. A model is described in Kendall's notation, which lists the arrival distribution, service time distribution and number of servers, as in "M/M/1". In the M/M/1 model, the average waiting time is ρ/(1 − ρ) × Ts, using the utilization ρ = arrival rate λ × average service time Ts. It is used in computer performance evaluation, network delay analysis and analysis of work in progress in factories. 待ち行列理論

items.n: Quiescent current
items.x: The current consumed by an IC's own internal circuitry, such as a regulator's, separate from the current delivered to the load; written IQ. It dominates standby consumption in battery-powered equipment and ranges from under 1 µA to several mA depending on the product. 静止電流

items.n: R-2R ladder DAC
items.x: A DAC built from a ladder of only two resistor values, R and 2R. It needs few resistor types, and the resistor ratio does not grow as bits are added. R-2Rラダー型DAC

items.n: Race to idle
items.x: The strategy of finishing work quickly at high performance and entering deep sleep early, often advantageous when static power or other components' power is large. レーストゥアイドル

items.n: Radical
items.x: A neutral atom or molecule with an unpaired electron that is highly reactive chemically. Plasmas contain far more radicals than ions, and they drive chemical etching and deposition. ラジカル

items.n: RAID
items.x: A technology that combines several disks and uses them like a single storage device to improve speed or reliability. Its levels include RAID 0 (striping, which splits data across disks), RAID 1 (mirroring, which writes the same data to two disks), RAID 5 and RAID 6 (which write parity distributed across the disks), and RAID 10 (which combines mirroring and striping). RAID

items.n: Rail-to-rail
items.x: Describes an op amp or similar whose input or output range extends close to both supply rails. It allows large signal swings in single-supply, low-voltage circuits, although the output still saturates some tens of mV short of the rails depending on load current. レール・ツー・レール

items.n: Random dopant fluctuation (RDF)
items.x: Threshold-voltage variation in small transistors caused by statistical variation in the number and position of dopant atoms in the channel. FinFETs and FD-SOI, which allow lightly doped channels, reduce it. ランダムドーパントゆらぎ(RDF)

items.n: Ransomware
items.x: Malware that makes files on a computer unusable, for example by encrypting them, and demands a ransom in exchange for restoring them. Some attackers also threaten to publish stolen data. Backups kept disconnected from the network are an important safeguard. ランサムウェア

items.n: Rapidus
items.x: A Japanese semiconductor manufacturer founded in 2022 to mass-produce leading-edge logic chips at the 2 nm generation. It has a fab in Chitose, Hokkaido, and plans to start volume production in 2027 as a foundry that manufactures chips designed by other companies. ラピダス(Rapidus)

items.n: RC delay
items.x: Signal delay determined by the product of wire resistance (R) and capacitance (C). It grows as scaling makes wires thinner, limiting performance. RC遅延

items.n: RCA clean
items.x: A cleaning method that removes particles and organics with SC-1 (ammonia and hydrogen peroxide) and metal contamination with SC-2 (hydrochloric acid and hydrogen peroxide). RCA洗浄

items.n: Reactive sputtering
items.x: Sputtering a metal target in an atmosphere containing a reactive gas such as nitrogen or oxygen to form nitride or oxide films. It is used for films such as titanium nitride (TiN). 反応性スパッタリング

items.n: Read disturb
items.x: In NAND flash, the gradual shift in threshold voltage of unread cells caused by the weak voltage applied to them when the same block is read many times. リードディスターブ

items.n: Read-modify-write
items.x: A sequence that reads a value, changes part of it and writes it back. If interrupted midway, other changes can be lost. 読み出し・変更・書き込み

items.n: Reader-writer lock
items.x: A lock that admits any number of readers together but only one writer at a time, excluding everyone else while writing. 読み書きロック

items.n: Real-time operating system (RTOS)
items.x: An embedded OS that switches tasks by priority so the system responds within set time limits, such as FreeRTOS and Zephyr. RTOS(リアルタイムOS)

items.n: Recommended operating conditions
items.x: The range of conditions, such as supply voltage and ambient temperature, under which an IC is meant to operate. The min/max values in the electrical characteristics table are guaranteed only within this range. For a 3.3 V part, for example, the supply might be specified as 3.0 to 3.6 V. 推奨動作条件

items.n: Recovery check
items.x: A timing check that the release of an asynchronous reset or similar does not come too soon before a clock edge; it corresponds to setup. It is paired with the removal check, which verifies that release does not come too soon after the edge and corresponds to hold. リカバリーチェック

items.n: Recurrent neural network (RNN)
items.x: A neural network that processes sequence data one element at a time and passes the information so far to the next time step as a hidden state. The same weights are reused at every time step, so sequences of different lengths can be handled. Because vanishing gradients readily occur on long sequences, LSTM and GRU, which control the retention and forgetting of information with gates, were devised. Because it must compute in time order and is hard to parallelize, it has been replaced by the Transformer in many language-processing applications. 再帰型ニューラルネットワーク(RNN)

items.n: Recursion
items.x: A function calling itself as part of its own processing. The problem is split into smaller problems of the same form, and the calls stop at a case that is not split further (the base case). Each call uses stack space, so recursion that is too deep overflows the stack. Tail recursion, where the recursive call is the last thing the function does, can be converted into a loop. 再帰

items.n: Redistribution layer (RDL)
items.x: A wiring layer formed on a chip or wafer surface to route pads out to the positions of the external terminals. It is used in fan-out packages and interposers. 再配線層(RDL)

items.n: Redundancy repair
items.x: Replacing rows or columns that contain defective memory cells with spare rows or columns prepared in advance. The defect locations are found by testing and the switch is made with fuses or similar. It greatly improves yield. 冗長救済

items.n: Reference model
items.x: A separate model, often in C, implementing the same function as the circuit. Its results for the same inputs serve as expected values for the design's outputs. 参照モデル

items.n: Reflow soldering
items.x: Printing solder paste on a circuit board, placing components and heating everything in an oven to melt the solder. It is the standard method for surface mounting. リフローはんだ付け

items.n: Refractive index
items.x: The speed of light in vacuum divided by its speed in a material. At a wavelength of 1.55 µm, silicon is about 3.48 and oxide (SiO2) about 1.45; the larger this contrast, the more tightly light can be confined in a small waveguide. 屈折率

items.n: Refresh
items.x: The periodic reading and rewriting of DRAM data before the charge in its capacitors is lost through leakage. リフレッシュ

items.n: Register allocation
items.x: Assigning program variables and temporaries to the CPU's limited registers, ensuring values in use at the same time get different registers, often via coloring an interference graph. レジスタ割り当て

items.n: Register spilling
items.x: Saving some values to memory (the stack) during register allocation when more values are live than there are registers. The extra stores and reloads slow the code. スピル

items.n: Regression testing
items.x: Re-running existing tests after each design change to confirm that previously working features still work. 回帰テスト

items.n: Regularization
items.x: A method of reducing overfitting by adding to the loss function a penalty term that depends on the size of the weights, keeping the weights from growing too large. L1 regularization, which adds the sum of absolute weight values, tends to drive some weights to exactly zero, while L2 regularization (weight decay), which adds the sum of squared weights, shrinks the weights overall. The penalty strength is a hyperparameter chosen by cross-validation or similar means. In a broader sense, dropout, early stopping and other techniques for improving generalization are also collectively called regularization. 正則化

items.n: Reinforcement learning
items.x: A machine learning approach in which an agent (the learner) observes the state of an environment, chooses actions and learns by trial and error a way of choosing actions (a policy) that maximizes the total reward it receives, including future rewards. No correct answer is given for each action, and rewards often arrive with a delay. It is used for games, robot control and for tuning the output of language models to match human evaluations. 強化学習

items.n: Relational database
items.x: A database that represents data as tables (relations) of rows and columns and relates tables to each other through shared values. Also called an RDB. Queries and updates are made in SQL, and constraints such as primary keys and foreign keys keep the data consistent. 関係データベース

items.n: Relocation
items.x: Rewriting placeholder addresses in instructions and data with correct values once final addresses are decided. The linker does it, and with dynamic linking part of it is done at run time by the dynamic linker. 再配置

items.n: Remote attestation
items.x: A mechanism in which a device signs the state of its running software with an on-chip key and presents it to a remote server for trust verification. リモートアテステーション

items.n: ReRAM (resistive RAM)
items.x: Nonvolatile memory that applies voltage to form and break conductive paths in an oxide or similar material, storing information as differences in resistance. ReRAM(抵抗変化メモリ)

items.n: Reset synchronizer
items.x: A circuit that applies an asynchronous reset immediately but aligns its release to the clock through two flip-flops before distributing it. リセット同期化回路

items.n: Retention register
items.x: A flip-flop that keeps its state in a small always-powered storage element while the block is power-gated, allowing operation to resume where it left off. リテンションレジスタ

items.n: Retimer
items.x: A circuit that receives a high-speed serial signal, decides the bits and retransmits a clean signal. Inserted mid-channel to extend reach. リタイマ

items.n: Retrograde well
items.x: A well whose doping is higher deeper below the surface, made by high-energy implantation. It suppresses punch-through and latch-up while keeping the channel doping at the surface low. レトログレードウェル

items.n: Return address
items.x: The address to go back to when a function finishes. In RISC-V, jal puts the next instruction's address in ra (x1); in x86, call pushes it on the stack. リターンアドレス

items.n: Return value
items.x: The value a function returns to its caller when it finishes. In pseudocode, the value of the expression written after return becomes the return value, and the function ends when return is executed. 戻り値

items.n: Reverse recovery time
items.x: The time during which reverse current keeps flowing after a conducting diode is reverse-biased, until the stored minority carriers are removed. It causes switching loss and noise. 逆回復時間

items.n: RIE (reactive ion etching)
items.x: Dry etching that combines reactive species in a plasma with ions accelerated by an electric field. It enables vertical, anisotropic etching. RIE(反応性イオンエッチング)

items.n: Ring resonator
items.x: A looped waveguide that resonates only at wavelengths for which one round trip's optical length is an integer number of wavelengths. It is used as a wavelength filter or compact modulator. In silicon the resonance shifts by about 0.08 nm per °C, so heaters are often used to control its temperature. リング共振器

items.n: Risk assessment
items.x: Identifying the hazards of tasks or chemicals, estimating the size of the risks and deciding countermeasures in order of priority. リスクアセスメント

items.n: ROE (return on equity)
items.x: Net income divided by equity: how much profit a company earned relative to the funds provided by shareholders. It equals ROA (return on assets) multiplied by financial leverage (total assets ÷ equity). ROE(自己資本利益率)

items.n: RoHS Directive
items.x: The EU regulation restricting the use of specific hazardous substances such as lead and mercury in electrical and electronic equipment. RoHS指令

items.n: Rolling shutter
items.x: A readout method that exposes and reads pixel rows one after another. It is simple, but fast-moving subjects appear skewed. Exposing all pixels at once is a global shutter. ローリングシャッター

items.n: Roofline model
items.x: A model expressing attainable performance as the smaller of peak compute and memory bandwidth × arithmetic intensity, used to tell compute-bound from memory-bound work. Rooflineモデル

items.n: Root complex
items.x: The root of the PCI Express tree, connected to the CPU and memory, from which links fan out through switches to devices (endpoints). ルートコンプレックス

items.n: Root of trust
items.x: The component unconditionally trusted as the starting point of security checks, such as immutable ROM boot code and a public key inside the chip. ルートオブトラスト

items.n: Round half to even
items.x: Rounding to the nearest representable value and, on an exact tie, to the one whose last bit is even (0). It is the IEEE 754 default and keeps rounding errors from accumulating in one direction. 最近接偶数丸め

items.n: Rounding error
items.x: The error that arises when a real number is represented with a finite number of digits and a value that cannot be represented is rounded to a nearby one. 0.1 cannot be represented exactly as a binary floating-point number, so errors build up when it is added repeatedly, and adding 0.1 ten times in double precision does not give 1.0. Avoid comparing real numbers with = and counting loop iterations with real numbers. 丸め誤差

items.n: Rowhammer
items.x: A DRAM phenomenon in which repeatedly activating the same row in a short time drains charge from cells in neighboring rows and flips their data. Because it can be exploited in attacks, countermeasures are built into DRAMs and memory controllers. ロウハンマー

items.n: RPO (recovery point objective)
items.x: A target expressing to what point in time data must be recoverable when a failure or disaster occurs. With an RPO of 1 hour, at most the last hour of data may be lost, so backups or copies of the data must be taken at least every hour. RPO(目標復旧時点)

items.n: RTL (register-transfer level)
items.x: A design abstraction that describes circuits by how data moves and is processed between registers. It is written in Verilog or VHDL and serves as the input to logic synthesis. RTL(レジスタ転送レベル)

items.n: RTO (recovery time objective)
items.x: A target for the time allowed from the occurrence of a failure or disaster until business operations or the system resume. The shorter the RTO, the more equipment and cost are needed, such as standby systems and backups ready for immediate use. RTO(目標復旧時間)

items.n: RTP (rapid thermal processing)
items.x: Heating single wafers to high temperature for a few seconds, typically with lamps. It allows annealing and thin oxide growth while limiting unwanted dopant diffusion. RTP(急速熱処理)

items.n: Sacrificial layer etching
items.x: A typical MEMS fabrication method that etches away a temporary layer (the sacrificial layer) beneath a structure, freeing beams or membranes so they can move. 犠牲層エッチング

items.n: SADP (self-aligned double patterning)
items.x: Forming spacers on the sidewalls of a core pattern, removing the core and using the spacers as the mask to make a pitch half of what lithography alone allows. Doing it twice is SAQP. SADP(自己整合ダブルパターニング)

items.n: Safe operating area
items.x: The range of voltage and current combinations in which a power transistor can be used without damage, abbreviated SOA. It is shown on a log-log graph, with boundaries set by on-resistance, current rating, power (thermal) limits and breakdown voltage. The thermal limit relaxes for shorter pulse widths. 安全動作領域

items.n: Safety goal
items.x: The top-level safety requirement defined for each hazardous event found in the HARA. It is phrased like "prevent unintended sudden acceleration" and inherits the ASIL of that event. 安全目標

items.n: Safety mechanism
items.x: A means of detecting faults and moving to a safe state, or containing their effects, before they lead to a hazardous event. Examples include ECC, lockstep CPUs, watchdog timers, voltage and clock monitors, and BIST. 安全機構

items.n: Salt
items.x: A random value added for each user when computing the hash value of a password. It makes the same password produce different hash values, making cracking with tables of precomputed hash values difficult. It is stored together with the hash value and does not need to be kept secret. ソルト

items.n: Sample-and-hold circuit
items.x: A circuit that captures (samples) the input voltage at an instant and holds it constant until AD conversion finishes. It is built from a switch and a capacitor. サンプルホールド回路

items.n: Sampling theorem
items.x: The theorem stating that a signal can be reconstructed if it is sampled at a frequency higher than twice its highest frequency component. Also called the Nyquist-Shannon theorem. サンプリング定理

items.n: Saturating arithmetic
items.x: Arithmetic that clamps results exceeding the representable range to the maximum or minimum instead of wrapping around. Used in audio and image signal processing to avoid large errors. 飽和演算

items.n: Saturation region
items.x: The state of a bipolar transistor in which both the base-emitter and base-collector junctions are forward-biased. The collector-emitter voltage falls to about 0.1-0.3 V, corresponding to a switch in the on state. 飽和領域

items.n: SC-1 (APM)
items.x: A mixture of ammonia, hydrogen peroxide and water used first in RCA cleaning. It removes particles and organics while lightly etching the surface. SC-1(APM)

items.n: SC-2 (HPM)
items.x: A mixture of hydrochloric acid, hydrogen peroxide and water used after SC-1 in RCA cleaning to remove metal contamination. SC-2(HPM)

items.n: Scale-out
items.x: A way of raising the processing capacity of a whole system by adding servers and sharing the processing among them. Compared with scale-up, which makes the parts of one server faster, capacity is easier to add and redundancy is gained, but the system must be designed so that the processing can be divided. Reducing the number of servers is called scale-in. スケールアウト

items.n: Scan test
items.x: A test method that uses scan chains, formed by linking a circuit's flip-flops in series, to set and observe internal states. スキャンテスト

items.n: Scanner
items.x: An exposure tool that moves the mask and wafer in sync under a slit of light. It is the mainstream production lithography tool and generally projects the mask pattern at 1/4 size. スキャナー

items.n: Schmitt trigger
items.x: A circuit whose switching threshold differs for rising and falling inputs (hysteresis). Its output does not chatter even with slowly changing or noisy signals. シュミットトリガ

items.n: Schottky barrier diode
items.x: A diode that uses a metal-semiconductor junction (Schottky junction). It has a low forward voltage and switches fast because there is no minority-carrier storage. ショットキーバリアダイオード

items.n: Scrum
items.x: A representative framework of agile development. With three roles, the Product Owner, the Scrum Master and the Developers, and the events held within Sprints of a fixed length of one month or less (Sprint Planning, the Daily Scrum, the Sprint Review and the Sprint Retrospective), a working product is built a little at a time. スクラム

items.n: SDC
items.x: A format for timing constraints that describes clock periods and waveforms, input and output delays, timing exceptions and so on. Written as Tcl commands, it is shared by logic synthesis, place-and-route and STA tools. SDC

items.n: SDS (safety data sheet)
items.x: A document describing the hazards of a chemical, how to handle it, first-aid measures and more. SDS(安全データシート)

items.n: Seasoning
items.x: Running dummy wafers before product to stabilize the condition of an etch (or similar) chamber's walls, since wall changes alter process results. シーズニング

items.n: Secure boot
items.x: A mechanism that verifies the digital signature of the next software at each boot stage and starts only authentic software, forming a chain of trust. セキュアブート

items.n: Secure enclave
items.x: A TEE approach in which part of an application runs in a region whose memory the CPU encrypts and protects, hidden even from the OS and hypervisor. エンクレーブ

items.n: Seed layer
items.x: A thin copper film deposited by sputtering or similar before copper electroplating. It provides the conductive path for the plating current. シード層

items.n: Segregation coefficient
items.x: The ratio of impurity concentration in the crystal to that in the melt during solidification. For most impurities it is below 1, so they concentrate in the melt and the later part of a CZ crystal has higher impurity levels. 偏析係数

items.n: Segregation of duties
items.x: An internal control principle that divides responsibilities and authority so that no single person can complete, alone, the initiation (input), approval, recording and custody of assets for a transaction. Errors and fraud cannot be completed by one person's decision, and they are easier to find through mutual checks. In information systems, it is applied by separating the people who develop programs from those who deploy them to production and operate them, and by separating the authority to enter data from the authority to approve it. 職務分掌

items.n: Selective epitaxial growth
items.x: A method that grows crystal only where silicon is exposed, not on areas covered by insulating film. It is used for SiGe in transistor sources and drains and elsewhere. 選択エピタキシャル成長

items.n: Selectivity
items.x: In etching, the ratio of the etch rate of the target film to that of the mask or underlying film. Higher selectivity means less damage to the underlayer. 選択比

items.n: Self-bias
items.x: The negative DC potential that the wafer electrode naturally acquires in a capacitively coupled plasma. It accelerates positive ions toward the wafer, aiding anisotropic etching. セルフバイアス

items.n: Self-refresh
items.x: A low-power DRAM state in which the DRAM refreshes itself to retain contents without commands from the memory controller, used during system sleep. セルフリフレッシュ

items.n: SEM (scanning electron microscope)
items.x: A microscope that scans a finely focused electron beam over a sample and detects secondary electrons and other signals to image the surface. It resolves features of a few nanometers, far beyond optical microscopes. SEM(走査電子顕微鏡)

items.n: Semaphore
items.x: A synchronization mechanism holding a counter of remaining units: decrement before use (waiting at 0) and increment when done. Used to manage resources with a fixed number of units. セマフォ

items.n: Sense amplifier
items.x: A circuit that amplifies the tiny voltage difference read from a memory cell and decides whether it is 0 or 1. センスアンプ

items.n: Sensitivity list
items.x: The list in @( ) after a Verilog always that names the signals triggering the block. Omissions in combinational logic make simulation and hardware disagree. センシティビティリスト

items.n: Sequential circuit
items.x: A logic circuit that stores state in flip-flops and the like, so its output depends on both inputs and past state. Examples include counters and registers. 順序回路

items.n: Sequential consistency
items.x: The most intuitive memory consistency model: all cores' operations appear in one order in which each core's operations keep their program order. 逐次一貫性

items.n: SerDes
items.x: Serializer/deserializer: a circuit that turns parallel on-chip data into a fast serial bit stream for transmission and restores the parallel data at the receiver. It is the heart of high-speed serial physical layers. SerDes

items.n: Service desk
items.x: A single point of contact (SPOC) that receives all inquiries, failure reports, service requests and the like from users. It records what it receives, resolves what it can itself, escalates what it cannot to specialist technical teams and others, tracks progress and informs users of the outcome. Forms include a local service desk at each site, a centralized one in a single location and a virtual one that links staff in various places over a network. サービスデスク

items.n: Set-associative cache
items.x: A cache organization in which data can go in any of several locations (ways) within the one set selected by the address. An n-way cache compares n tags in parallel on each access. セットアソシアティブ方式

items.n: Setup time
items.x: The minimum time before the active clock edge during which a flip-flop's data input must be stable. Paths that cannot meet it limit the maximum operating frequency. セットアップ時間

items.n: Shadowing
items.x: When implanting at a tilt, the effect of tall patterns such as resist casting shadows so that some areas receive no implant. シャドウイング

items.n: Shannon–Hartley theorem
items.x: A theorem stating that for a channel with bandwidth B and signal-to-noise ratio S/N, the theoretical upper limit on the error-free transmission rate (the channel capacity) is C = B·log₂(1 + S/N). S/N is used as a linear ratio. Capacity is proportional to bandwidth but grows only logarithmically with S/N. シャノンの定理

items.n: Shared library
items.x: A library loaded at run time by dynamic linking: .so on Linux, .dll on Windows. Built as position-independent code, its code pages can be shared by many processes. 共有ライブラリ

items.n: Shift register
items.x: A chain of flip-flops that moves data one bit to the next stage on each clock. It is used for serial-parallel conversion and as the scan chain in scan testing. シフトレジスタ

items.n: Shor's algorithm
items.x: A quantum algorithm that solves factoring of large integers and the discrete logarithm problem in polynomial time by finding periods with the quantum Fourier transform. It was published by Peter Shor in 1994. It can break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography, but running it requires a large fault-tolerant quantum computer. ショアのアルゴリズム

items.n: Short-channel effect
items.x: Phenomena in which, as gate length shrinks, the drain's electric field lowers the threshold voltage and increases off-state leakage current. 短チャネル効果

items.n: Short-circuit current
items.x: Current that flows from supply to ground in a CMOS gate during the brief time while the input switches and both the pMOS and nMOS are on. Also called crowbar current, it adds to power consumption. 貫通電流

items.n: Short-circuit evaluation
items.x: A way of evaluating the logical operators and and or that skips the right side when the left side alone decides the result. With and, the right side is not evaluated if the left side is false; with or, if the left side is true. It is often used to prevent out-of-range accesses by putting the array range check on the left. 短絡評価

items.n: Short-circuit withstand time
items.x: The time a power device can survive a short circuit, such as both inverter switches turning on at once, without being destroyed. Protection circuits must cut the current within this time. 短絡耐量

items.n: Shot noise
items.x: Noise from statistical fluctuation in the number of photons or electrons. Its size is proportional to √N for a signal of N electrons, so it is relatively larger when light is scarce. ショットノイズ

items.n: SiC (silicon carbide)
items.x: A wide-band-gap semiconductor with a band gap of about 3.3 eV. Its high breakdown field makes it suitable for high-voltage, low-loss power devices. SiC(炭化ケイ素)

items.n: Side-channel attack
items.x: An attack inferring secrets such as keys from physical information other than the intended output, such as processing time, power consumption or electromagnetic emissions. サイドチャネル攻撃

items.n: Siemens process
items.x: A method that reduces trichlorosilane with hydrogen to deposit high-purity polycrystalline silicon on heated silicon rods. It is the main way to make raw silicon for semiconductors. シーメンス法

items.n: SiGe (silicon-germanium)
items.x: An alloy of silicon and germanium with a larger lattice constant than silicon. Grown epitaxially, it is used to strain channels, as the base of HBTs and as the sacrificial layer in GAA transistors. SiGe(シリコンゲルマニウム)

items.n: Sign extension
items.x: Widening a signed integer to more bits by copying its top (sign) bit into all the new upper bits, which preserves its value. Filling the upper bits with zeros is zero extension. 符号拡張

items.n: Signal equalizer
items.x: A circuit that compensates for a channel attenuating high frequencies more, which smears the signal. Examples include receiver CTLE and DFE and transmitter de-emphasis. イコライザ

items.n: Significand
items.x: The bits of a floating-point number holding its significant digits. For normalized numbers the leading 1 is implied, so single precision stores 23 bits but has 24 bits of precision. 仮数

items.n: Silane (SiH4)
items.x: A gas compound of silicon and hydrogen used as the source for CVD of polysilicon, silicon oxide and silicon nitride. It ignites spontaneously in air, so it is handled under strict control. シラン(SiH4)

items.n: Silicide
items.x: A compound of silicon and a metal, such as NiSi or TiSi2. It is formed on source, drain and gate surfaces to reduce resistance and contact resistance. シリサイド

items.n: Silicon cycle
items.x: The recurring boom-and-bust pattern of the semiconductor market driven by supply and demand. One cause is that fabs take years to build, so supply lags changes in demand. シリコンサイクル

items.n: Silicon interposer
items.x: A silicon intermediate substrate that holds chips side by side and connects them densely with fine wiring. It is used to connect GPUs and HBM, among other things. シリコンインターポーザ

items.n: Silicon photonics
items.x: Technology for integrating optical circuits such as waveguides, modulators and photodetectors on silicon. It uses the materials and processes of CMOS fabs, enabling volume production on 200 mm or 300 mm wafers. Because silicon emits light poorly, lasers are added using compound semiconductors. シリコンフォトニクス

items.n: SIMD
items.x: Short for single instruction, multiple data: one instruction performs the same operation on several data elements at once. It speeds up image processing and AI calculations. SIMD

items.n: SIMS (secondary ion mass spectrometry)
items.x: A method that sputters a sample with primary ions and mass-analyzes the secondary ions to measure impurity depth profiles with high sensitivity. SIMS(二次イオン質量分析法)

items.n: Single instruction, multiple threads (SIMT)
items.x: An execution model in which programs are written per thread while hardware bundles threads into warps (32 on NVIDIA) that execute the same instruction in lockstep. SIMT

items.n: Single point of failure (SPOF)
items.x: A point where a stop in just that one place stops the whole system. Besides equipment that is not made redundant, a shared power supply, a network line or a configuration file can also be a single point of failure. In reliability design, finding single points of failure and making them redundant is a basic step. 単一障害点(SPOF)

items.n: Single-mode fiber
items.x: Optical fiber that carries only one propagation mode, with a core diameter of about 9 µm. With no pulse spreading from different modes traveling at different speeds (modal dispersion), it is used for long-distance and high-speed links. シングルモードファイバ

items.n: Single-wafer cleaning
items.x: A cleaning method that processes one wafer at a time. It minimizes cross-contamination and allows per-wafer control. Immersing many wafers in a tank at once is batch cleaning. 枚葉式洗浄

items.n: Skin effect
items.x: The concentration of high-frequency current near the surface of a conductor, which raises its effective resistance. The higher the frequency, the thinner the surface layer carrying the current. 表皮効果

items.n: SLA (service level agreement)
items.x: An agreement between the provider and the user of an IT service that sets the quality levels, such as availability, response time, time to recover from failures and support hours, together with how they are measured and what happens if they are not met. SLA(サービスレベル合意)

items.n: Slack
items.x: A value expressing timing margin. For setup it is required time minus arrival time, and for hold it is arrival time minus required time; a negative value means a violation. スラック

items.n: SLC (single-level cell)
items.x: A flash format that stores one bit per cell. With only two threshold-voltage states it is faster and more durable than multi-level formats. SLC(シングルレベルセル)

items.n: Sleep mode
items.x: A microcontroller state that stops clocks or power to the CPU and peripherals while idle to save power, waking on an interrupt or similar. スリープモード

items.n: Slew rate
items.x: The maximum rate at which an op-amp's output voltage can change, expressed in V/µs. If it is insufficient for large, high-frequency signals, the waveform distorts. スルーレート

items.n: Slip
items.x: A defect in which crystal planes shift and dislocations form under stress from temperature differences or the wafer's own weight during high-temperature processing of large wafers. It can cause problems such as overlay errors. スリップ

items.n: Slurry
items.x: The liquid used in CMP, with fine abrasive particles dispersed in chemicals. It flattens surfaces by combining chemical action with mechanical polishing. スラリー

items.n: SMT (simultaneous multithreading)
items.x: A technique in which one CPU core processes instructions from several threads at once, making better use of its execution units. Intel calls it Hyper-Threading. SMT(同時マルチスレッディング)

items.n: Snubber circuit
items.x: A network such as a resistor and capacitor placed across a power device to suppress the voltage spikes (surges) and ringing that occur during switching. スナバ回路

items.n: SoC (system on chip)
items.x: An IC that integrates the functions a system needs, such as CPU, GPU, memory controller and communications, on one chip. The heart of a smartphone is a typical example. SoC(システムオンチップ)

items.n: Social engineering
items.x: The general term for techniques that exploit people's psychology, habits and carelessness rather than technical means, to get them to reveal important information such as passwords or to perform actions. Examples include impersonation calls, peeking over someone's shoulder (shoulder surfing) and rummaging through trash (dumpster diving). ソーシャルエンジニアリング

items.n: Soft error
items.x: A temporary flip of data stored in memory or flip-flops caused by neutrons from cosmic rays, alpha particles and the like. The device is not damaged, so rewriting restores correct operation. ソフトエラー

items.n: Soft switching
items.x: Turning a switch on or off when the voltage across it or current through it is nearly zero, as in zero-voltage switching (ZVS). It reduces switching loss and noise. ソフトスイッチング

items.n: SOI wafer
items.x: A wafer with a thin silicon layer on a buried oxide (BOX) layer over a silicon substrate. It is made, for example, by bonding a hydrogen-implanted wafer and splitting it. Its low parasitic capacitance suits FD-SOI devices and MEMS. SOIウエハ

items.n: Solid solubility
items.x: The maximum concentration of an impurity that can dissolve in a crystal at a given temperature. It sets the upper limit of electrically active dopant concentration. 固溶度

items.n: SOT-MRAM
items.x: MRAM that flips magnetization by spin-orbit torque from a current in a heavy-metal layer. The write and read current paths are separate, giving fast, durable writes. SOT-MRAM

items.n: SOTIF (safety of the intended functionality)
items.x: The concept that addresses hazards arising without any component failure, from sensor performance limits, insufficient specifications or reasonably foreseeable misuse. It is standardized as ISO 21448 and is central to developing automated driving and driver-assistance systems. SOTIF(意図した機能の安全性)

items.n: SPAD (single-photon avalanche diode)
items.x: A photodetector biased above breakdown so that even a single photon triggers a large avalanche pulse. It is used for ranging, such as in LiDAR. SPAD(単一光子アバランシェダイオード)

items.n: Spatial locality
items.x: The tendency to access addresses near one just accessed, as when reading an array in order. It is why caches fetch data a whole cache line at a time. 空間的局所性

items.n: SPC (statistical process control)
items.x: A method of maintaining quality by monitoring process data with control charts and the like and detecting anomalies statistically. SPC(統計的工程管理)

items.n: SPEC CPU
items.x: A standard CPU benchmark suite of many programs based on real applications, reporting ratios against a reference machine combined by geometric mean. SPEC CPU

items.n: Specialty gases
items.x: High-purity gases with toxic or flammable properties used in semiconductor manufacturing, such as silane, arsine and phosphine. They are supplied under strict control. 特殊材料ガス

items.n: Spectre
items.x: A class of vulnerabilities, disclosed in 2018, that induces mispredicted speculative execution to read secret data and infers its value from traces left in the cache. Spectre

items.n: Speculative decoding
items.x: Speeding up inference by having a small model draft several tokens ahead and a large model verify them together, accepting the correct ones at once. 投機的デコーディング

items.n: Speculative execution
items.x: A CPU technique that executes instructions ahead based on predictions, such as branch outcomes, before they are known. Wrong results are discarded, but traces such as cache state may remain. 投機的実行

items.n: Speedup
items.x: Execution time before an improvement divided by the time after; a value of 2 means twice as fast. 速度向上率

items.n: SPFM (single-point fault metric)
items.x: An ISO 26262 hardware metric expressing how small the share of single-point faults (which alone violate a safety goal) and residual faults is among safety-related faults. Typical targets are at least 90% for ASIL B, 97% for ASIL C and 99% for ASIL D. SPFM(単一点故障指標)

items.n: SPI
items.x: Serial Peripheral Interface: synchronous serial communication in which data is exchanged in both directions on a master-driven clock, with devices selected by chip-select lines. Used for fast parts. SPI

items.n: SPICE
items.x: A circuit simulator that calculates voltages and currents in transistor-level circuits in detail using device models. It is used for analog design and cell characterization. SPICE

items.n: Spike anneal
items.x: An anneal that ramps the wafer quickly to a high temperature and cools it again with almost no hold time. It activates dopants while limiting diffusion, for shallow junctions. スパイクアニール

items.n: Spin coating
items.x: Dispensing a liquid at the center of the wafer and spinning it at high speed so centrifugal force spreads a thin, uniform film. It is used for photoresist and spin-on dielectrics. スピンコート

items.n: Spin qubit
items.x: An approach that uses the spin direction of electrons or atomic nuclei as qubits. In silicon, single electrons are confined in quantum dots formed by gate electrodes. The qubits are small and are expected to be integrated using CMOS fabrication technology. To reduce noise from nuclear spins, silicon enriched in ²⁸Si is used. スピン量子ビット

items.n: Spinlock
items.x: A lock that waits by repeatedly checking the lock variable in a loop. Fast for short waits, but it keeps using the CPU while waiting. スピンロック

items.n: SPM (sulfuric acid-hydrogen peroxide mixture)
items.x: A mixture of sulfuric acid and hydrogen peroxide. Its strong oxidizing power removes organics such as resist. SPM(硫酸過水)

items.n: Spread-spectrum clocking (SSC)
items.x: Slowly varying a clock's frequency slightly to spread electromagnetic emission energy across a wider band and lower its peaks. スペクトラム拡散クロック

items.n: Sputtering
items.x: A type of PVD in which ions in a plasma bombard a target and the ejected atoms are deposited on the wafer. スパッタリング

items.n: SQL
items.x: The standard language for defining tables, searching, inserting, updating and deleting data, and controlling privileges in relational databases. It is standardized by ISO/IEC. Its statements include SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE TABLE and GRANT. SQL

items.n: SQL injection
items.x: An attack that exploits a web application building SQL statements by simply concatenating user input, using the input to change the meaning of the command and manipulate the database without authorization. Prepared statements with placeholders are the fundamental countermeasure. SQLインジェクション

items.n: SRH recombination (Shockley-Read-Hall recombination)
items.x: Recombination of electrons and holes through deep levels (traps) in the band gap. It mainly determines minority-carrier lifetime in silicon and is accelerated by metal contamination and crystal defects. SRH再結合(ショックレー・リード・ホール再結合)

items.n: SSA form
items.x: An IR form in which variables are renamed so each is assigned exactly once, with φ functions selecting values at join points. Clear definition-use relationships make optimization easier. SSA形式

items.n: SSD (solid-state drive)
items.x: A storage device that stores data using NAND flash memory and a controller. It has no moving parts and offers faster random access and better shock resistance than an HDD. SSD
