items.n: STA (static timing analysis)
items.x: A method that calculates the delay of every path in a circuit without test patterns and checks that timing constraints are met. STA(静的タイミング解析)

items.n: Stable sort
items.x: A sort that keeps elements with equal keys in their original relative order. Bubble sort, insertion sort and merge sort are stable, while selection sort, quicksort and heapsort are generally not. Stability is needed when sorting by several keys in turn. 安定ソート

items.n: Stack
items.x: A last-in, first-out (LIFO) data structure in which the element added last is removed first. Adding an element is called push and removing one is called pop. Stacks are used to manage return addresses and local variables in function calls (the call stack), to evaluate expressions in Reverse Polish notation and for depth-first search. スタック

items.n: Stack frame
items.x: The area reserved on the stack each time a function is called. It holds the return address, saved registers and local variables and is freed when the function returns. スタックフレーム

items.n: Stack pointer
items.x: The register that points to the current top of the stack; sp (x2) in RISC-V. In many ISAs the stack grows toward lower addresses. スタックポインタ

items.n: Stacked CMOS image sensor
items.x: An image sensor whose pixel array and signal-processing circuitry are made on separate chips and bonded together. Each can use the most suitable process, making the chip smaller and processing faster. 積層型CMOSイメージセンサ

items.n: Stacking fault
items.x: A planar defect in which the stacking order of atomic planes is disrupted. It is a concern in epitaxial layers, thermal oxidation (OSF) and SiC crystals. 積層欠陥

items.n: Standard cell
items.x: A pre-designed, pre-verified building block such as a logic gate or flip-flop. Cells share a common height so automatic place-and-route can line them up to build large circuits. スタンダードセル

items.n: Standard deviation
items.x: A quantity expressing the size of the spread of data or of a random variable, often written σ (sigma). The variance is the average of the squared differences between each value and the mean, and the standard deviation is its positive square root. It has the same unit as the original data, so the width of the spread can be expressed directly, as in the mean ±1σ or ±3σ. It is widely used for control limits in process control, process capability indices, evaluating measurement errors and calculations with the normal distribution. 標準偏差

items.n: Static library
items.x: An archive bundling many object files (.a on Linux). During static linking, the linker extracts only the objects it needs into the executable. 静的ライブラリ

items.n: Static linking
items.x: Linking that copies the code of the libraries used into the executable. It runs without the libraries present, but the file is larger and library fixes require rebuilding. 静的リンク

items.n: Static power
items.x: Power consumed continuously by leakage currents through off transistors even when signals do not switch, also called leakage power. It rises steeply with temperature. 静的消費電力

items.n: Step coverage
items.x: A measure of how uniformly a film covers the sidewalls and bottoms of steps and holes compared with flat areas. ALD gives excellent step coverage. ステップカバレッジ

items.n: Step-flow growth
items.x: A growth mode in which the crystal extends sideways from atomic steps on a slightly off-axis substrate. In SiC it is used so the layer inherits the substrate's polytype. ステップフロー成長

items.n: STI (shallow trench isolation)
items.x: Isolating devices by etching shallow trenches in silicon, filling them with insulator and planarizing by CMP. It has no bird's beak like LOCOS and is the standard isolation for fine-pitch ICs. STI(シャロートレンチ分離)

items.n: Stiction
items.x: The sticking of tiny moving MEMS parts to the substrate through surface tension or surface adhesion, so they no longer move. It often happens during drying after sacrificial-layer removal. スティクション

items.n: Storage-class memory
items.x: Non-volatile memory intended to bridge the gap in speed, capacity and cost between DRAM and NAND flash. Products based on 3D XPoint were the best-known example. ストレージクラスメモリ

items.n: Store buffer
items.x: A small buffer in which a core holds writes temporarily. The core can move on without waiting for writes to complete, but other cores see the writes later. ストアバッファ

items.n: Strained silicon
items.x: Silicon whose band structure is modified by strain to raise carrier mobility. Tensile strain helps nMOS and compressive strain helps pMOS; it is applied with SiGe source/drain regions, nitride films and the like. ひずみシリコン

items.n: STREAM benchmark
items.x: A benchmark that copies and adds large arrays to measure the memory bandwidth actually achievable. STREAMベンチマーク

items.n: Streaming multiprocessor
items.x: On NVIDIA GPUs, a unit bundling arithmetic units, registers, shared memory and warp-scheduling circuitry. A GPU is built from many SMs. ストリーミングマルチプロセッサ

items.n: Strength reduction
items.x: Replacing expensive operations such as multiplication with cheaper ones such as addition or shifts, for example adding 4 each iteration instead of computing i * 4 every time. 強度低減

items.n: Strong scaling
items.x: Parallel performance evaluation that fixes problem size and measures how much time drops as processors are added. 強いスケーリング

items.n: Structured sparsity
items.x: Sparsity in which zero weights follow a fixed pattern; 2:4 sparsity, with two zeros in every four weights, lets matrix units compute about twice as fast. 構造化スパース

items.n: STT-MRAM
items.x: MRAM that writes by flipping the magnetization of the MTJ's free layer using the spin-transfer torque of a spin-polarized current. It is in volume production as embedded non-volatile memory. STT-MRAM

items.n: Stuck-at fault
items.x: The basic fault model in logic testing, which assumes a signal line is stuck at 0 or 1. 縮退故障

items.n: Subnet mask
items.x: A 32-bit value that shows how many upper bits of an IP address represent the network (the network part). Written like 255.255.255.0, which means the same as /24 in CIDR notation. サブネットマスク

items.n: Subnormal number
items.x: A floating-point number whose exponent field is all zeros, without an implied leading 1, representing values smaller than the smallest normal number. It fills the gap to zero gradually (gradual underflow), so x − y = 0 implies x = y. 非正規化数

items.n: Subthreshold swing
items.x: The gate voltage needed to change drain current tenfold below threshold. Its theoretical lower limit at room temperature is about 60 mV per decade; the smaller it is, the sharper the on/off switching. サブスレッショルドスイング

items.n: Successive-approximation ADC
items.x: An ADC that uses an internal DAC and comparator to determine one bit at a time, starting from the most significant. It balances speed, accuracy and power well. 逐次比較型ADC

items.n: Super loop
items.x: A firmware structure without an OS in which an infinite loop in main calls each task in turn, with urgent work done in interrupts. スーパーループ

items.n: Super-junction MOSFET
items.x: A power MOSFET whose drift layer has alternating p-type and n-type pillars. It allows higher drift-layer doping without losing breakdown voltage, achieving on-resistance below the conventional silicon limit. スーパージャンクションMOSFET

items.n: Superheterodyne receiver
items.x: A receiver architecture that mixes the received signal with the local oscillator (LO) signal in a mixer to convert it to a fixed intermediate frequency (IF) before amplifying and demodulating it. Highly selective filters at the IF remove adjacent channels. Signals at the image frequency, on the opposite side of the LO from the desired signal, are converted to the same IF, so they must be removed before the mixer. スーパーヘテロダイン方式

items.n: Superlattice
items.x: A periodic structure of alternating layers of different materials, each a few nanometers thick. It shows electronic properties absent in bulk crystals and is used in lasers, buffer layers and more. 超格子

items.n: Superscalar
items.x: A processor design that issues and executes several instructions per clock cycle. It has multiple execution units and processes independent instructions in parallel. スーパースカラ

items.n: Supervised learning
items.x: A machine learning approach that trains a model to predict the correct answer from an input, using data made of pairs of inputs and correct answers (labels). It is called regression when the predicted output is a continuous number and classification when it is one of a fixed set of classes. Models such as linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, support vector machines and neural networks are used. Preparing the labels often takes considerable effort. 教師あり学習

items.n: Surface code
items.x: A code for quantum error correction in which qubits are arranged on a two-dimensional grid and errors are detected using only operations between neighboring qubits. Its threshold is high, roughly 1%, and it suits superconducting qubit chips well. The rotated version with code distance d uses 2d² − 1 physical qubits per logical qubit. 表面符号

items.n: Switching loss
items.x: Loss that occurs while a power device switches between on and off, when voltage and current are present at the same time. It grows with switching frequency. スイッチング損失

items.n: SWOT analysis
items.x: A method of working out strategy by sorting internal factors of the company into strengths and weaknesses, and external factors of the environment into opportunities and threats. SWOT分析

items.n: Symbol resolution
items.x: The linker step that matches each function or variable name referenced in a file with its definition. No definition gives an undefined-reference error; more than one gives a multiple-definition error. シンボル解決

items.n: Symbol table
items.x: The list of function and variable names, with their addresses and attributes, contained in object files and executables. Used for linking and debugging; strip can remove it. シンボルテーブル

items.n: Symmetric-key cryptography
items.x: A cryptographic method that uses the same key for encryption and decryption, also called secret-key cryptography. Its computation is light and it can encrypt large amounts of data quickly, but securely sharing the key with the other party (key distribution) is a challenge. AES is a typical example. 共通鍵暗号

items.n: Synchronizer
items.x: A circuit that aligns an asynchronous signal to the receiving clock. The basic form is two flip-flops in series, which raises the probability that metastability in the first stage resolves before the next edge. 同期化回路

items.n: Synchronous reset
items.x: A reset sampled at clock edges to initialize flip-flops. Timing is easier to analyze, but it does not act while the clock is stopped. 同期リセット

items.n: Syntax analysis (parsing)
items.x: The compiler phase that checks whether the token sequence follows the language grammar and builds the program's structure as a tree. Grammar errors are detected here. 構文解析

items.n: System call
items.x: The mechanism by which applications ask the OS for services such as file I/O or memory allocation. A dedicated instruction raises an exception that switches to privileged mode and invokes the kernel. システムコール

items.n: Systematic defect
items.x: A defect that occurs repeatedly at particular patterns or locations because of interactions between design and process. It is distinguished from random defects caused by chance particles. システマティック不良

items.n: Systems audit
items.x: An activity in which specialist auditors independent of the audited area (systems auditors) inspect and evaluate whether controls over the risks associated with information systems are properly designed and operated, and report the results to management and others as assurance or as advice for improvement. It proceeds through audit planning, a preliminary survey, the main audit, evaluation and conclusion, audit reporting and follow-up. In Japan, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry publishes the System Audit Standards and the System Management Standards. システム監査

items.n: SystemVerilog
items.x: An extension of Verilog adding design features such as the logic type and always_ff/always_comb, and verification features such as classes, constrained random and assertions. SystemVerilog

items.n: Systolic array
items.x: An arrangement of many multiply-accumulate units in a grid that computes matrix products by passing data to neighboring units step by step. It is used in AI accelerators. シストリックアレイ

items.n: Tail current
items.x: Current that keeps flowing like a tail as an IGBT turns off, because stored minority carriers prevent it from dropping to zero immediately. It causes turn-off loss. テール電流

items.n: Tail latency
items.x: The slow end of the response-time distribution, such as the 99th percentile, which governs overall latency when a task waits on many components. テールレイテンシ

items.n: Tamper resistance
items.x: The ability to withstand physical attacks such as opening a chip or probing it, protecting internal secrets, for example by erasing keys on detection. 耐タンパ性

items.n: Tape-out
items.x: Handing over the finished, verified layout data to manufacturing for mask making. The name comes from the days when data was delivered on magnetic tape. テープアウト

items.n: TDDB (time-dependent dielectric breakdown)
items.x: A phenomenon in which an insulating film under sustained voltage eventually breaks down even below its breakdown voltage. It is used to evaluate the lifetime of gate oxides and the like. TDDB(経時絶縁破壊)

items.n: TDP (thermal design power)
items.x: A guide to the heat a CPU or similar chip generates under a typical heavy load. Cooling systems are designed around it. TDP(熱設計電力)

items.n: TEM (transmission electron microscope)
items.x: A microscope that observes thinned samples by passing an electron beam through them. With atomic-level resolution, it reveals cross-sectional structures and crystal defects. TEM(透過電子顕微鏡)

items.n: Temperature cycling
items.x: A reliability test that repeatedly applies high and low temperatures to evaluate solder-joint fatigue and package cracking or delamination caused by differences in thermal expansion between materials. 温度サイクル試験

items.n: Temporal locality
items.x: The tendency to access the same data or instructions again soon after a first access, as with variables reused inside a loop. One of the reasons caches work. 時間的局所性

items.n: Tensor core
items.x: A GPU unit that computes the product and sum of small matrices in one instruction, mainly with low-precision numbers, greatly speeding up AI. テンソルコア

items.n: Tensor parallelism
items.x: Splitting one layer's weight matrix by rows or columns across GPUs, computing partial products and combining them through communication. テンソル並列

items.n: TEOS
items.x: Short for tetraethoxysilane, a liquid organosilicon compound widely used as the source for CVD silicon oxide. It gives oxide films with good step coverage. TEOS

items.n: Test-driven development (TDD)
items.x: A way of developing software in a short repeated cycle: first write a test for the feature to be built, then write the minimum code to make the test pass, then refactor while keeping the tests passing. It spread as a practice of Extreme Programming (XP). テスト駆動開発(TDD)

items.n: Testbench
items.x: Simulation-only code that drives inputs to the design under test and checks its outputs. Since it is never synthesized, delays, display statements and similar can be used freely. テストベンチ

items.n: THB (temperature-humidity-bias test)
items.x: A reliability test that applies voltage in a hot, humid environment, typically 85 °C/85% RH, to evaluate corrosion and increased leakage caused by moisture entering the package. It is also called the 85/85 test. 高温高湿バイアス試験(THB)

items.n: Thermal diffusion
items.x: A doping method that diffuses impurity atoms into a semiconductor at high temperature. They spread from regions of high concentration to low. 熱拡散

items.n: Thermal donor
items.x: Oxygen clusters that act as donors when CZ silicon is heated around 450°C. Because they change the wafer's resistivity, they are annihilated by a higher-temperature treatment. サーマルドナー

items.n: Thermal noise (Johnson noise)
items.x: Noise caused by the thermal motion of electrons in a resistor. Its mean-square voltage is 4kTRΔf, proportional to temperature, resistance and bandwidth. 熱雑音(ジョンソン雑音)

items.n: Thermal oxidation
items.x: A method of forming an SiO2 film on silicon by heating it in oxygen or water vapor. There are dry and wet oxidation. 熱酸化

items.n: Thermal resistance
items.x: A measure of how hard it is for heat to flow, in °C/W. Multiplying dissipated power by thermal resistance gives the temperature rise. Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance is written θJA. 熱抵抗

items.n: Thermal throttling
items.x: Control that lowers frequency and voltage when a chip gets too hot, reducing heat to protect it. サーマルスロットリング

items.n: Third normal form (3NF)
items.x: The state of a table that is in second normal form and has no column determined via a column other than the primary key (no transitive functional dependency). If there is a dependency such as emp_no → dept_code → dept_name, for example, splitting off a department table gives third normal form. 第3正規形

items.n: Thrashing
items.x: A state in which physical memory is so short that pages are constantly evicted and reloaded, and little useful work gets done. It is relieved by running fewer processes or adding memory. スラッシング

items.n: Thread block
items.x: A group of GPU threads that runs on a single SM. Threads in a block can share data through shared memory and synchronize. スレッドブロック

items.n: Threading dislocation
items.x: A dislocation that runs up through the grown layer to the surface. GaN on sapphire or silicon has high densities (about 10⁸-10⁹ cm⁻²), which degrade device performance and reliability. 貫通転位

items.n: Three-way handshake
items.x: The procedure that establishes a TCP connection. Three exchanges, the client's SYN, the server's SYN+ACK and the client's ACK, confirm each side's initial sequence number. 3ウェイハンドシェイク

items.n: Threshold voltage
items.x: The gate voltage at which a channel (inversion layer) forms in a MOSFET and current starts to flow. Written as Vth. しきい値電圧

items.n: Throughput
items.x: The amount of work, requests or data processed per unit time, a different metric from latency, which describes how fast one task completes. スループット

items.n: Tickless kernel
items.x: An OS kernel that stops the periodic timer tick on idle CPUs so they can sleep until the next work. ティックレスカーネル

items.n: Time complexity (Big-O notation)
items.x: A description of how the work (time complexity) or memory (space complexity) an algorithm needs grows with the number of data items n. It is written in Big-O notation, such as O(n), O(n log n) or O(n²), dropping constant factors and lower-order terms. 計算量

items.n: Time constant
items.x: A quantity describing how fast a circuit such as an RC network responds to a step; for an RC circuit τ = RC. The response reaches about 63% of its final value after τ and has nearly settled after about 5τ. 時定数

items.n: Timing attack
items.x: A side-channel attack exploiting processing time that varies with secret values, prevented by constant-time implementation. タイミング攻撃

items.n: TLB (translation lookaside buffer)
items.x: A small cache that holds recent virtual-to-physical address translations. It avoids walking the page tables in memory on every access, speeding up address translation. TLB(変換索引バッファ)

items.n: TLB shootdown
items.x: On a multiprocessor, the procedure for making other cores discard stale translations from their TLBs after a page table is modified. It uses inter-processor interrupts or instructions that broadcast the invalidation to all cores, and is costly. TLBシュートダウン

items.n: TLC (triple-level cell)
items.x: A flash format that stores three bits per cell, distinguishing eight threshold-voltage states. It lowers cost per bit but reduces endurance. Four bits per cell is QLC. TLC(トリプルレベルセル)

items.n: TLS
items.x: Transport Layer Security. A protocol that encrypts communication, detects tampering and authenticates servers with certificates. HTTPS is HTTP protected by TLS. TLS

items.n: TMAH
items.x: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide, a metal-ion-free organic alkali used as a photoresist developer. Care is needed because it can cause poisoning through skin absorption. TMAH

items.n: TMR ratio
items.x: In an MTJ, the difference between the resistances in the parallel and antiparallel states divided by the parallel-state resistance. The larger it is, the easier it is to tell 0 from 1; MgO barriers give large values. TMR比

items.n: ToF (time of flight)
items.x: Measuring distance from the time light takes to travel to an object and back. ToF sensors are used in face recognition, robotics and automotive LiDAR. ToF(Time of Flight)

items.n: Toggle synchronizer
items.x: A scheme that turns each pulse on the sending side into a toggle of a level signal, synchronizes it, and recovers a pulse on the receiving side by XORing it with its value one cycle earlier. Pulses shorter than the receiving clock period are not lost, but pulses must be spaced several receiving cycles apart. トグル同期

items.n: Top-down analysis
items.x: A method using performance counters to divide CPU issue slots into frontend bound, backend bound, bad speculation and retiring, narrowing down bottlenecks. トップダウン分析

items.n: TOPS
items.x: Trillions of operations per second, a performance figure for AI accelerators, usually a theoretical peak counted at low precision. TOPS

items.n: Total store order (TSO)
items.x: The x86 memory consistency model. It allows only a later read of a different address to overtake an earlier write, reflecting the presence of a store buffer. TSO(トータルストアオーダー)

items.n: Trace table
items.x: A table that records how the values of variables change as a program is executed line by line by hand. It is used to check the number of iterations and the final values and to locate mistakes. Because it is done on paper, it is also called desk checking. トレース表

items.n: Transaction
items.x: A series of operations on a database treated as a single unit. COMMIT makes the results permanent, and ROLLBACK returns the data to its state before the transaction began. The DBMS manages transactions with locks and logs so that they satisfy atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability (the ACID properties). トランザクション

items.n: Transactional memory
items.x: A mechanism that runs critical sections speculatively, committing them as a whole if there is no conflict and rolling back and retrying if there is. トランザクショナルメモリ

items.n: Transconductance
items.x: The ratio of the change in drain current to the change in gate voltage, written gm. It expresses a transistor's amplifying ability; amplifier gain is roughly gm times the load resistance. 相互コンダクタンス

items.n: Transfer learning
items.x: A method of applying the knowledge (such as ways of extracting features) that a model acquired on one task to a different task. Starting from the weights of a model pretrained on a large amount of data, the output layer is replaced, or part or all of the model is retrained on data for the new task (fine-tuning). It tends to reach high performance with less data and computation than training from scratch, and is widely used in image recognition and language models. 転移学習

items.n: Transient enhanced diffusion (TED)
items.x: A temporary speed-up of boron and other dopant diffusion early in post-implant annealing, caused by excess silicon interstitials from the implant. It hinders the formation of shallow junctions. 過渡増速拡散(TED)

items.n: Transimpedance amplifier
items.x: An amplifier that converts an input current to a voltage. The current enters the op-amp's inverting input and a feedback resistor turns it into a voltage. It is used to read photodiode signals. トランスインピーダンスアンプ

items.n: Transistor contact
items.x: The connection between a transistor's source, drain or gate and the lowest wiring layer. It is made by filling a contact hole in the insulator with tungsten or similar metal. コンタクト

items.n: Transition frequency
items.x: The frequency at which the common-emitter current gain falls to 1, written fT. It is a key indicator of a transistor's high-frequency performance. トランジション周波数

items.n: Transmission gate
items.x: An analog switch made of an nMOS and a pMOS connected in parallel. The nMOS passes 0 well and the pMOS passes 1 well, so both values pass without voltage loss. トランスミッションゲート

items.n: Transmon
items.x: A superconducting qubit that combines a Josephson junction with a capacitor. Its frequency is generally a few GHz, and the nonlinearity of the junction makes the energy levels unequally spaced, so the two lowest levels are used as a qubit. Its design makes it insensitive to charge noise, and it is widely used in superconducting platforms. トランズモン

items.n: Tri-state buffer
items.x: A buffer that can output 0, 1 or a disconnected high-impedance state. It prevents output conflicts when several circuits share one bus. トライステートバッファ

items.n: TRIM
items.x: A command by which the operating system tells an SSD which areas belong to deleted files. Knowing which data is no longer needed makes garbage collection more efficient. TRIM

items.n: True random number generator (TRNG)
items.x: A circuit generating random numbers from unpredictable physical phenomena such as thermal noise or oscillator jitter, serving as the source for cryptographic keys. 真性乱数生成器

items.n: Trusted execution environment (TEE)
items.x: A hardware-protected execution environment isolated even from the normal OS, used for critical work such as key handling and authentication, for example Arm TrustZone. TEE(信頼できる実行環境)

items.n: Trusted Platform Module (TPM)
items.x: A security chip or function that generates and stores keys, records measurements of booted software and attests to platform state. TPM

items.n: TrustZone
items.x: Arm's processor security architecture, switching between secure and normal worlds and using bus signals to distinguish and restrict access to memory and peripherals. TrustZone

items.n: Truth table
items.x: A table listing the output for every combination of inputs. It is used to describe the behavior of logic circuits. 真理値表

items.n: TSV (through-silicon via)
items.x: An electrode that passes through the silicon substrate. It connects stacked chips vertically over a short distance. TSV(シリコン貫通電極)

items.n: Tunnel diode (Esaki diode)
items.x: A diode with very heavily doped p and n sides that shows negative resistance in forward bias due to tunneling. It was discovered by Leo Esaki in 1957. トンネルダイオード(エサキダイオード)

items.n: Turbo mode
items.x: Operation in which a CPU or similar automatically raises frequency above its rated value when power and thermal headroom allow. ターボ動作

items.n: Two-phase locking (2PL)
items.x: A concurrency control method in which each transaction has two phases, one acquiring locks and one releasing them, and acquires no new locks once it starts releasing. It guarantees serializability, but deadlocks can still occur. 2相ロック

items.n: Two's complement
items.x: The usual binary representation of negative integers. Inverting all bits and adding 1 negates a number. n bits cover −2ⁿ⁻¹ to 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, and the same adder can be used for subtraction. 2の補数

items.n: TXRF (total reflection X-ray fluorescence)
items.x: An analysis method that shines X-rays at a grazing angle so they totally reflect, then sensitively measures the fluorescent X-rays from trace metal contamination on the wafer surface. TXRF(全反射蛍光X線分析)

items.n: UART
items.x: A circuit for asynchronous serial communication without a clock wire, in which both sides agree on a baud rate and characters are framed by start and stop bits. UART

items.n: UCIe
items.x: Short for Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express: an industry-standard die-to-die interface intended to let chiplets from different companies connect to each other. UCIe

items.n: ULPA filter
items.x: A high-performance air filter that captures even finer particles than a HEPA filter. It is used in the ceilings of high-cleanliness cleanrooms. ULPAフィルタ

items.n: Ultrapure water
items.x: Water from which ions, particles and organic matter have been removed to the extreme. Used in large amounts for wafer cleaning, with purity controlled by resistivity and other measures. 超純水

items.n: Underfill
items.x: Resin filled into the gap between the chip and the substrate in flip-chip assembly. It spreads out stress from thermal expansion mismatch and protects the bump joints. アンダーフィル

items.n: Unified memory
items.x: Memory accessible from CPU and GPU through the same pointer, with data migrating automatically on access. It simplifies programs, but migration costs need attention. ユニファイドメモリ

items.n: Unintended latch
items.x: A latch created by synthesis when a description intended as combinational logic fails to assign an output under some condition, so the value must be held. 意図しないラッチ

items.n: Unsupervised learning
items.x: A machine learning approach that finds groupings or structure in data that has no correct-answer labels. It is used for clustering, which divides similar data into groups (k-means and others), dimensionality reduction, which represents data with fewer variables (principal component analysis and others), and anomaly detection, which finds data that differs greatly from the rest. No labels need to be prepared, but the quality of the result is harder to evaluate. 教師なし学習

items.n: USB Power Delivery
items.x: A specification in which source and sink negotiate voltage and current over USB, allowing up to 48 V and 240 W. USB PD

items.n: V-model
items.x: A development model that arranges the phases going down from requirements definition through design to implementation and the testing phases going back up from unit testing to acceptance testing in a V shape, and pairs the two sides, such as requirements definition with acceptance testing, design with integration and system testing, and module design with unit testing. Which design phase is paired with which test differs slightly between organizations and textbooks. V字モデル

items.n: Vacuum evaporation
items.x: Forming a film by heating a material in vacuum until it evaporates and condenses on the substrate. Electron-beam heating handles high-melting-point materials, but step coverage is poor. 真空蒸着

items.n: Value chain
items.x: A framework, proposed by Michael Porter, that divides a company's activities into primary activities (inbound logistics, operations, outbound logistics, marketing and sales, service) and support activities, to analyze which activities create value and where costs arise. バリューチェーン

items.n: Value change dump (VCD)
items.x: A standard file format recording signal value changes during simulation, viewed in waveform tools for debugging. VCD

items.n: Variable
items.x: A named container that holds a value in a program. It is declared with a type such as integer or real and changed by assignment. Assigning a new value discards the previous one. 変数

items.n: Variable cost
items.x: A cost that rises and falls in proportion to production volume or sales, such as material costs, outsourcing costs and sales commissions. The ratio of variable costs to sales is called the variable cost ratio. 変動費

items.n: VCSEL (vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser)
items.x: A semiconductor laser that emits light perpendicular to the substrate. It can be tested on the wafer and easily arranged in 2D arrays, so it is used in data links and as the light source for face recognition. VCSEL(垂直共振器面発光レーザー)

items.n: Vectorization
items.x: Transforming a loop that performs the same computation on each element so that SIMD instructions process several elements at once. It requires no data dependence between iterations. ベクトル化

items.n: Vegard's law
items.x: The empirical rule that the lattice constant of an alloy varies almost linearly with composition. It is used to find the composition that lattice-matches a given substrate. ベガード則

items.n: Velocity saturation
items.x: Under strong electric fields, carrier drift velocity stops increasing in proportion to the field and levels off at about 1×10⁷ cm/s. In short-channel MOSFETs it makes drain current smaller than the square law predicts. 速度飽和

items.n: Verilog
items.x: A hardware description language widely used for digital design and verification, describing circuits as modules with behavior expressed through assign and always. Verilog

items.n: Virtual memory
items.x: A system in which the OS and hardware map the addresses a program uses (virtual addresses) to physical memory addresses. Each program gets a large, independent address space. 仮想記憶

items.n: Virtual short
items.x: The property of an ideal op-amp with negative feedback that its two input voltages become nearly equal. Although no current flows between them, they can be treated as shorted, which makes gain calculations simple. 仮想短絡(イマジナリーショート)

items.n: VLAN
items.x: Virtual LAN. A function that creates logically separate networks (broadcast domains) on the same physical equipment, typically per switch port. Between switches, VLANs are distinguished by IEEE 802.1Q tags. VLAN

items.n: Voltage follower
items.x: A unity-gain op-amp circuit with the output tied directly to the inverting input. With high input impedance and low output impedance, it is used as a buffer. ボルテージフォロワ

items.n: Von Neumann architecture
items.x: A computer organization that keeps programs and data in the same main memory and fetches and executes instructions in sequence. ノイマン型アーキテクチャ

items.n: Wafer test (probe test)
items.x: Checking the electrical characteristics of each chip on the wafer by touching probes to its pads before dicing. It finds bad chips before assembly so they are not packaged needlessly. ウエハテスト(プローブテスト)

items.n: Wall-clock time
items.x: The actual elapsed time from start to finish, including I/O waits and time when other programs ran. 壁時計時間

items.n: Wallace tree
items.x: A multiplier structure that reduces many partial products in parallel with a tree of carry-save adders. Its depth grows only logarithmically with width, so it is used in fast multipliers; a final adder sums the last two numbers. ウォレスツリー

items.n: Warp divergence
items.x: The splitting of threads within one warp onto different paths at a conditional branch. The paths execute one after another, lowering efficiency. ワープダイバージェンス

items.n: Watchdog timer
items.x: A timer that resets the microcontroller if software does not kick it within a set time, recovering from runaway or hung programs. ウォッチドッグタイマ

items.n: Waterfall model
items.x: A software development model in which phases such as requirements definition, design, programming and testing are carried out in order from upstream, and in principle the next phase starts only after the previous phase's deliverables are finalized. Planning and progress are easy to control, but an error in the requirements found in a later phase causes a lot of rework. ウォーターフォールモデル

items.n: Waveguide
items.x: A structure that confines and guides light by surrounding a high-index core with a lower-index cladding. Silicon photonics commonly uses silicon about 0.5 µm × 0.22 µm in cross section surrounded by oxide, allowing bend radii of just a few µm. 導波路

items.n: WBS (work breakdown structure)
items.x: A tree that breaks down the deliverables of a project and the work needed for them from the top level to lower levels. The lowest elements are called work packages and are the units for estimating, scheduling, assigning people and tracking progress. WBS(作業分解構成図)

items.n: WDM (wavelength division multiplexing)
items.x: A method of carrying separate signals on different wavelengths of light and sending them together over a single fiber. CWDM uses wide 20 nm spacing, while DWDM packs many wavelengths at narrow spacings such as 100 GHz (about 0.8 nm). WDM(波長多重)

items.n: Weak scaling
items.x: Parallel performance evaluation that fixes problem size per processor while growing the total and checks whether time stays constant. 弱いスケーリング

items.n: Weak symbol
items.x: A fallback definition replaced by any ordinary (strong) definition with the same name. Embedded code uses it for default interrupt handlers and similar. 弱いシンボル

items.n: Wear leveling
items.x: A technique that spreads writes so rewrites do not concentrate on particular flash blocks, extending the memory's life. ウェアレベリング

items.n: Weibull distribution
items.x: A probability distribution widely used to analyze lifetime data. Its shape parameter can represent early-failure, random-failure and wear-out behavior. ワイブル分布

items.n: Wet etching
items.x: Etching that dissolves films by immersing them in chemicals. Selectivity is high and damage low, but it generally proceeds isotropically and does not suit fine patterning. ウェットエッチング

items.n: Wet oxidation
items.x: Thermal oxidation in an atmosphere containing water vapor. It grows faster than dry oxidation and is used to make thick oxides. ウェット酸化

items.n: White-box testing
items.x: A testing approach that creates test cases based on the internal structure of a program (statements, branches and conditions) and checks how much of it has been executed using coverage criteria such as statement coverage and branch coverage. It is used mainly in unit testing. ホワイトボックステスト

items.n: Wide-bandgap semiconductor
items.x: Semiconductors with a larger band gap than silicon, such as SiC and GaN. Their high breakdown field makes them strong for high-voltage, high-temperature operation. ワイドバンドギャップ半導体

items.n: Wire bonding
items.x: A method of connecting the chip's bond pads to a lead frame or substrate with thin wires of gold, copper or similar metals. ワイヤボンディング

items.n: WLP (wafer-level package)
items.x: A package in which redistribution wiring and external terminals are formed while the chips are still in wafer form, before dicing. The result is a small package about the size of the chip. WLP(ウエハレベルパッケージ)

items.n: WNS (worst negative slack)
items.x: In STA, the worst (smallest) slack among all paths. Together with TNS (total negative slack), the sum of negative slack over violating endpoints, it indicates how large and how widespread the timing violations are. WNS(ワーストネガティブスラック)

items.n: Word line
items.x: The wire connected to the gates of memory-cell transistors that selects the row to read or write. ワード線

items.n: Work function
items.x: The energy difference between the vacuum level and the Fermi level: the minimum energy needed to remove an electron from a material. It affects the threshold voltage of metal gates and the height of Schottky barriers. 仕事関数

items.n: Write amplification
items.x: The amount of data actually written to flash exceeding what the host wrote, because of garbage collection and similar operations. The larger it is, the shorter the SSD's life. 書き込み増幅(ライトアンプリフィケーション)

items.n: Write-allocate
items.x: A policy that, on a write miss, first brings the line into the cache and then writes it. Usually paired with write-back; writing directly to the lower level without fetching is called no-write-allocate. ライトアロケート

items.n: Write-through
items.x: A write policy that writes to the level below (such as main memory) at the same time as the cache. The lower level stays up to date, but write traffic is heavy, so it is paired with a write buffer. ライトスルー方式

items.n: Wurtzite structure
items.x: The hexagonal crystal structure of GaN, ZnO and others. It has polarization along certain crystal directions, which creates the 2DEG in GaN HEMTs. ウルツ鉱型構造

items.n: X-optimism
items.x: In HDL simulation, the tendency for conditions containing unknown X to resolve to definite values instead of propagating X, hiding bugs. X楽観主義

items.n: XPS (X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy)
items.x: An analysis method that determines the elements in the top few nanometers of a surface and their chemical bonding states from the energies of photoelectrons emitted under X-ray irradiation. XPS(X線光電子分光法)

items.n: XRD (X-ray diffraction)
items.x: An analysis method that shines X-rays on a crystal and uses the angles and intensities of the diffracted beams to determine crystal structure, lattice constant, film strain and crystal quality. XRD(X線回折)

items.n: Yield
items.x: The proportion of good products to the total produced. A key factor in semiconductor manufacturing cost. 歩留まり

items.n: Zener diode
items.x: A diode that provides a constant voltage by using the nearly fixed reverse breakdown voltage. ツェナーダイオード

items.n: Zero defects
items.x: An approach that aims for zero failures by combining design margin, process control and tests that remove outlier chips, preventing defects from being built in or shipped. Because a car uses thousands of semiconductors, automotive defect rates are managed in ppm (parts per million) with zero as the goal. ゼロディフェクト

items.n: Zero-day attack
items.x: An attack that exploits a software vulnerability in the period after it is discovered but before a fix (patch) is provided. Since patches cannot prevent it, damage is limited with multiple layers of defense. ゼロデイ攻撃

items.n: Zonal architecture
items.x: A vehicle electronics layout in which zone ECUs placed in each area of the car connect nearby sensors and actuators, while control processing is concentrated in a central high-performance computer. It allows a shorter, lighter wiring harness than the traditional one-ECU-per-function approach. ゾーンアーキテクチャ

items.n: Semiconductor physics
items.x: Practice the basics of semiconductor physics — band gap, carriers, donors and acceptors — with multiple-choice questions and explanations.

items.n: PN junctions and diodes
items.x: Learn about the depletion layer of PN junctions, forward and reverse bias, breakdown and diode applications through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Bipolar transistors
items.x: Check the basics of bipolar transistors — NPN/PNP structure, bias conditions and current gain — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: MOSFET
items.x: Learn MOSFET structure, threshold voltage, gate capacitance and why CMOS uses little power through multiple-choice questions and explanations.

items.n: Logic circuits
items.x: Check the basics of logic circuits — logic gates, De Morgan's laws and flip-flops — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Circuit and electromagnetism basics
items.x: Learn the electrical fundamentals behind electronics — Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws, Thevenin's theorem, AC impedance and resonance, RC and RL transients, and electromagnetic induction — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Analog and electronic circuits
items.x: Learn the basics of analog circuits — op-amp properties, inverting amplifier gain and the cutoff frequency of RC filters — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: A/D and D/A conversion
items.x: Learn ADC resolution, the sampling theorem, the differences between flash and successive-approximation types, and quantization error through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: DRAM
items.x: Learn about the DRAM 1T1C cell, why refresh is needed and how reading works through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: SRAM and flash memory
items.x: Check the 6-transistor SRAM cell, the differences between NAND and NOR flash, and SLC/MLC/TLC with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Emerging memories
items.x: Learn how emerging memories such as MRAM, PCM (phase-change memory), ReRAM and FeRAM store data through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: CPUs and architecture
items.x: Check CPU basics such as pipelining, cache memory and the von Neumann architecture with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Power semiconductors
items.x: Learn the basics of power semiconductors — the strengths of SiC and GaN, IGBT operation and the two-dimensional electron gas in GaN HEMTs — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Image sensors and optical devices
items.x: Check the basics of optical devices — CMOS image sensors, backside illumination (BSI) and what determines LED color — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Compound semiconductors
items.x: Learn the features of compound semiconductors such as GaAs, GaN and InP, and the difference between direct and indirect band gaps, through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Advanced transistors (FinFET and GAA)
items.x: Check the key points of advanced transistors — FinFET and GAA structures, short-channel effects, high-k/metal gates and strain engineering — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: MEMS and sensors
items.x: Learn about MEMS features, capacitive accelerometers, sacrificial-layer etching, the piezoresistive effect and Hall sensors through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Automotive Semiconductors and Functional Safety
items.x: Learn the basics of automotive semiconductors — AEC-Q100 temperature grades, ISO 26262 ASILs with SPFM, LFM and PMHF, safety mechanisms such as lockstep, CAN and automotive Ethernet, load dump and SOTIF — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Silicon photonics
items.x: Learn optical components such as silicon waveguides, optical modulators, ring resonators and Ge photodetectors, the basics of telecom wavelength bands, optical interconnects for data centers using WDM and CPO, and key points of fabrication and testing through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Quantum Computing Hardware
items.x: Learn quantum computing hardware with multiple-choice questions: qubit superposition and measurement, entanglement, calculations with quantum gates such as X, H, Z and CNOT, T1, T2 and gate fidelity, quantum error correction and the surface code, the superconducting (transmon), trapped-ion, neutral-atom, silicon spin and photonic platforms, and dilution refrigerators and control and readout electronics. Shor's algorithm and post-quantum cryptography are also covered.

items.n: Silicon wafers
items.x: Check the basics of silicon wafers — making single crystals by the CZ and FZ methods, and wafer diameters — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Epitaxial growth
items.x: Check the definition of epitaxial growth, homoepitaxy and heteroepitaxy, lattice mismatch, and MOCVD and MBE with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Oxidation and diffusion
items.x: Learn the difference between dry and wet oxidation, how much silicon thermal oxidation consumes, and how diffusion coefficients depend on temperature through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Ion implantation
items.x: Check ion implantation energy and dose, post-implant annealing and how to prevent channeling with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Deposition (CVD and PVD)
items.x: Learn the differences between CVD, PVD and ALD, sputtering and the advantages of plasma CVD through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Lithography
items.x: Check the basics of lithography — the resolution formula (k1·λ/NA), the EUV wavelength and positive resist — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Etching
items.x: Learn the basics of etching — anisotropic etching, selectivity and the differences between wet and dry etching — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: CMP and cleaning
items.x: Check planarization by CMP, dishing, and the purposes of RCA cleaning (SC-1 and SC-2) with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Interconnect processes
items.x: Learn the basics of interconnect processes — copper wiring and the damascene process, low-k materials and RC delay — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Process materials (gases and chemicals)
items.x: Learn the basics of process materials — specialty gases, ultrapure water, etching gases, sputtering targets and high-purity silicon — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Packaging and assembly
items.x: Check the basics of semiconductor packages and assembly — wire bonding, flip chip and BGA — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Testing and inspection
items.x: Learn the basics of semiconductor testing — wafer test, burn-in and scan test (DFT) — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Metrology and analysis
items.x: Check the basics of semiconductor metrology and analysis — SEM and TEM, ellipsometry, SIMS and four-point probe — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Yield and quality control
items.x: Check the basics of quality control — yield calculations, the relationship between defect density and chip area, and control charts — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Reliability
items.x: Learn the basics of semiconductor reliability — the bathtub curve, electromigration and MTBF — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: IC design flow and EDA
items.x: Check the IC design flow from specification through RTL design, logic synthesis, place and route, and static timing analysis with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Timing analysis and CDC
items.x: Check static timing analysis — setup/hold slack calculation, OCV and multicycle paths — and the design of clock domain crossings using synchronizers and asynchronous FIFOs, with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Cleanrooms and equipment
items.x: Learn the basics of fab environments and equipment — cleanroom cleanliness, yellow rooms and FOUPs — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Environment, health and safety
items.x: Check the basics of fab environment and safety — the hazards of hydrofluoric acid, SDSs, and PFC gases and global warming — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Semiconductor industry and market
items.x: Learn the structure and basic terms of the semiconductor industry — foundry, fabless, IDM and Moore's law — through multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Advanced packaging (3D and chiplets)
items.x: Check 3D integration and advanced packaging technologies such as chiplets, TSVs (through-silicon vias) and HBM with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: How to read datasheets
items.x: Learn how to read datasheets — absolute maximum ratings versus recommended operating conditions, typ versus min/max values, I/O levels and timing, thermal resistance and junction temperature, and key MOSFET and op-amp parameters — with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: Computer Arithmetic
items.x: Learn computer arithmetic with multiple-choice questions: fixed point, IEEE 754 floating point (normalization, subnormals, rounding, special values), rounding error and cancellation, bfloat16 and INT8, multipliers and carry-lookahead adders.

items.n: Probability, Statistics and Queueing
items.x: Learn probability, statistics and queueing with multiple-choice questions centered on calculations: permutations and combinations, the inclusion-exclusion principle, complementary events and conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, expected value, variance and standard deviation, the binomial, Poisson, uniform, normal and exponential distributions, the median, quartiles and box plots, the correlation coefficient and regression lines, the standard error and confidence intervals, hypothesis testing and p-values, queues (M/M/1) and Little's law, and the probabilities of bit errors and sampling inspection.

items.n: ISA & Assembly
items.x: Learn the basics of instruction sets and assembly language with multiple-choice questions: instruction formats, addressing modes, core RISC-V instructions, calling conventions and stack frames.

items.n: Compilers
items.x: Learn how compilers work with multiple-choice questions: lexing and parsing, SSA-form intermediate representations, optimizations such as constant folding and loop unrolling, and register allocation.

items.n: Linkers, Loaders & Executables
items.x: Learn about object files and the ELF format, symbol resolution and relocation, static and dynamic linking, and process memory layout with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: OS & Hardware
items.x: Learn the boundary between operating systems and hardware with multiple-choice questions: interrupts and exceptions, privilege modes and system calls, page tables and page faults, context switches and virtualization.

items.n: Memory Hierarchy
items.x: Learn about the memory hierarchy and performance with multiple-choice questions: cache organization, tag/set/offset calculations, replacement and write policies, the three types of misses, and average memory access time.

items.n: Multicore & Synchronization
items.x: Learn about the MESI protocol, memory consistency models, atomic instructions such as CAS and LL/SC, locks and memory barriers, false sharing and data races with multiple-choice questions.

items.n: GPU Programming
items.x: Learn the principles of GPU programming with multiple-choice questions: the grid/block/warp hierarchy, shared memory, coalesced memory access, warp divergence and occupancy.

items.n: AI Hardware & Software Stack
items.x: Learn about AI hardware and software with multiple-choice questions: inference versus training, quantization, arithmetic intensity and the roofline model, systolic arrays, operator fusion and tiling.

items.n: Machine Learning Basics
items.x: Learn machine learning with multiple-choice questions, including calculations: supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, classification and regression, k-means and principal component analysis, cross-validation, overfitting and regularization, confusion matrices with precision, recall and F1 score, models such as decision trees, SVMs and naive Bayes, the forward pass and activation functions of neural networks, gradient descent and backpropagation, CNNs, RNNs and the Transformer, transfer learning and generative models.

items.n: Embedded Systems & Firmware
items.x: Learn the basics of embedded systems and firmware with multiple-choice questions: register access and bit manipulation, GPIO and timers, interrupt-handler pitfalls, UART, SPI and I2C, RTOSes and watchdogs.

items.n: HDL & Verification
items.x: Learn Verilog and SystemVerilog basics with multiple-choice questions: synthesizable code, blocking versus nonblocking assignments, unintended latches, state machines, testbenches and assertions.

items.n: I/O Interfaces & Buses
items.x: Learn about I/O interfaces and buses with multiple-choice questions: PCI Express lanes and bandwidth calculations, SerDes serial links, USB, on-chip buses such as AXI, CXL, and bandwidth versus latency.

items.n: Computer Networking Basics
items.x: Learn computer networking with multiple-choice questions: the OSI reference model and TCP/IP, IP addressing and subnet calculations, ARP and routing, TCP and UDP, DNS, DHCP and TLS, transfer-time calculations, wireless LAN, firewalls and VPNs.

items.n: Wireless Communication Basics
items.x: Learn wireless communication with multiple-choice questions: wavelength and frequency, dBm and link budgets, free-space path loss and fading, ASK, PSK and QAM with symbol rates, Shannon's theorem, OFDM and OFDMA, MIMO and beamforming, the hidden node problem in wireless LANs, BLE, LPWA and NFC, LNAs, mixers, PAs and noise figure, and superheterodyne and direct-conversion receivers.

items.n: Information Security Basics
items.x: Learn information security with multiple-choice questions: the CIA triad and risk, symmetric-key and public-key cryptography, hash functions and digital signatures, authentication and multi-factor authentication, access control, malware and phishing, web attacks such as SQL injection and XSS, and backups and incident response.

items.n: Database Basics
items.x: Learn databases with multiple-choice questions: tables and keys in relational databases, SQL searches, aggregation, joins and subqueries, normalization and E-R diagrams, transactions and the ACID properties, concurrency problems and isolation levels, locks and deadlocks, recovery from failures, indexes and NoSQL.

items.n: Data Structures and Algorithms
items.x: Learn data structures and algorithms with multiple-choice questions: time complexity and Big-O notation, arrays and linked lists, stacks and queues, hash tables, binary search, how sorting algorithms work and their stability, binary search trees and heaps, graph search and shortest paths, and recursion, dynamic programming and greedy algorithms, including how they relate to caches and GPUs.

items.n: Programming Basics (Pseudocode Tracing)
items.x: Learn to trace short programs line by line with multiple-choice questions, written in the same pseudo-language as Part B of Japan's Fundamental Information Technology Engineer Examination. Topics include variables and assignment, loops and conditional branching, arrays and strings, integer division and remainders, recursion, bitwise operations, stacks and queues, linked lists, off-by-one errors, short-circuit evaluation, floating-point error, and classes and instances.

items.n: Software Development and Project Management
items.x: Learn software development and project management with multiple-choice questions: development processes such as the waterfall model, the V-model and agile development (Scrum), requirements and design (UML, module cohesion and coupling), test techniques (equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, statement and branch coverage), Git and reviews, project management with WBS, critical paths, EVM and PERT, and SLAs and problem management.

items.n: Business Strategy and Accounting Basics
items.x: Learn business strategy and accounting basics with multiple-choice questions: income statements and balance sheets, break-even analysis (variable cost ratio, contribution margin ratio, margin of safety), depreciation (straight-line and declining-balance), financial indicators such as ROE, inventory valuation, business strategy tools such as SWOT analysis, PPM, five forces analysis and the value chain, marketing concepts such as the 4Ps and the product life cycle, analysis methods such as ABC analysis, decision trees and linear programming, investment appraisal by NPV, and the basics of intellectual property and contracts.

items.n: IT Service Management and Systems Audit
items.x: Learn IT service management and systems audit with multiple-choice questions, including calculations: the approach of IT service management, SLAs and service level management, incident and problem management (workarounds and known errors), change and release management, configuration management (CMDB), the service desk and escalation, capacity management and availability calculations (MTBF and MTTR), business continuity plans (BCP), facilities such as UPS units and fire suppression, how a systems audit proceeds, audit trails and audit techniques, internal control and IT governance.

items.n: System Architecture and Reliability
items.x: Learn system architecture and reliability with multiple-choice questions: system configurations such as client-server and three-tier systems, dual and duplex systems and hot standby, RAID capacity and tolerated failures, full, differential and incremental backups with RPO and RTO, fail-safe, fail-soft and fool-proof design, cloud and virtualization, SAN and NAS, PUE, and capacity planning.

items.n: Performance Analysis
items.x: Learn performance analysis with multiple-choice questions: execution time = instruction count × CPI × cycle time, Amdahl's law calculations, benchmarking pitfalls, performance counters and identifying bottlenecks.

items.n: Hardware Security
items.x: Learn hardware security with multiple-choice questions focused on principles and countermeasures: speculative-execution side channels (Spectre and Meltdown), power analysis and timing attacks, secure boot, TEEs, PUFs and hardware Trojans.

items.n: Power Management
items.x: Learn software-controlled power management with multiple-choice questions: dynamic and static power, DVFS and OS frequency control, power gating versus clock gating, sleep states and thermal throttling.
